**Location:** design §4.5a *Org top bar: build chip*, §6 *Promote* (the readings); `src/sessionorc/promote.py` (`read_main` ~L107 reads `main` and `moved`; `live` and `ahead` are set in the tick's pass ~L520–528, where the two new readings go: `live_at` — `git log -1 --format=%cI <live>` — and `pending` — `git log --format=%h%x09%s <live>..<main>`, ten plus a count; both empty when live or main is unknown), `src/sessionorc/build.py` (`chip` ~L83: always a dict, `{"text", "title", "cls"}` with `cls` `live` / `behind` / `inflight` / `held` / `unknown`; `line` gains the pending list; the time drawn local to the page — the chip carries the ISO time in `data-at` and `app.js` prints it in the browser's zone, as other times are), `src/agentorc/ui/app.py` ~L1170 (`build_chip` on every page's context, with the page's own `build.info()` and the host's linked nodes' builds), `src/agentorc/ui/templates/base.html` ~L32 (the chip unconditional, `data-at`), `src/agentorc/ui/static/app.js` (the local-time print, the Inbox poll redraw), `tests/test_build.py`, `tests/test_promote.py`, `tests/test_ui_promote.py`, mockups `Main.dc.html`/`MainDark.dc.html` (`docs/mockups/gen.py`: the chip in the bar)

**Why:** TD-539: Paul could not tell from the page whether a fix he was asked to look at was live; the hashes are in a terminal, and the chip today is nothing in the common case.

**Fix:**

Text *live <MM-DD HH:MM>* (the year in front when not this year), then *· main +n* / *· promoting…* / *· held* / *· main unknown* as the reading says; *build unknown* without a record. `title`: `line`'s sentence, a blank line, *not live yet:* and the pending lines, *… and n more*; *this page: <sha7> <time>* when the UI's `build.info()` commit differs; *<node>: <sha7>, stale* per linked node marked so.

4. Tests: the readings' two new fields on a scratch repo (live behind main by three commits: three pending; live at main: empty); `chip` for each `cls`; the page draws the chip when live is main's head; the hover carries the pending subjects; `ao promote status` unchanged.
5. UI check on a scratch home (§4.9b): the bar reads *live <today's time>*; merge one commit to the scratch repo's main — *main +1* and its subject on hover within the readings' cadence; promote — *promoting…*, then the new time. Shots `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-10-td-542-*.png` in the PR.

**Done when** every page's top bar names the live build by its commit's local date and time, says *main +n* when merges are not yet live with their subjects on hover, says *promoting…* and *held* when the readings do, shows the page's own build when it differs, and the tests pin it.

**Related:** TD-539 (the design), TD-062 (the promoted install), TD-120 / TD-132 (Promote; slice 5 built the first chip), TD-226 (rollback and its hold), TD-233 (the usage chip beside it).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-10 (PR #1500) — `promote.read_since` puts `live_at` and `pending` (ten, `pending_more` the rest) on each repo's reading in the full pass; `build.chip` is always drawn, *live <MM-DD HH:MM>* then *· promoting…* / *· held* / *· main unknown* / *· main +n*, the hover the live sha and subject, *not live yet:* with the pending list, the page's own build where it differs and each stale node; `app.chip_build` puts it on every page and on the Inbox poll, `app.js` prints the time in the browser's zone. `tests/test_promote.py`, `test_build.py` and `test_ui_promote.py` pin it; the UI check on a scratch home held *live*, *main +1* with its subject, *promoting…* and the promoted build's new time (PR body).

## TD-497: Build the watch (TD-489): `agentorc-watch` and its system timer beside the tmux unit, the manager's restart, the three Telegram lines under `notify.telegram`, the doctor's agent line

## TD-489: A session killed `systemd --user` by killing a stray process's parent, and nothing noticed the host agent was down for 4h20m

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-09 (ao-paul, the cause of the 2026-10-09 outage, found from designer-ao-1's transcript)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Blocked by:** TD-496, TD-497
**Location:** `src/agentorc/briefs/` (the role briefs) and `docs/briefs/` (held paths); design §6 (supervision, alarms), §4.4a (the home); designer-ao-1's transcript `2acd2a63-…` at 18:30:53Z

**Why:** to stop its own `sleep 90` polling loops, designer-ao-1 ran `for p in $(ps … grep '[s]leep 90' …); do pp=$(ps -o ppid= -p $p); kill $pp $p; done`. One of those `sleep`s had been orphaned, so its parent was `/usr/lib/systemd/systemd --user`. The loop killed it, which is TD-488's outage. Two gaps: (1) nothing tells a session never to signal a process it did not start, and "kill the parent" is how a cleanup reaches pid 1 or the user manager; (2) no alarm fired. The host agent, the UI and every session were gone for 4h20m, and the person found out only by logging in.

**Fix:** design first, two parts. (1) A rule in every role brief and in `ao --skill`: signal only a pid this session started itself and still holds (a `$!`, a background task id), never a parent, and never by matching a name across the machine. Look at whether a guard fits too, such as a `PreToolUse` hook that refuses a `kill` of pid 1, the user manager, the tmux server or the host agent; a guard is wiring, so it goes in the adapter. (2) An alarm that does not need the host agent alive: something outside `user@1000` that sees the agent socket silent past a bound and reaches the person through the board's push or Telegram (§4.10; TD-092, built as TD-319). **Done when** the briefs and the skill carry the rule, the guard is built or written down as not built, and stopping the host agent on a scratch home raises the alarm within the bound.

**Related:** TD-488, TD-092 and TD-319 (Telegram), TD-111 (`ao doctor`).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-10 — both builds landed: TD-496 (the process rule and the kill guard) and TD-497 (the watch, live-checked 2026-10-10).

## TD-550: The tick keeps a record's `files` when a read fails and saves when only the list moved: neither is tested, and the failing form empties the list

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-11 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1497, TD-538)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_refresh_git`: `files = {... if isinstance(r, list)}` and `changed = changed or files[s.id] != live.files`); `tests/test_recent_files.py::test_the_tick_reads_the_list_when_the_status_moves_and_a_shell_session_shows_it`

**Why:** the comment #1497 wrote says *"a read that failed keeps the list it had, and is taken again next time"*, and `changed_files`'s docstring says *"None when a read fails, so the record keeps what it had"*. The unit test holds the None at `changed_files`; the tick test never makes a read fail. Probes on `tests/test_recent_files.py` and `tests/test_ui_focus_recent_files.py`: replace `if isinstance(r, list)}` with `if not isinstance(r, BaseException)}` — a failing read would then set `live.files = None`, and it is marked read, so it is not taken again — passes; replace `changed = changed or files[s.id] != live.files` with `pass` (the list moving with no change in `git`, as a commit after a fetch does) — passes, and the test reads through `get`, never the store.

**Fix:** in the tick test, monkeypatch `_recent_files` to return None once: expect the list unchanged and `_files_read` not advanced, then a next tick that reads it; and a read whose list differs while `git` is equal expects `store.save` (read the record back from the store, not `get`).

**Related:** TD-538 (the build).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-11 (PR #1507) — `test_the_tick_reads_the_list_when_the_status_moves_and_a_shell_session_shows_it` now fails a read once (the list kept, `_files_read` not advanced, the next tick reads it) and reads a moved list with `git` unchanged back from the store. Probes: both mutations named in **Why** fail it.

## TD-547: The build chip's browser half (`drawBuildChip`, `buildStamp`, the Inbox poll's redraw) has no test: delete it and the suite stays green

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-11 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1500, TD-539)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/agentorc/ui/static/app.js` (`buildStamp`, `drawBuildChip`, the `if (got.build_chip) drawBuildChip(...)` line in the Inbox poll); `tests/test_ui_promote.py::test_every_page_and_the_inbox_poll_draw_the_build_chip`

**Why:** the comment #1500 wrote says the chip is *"Drawn at load and again from each Inbox poll's `build_chip`, so a merge shows without a reload"* and reprints *live <MM-DD HH:MM>* "in the browser's zone — the year in front only when it is not this one". Every test of it is server-side: `test_ui_promote.py` greps the HTML for `data-at`/`data-rest` and the poll's JSON for `build_chip`, and `grep -rn 'drawBuildChip\|buildStamp' tests/` finds nothing. Probes, each run over all of `tests/` in a scratch worktree: delete `drawBuildChip(null);` (the load draw), delete `if (got.build_chip) drawBuildChip(got.build_chip);` (the poll redraw), and replace the year rule with `return false ? md` — each `pytest -x` run passes. So the page can show the server's sentence in the server's zone, never refresh after a merge, or print the wrong year, and nothing fails.

**Fix:** a node probe in the style of `tests/test_recent_links.py::PROBE`: load `app.js`, call `drawBuildChip({at, rest, ...})` on a stub element and expect `live <MM-DD HH:MM><rest>` (with TZ set), the year in front for an `at` of another year, `text` kept when there is no `at`, and a call with `null` re-stamping from `dataset`. A second line: the poll function handed `{build_chip: {...}}` reaches `drawBuildChip`.

**Related:** TD-539 (the build), TD-546 (the probe pattern).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-11 (PR #1508) — `tests/test_ui_build_chip.py` runs `app.js` in node against a stub `#buildchip` under `TZ=America/New_York`: the load draw reprints `data-at`/`data-rest` in the browser's zone, an Inbox poll handed `build_chip` redraws it (the year in front only for another year), a chip with no `at` keeps its text, and a poll with no chip changes nothing. Deleting the load draw, the poll's redraw, the year rule or the `at` branch each fails it.

## TD-555: `service._remove_legacy_system_units` — the root step that stops `agentorc-tmux` and ends every session in it unless the server is empty — has no test: gut the function and `tests/test_service.py` stays green

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-11 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1505)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/service.py` (`_remove_legacy_system_units`, `LEGACY_SYSTEM_UNITS`, its call in `install_system`); `tests/test_service.py::test_install_system_writes_the_unit_made_again_as_root_and_starts_it`

**Why:** #1505's description says *"`install --system` stops and removes the old system units first, refused while their server holds a session"*, and the function's docstring gives the reason: *"stopping `agentorc-tmux` ends every session in it"*. It runs as root, once per machine, and `grep -rn "_remove_legacy\|LEGACY_SYSTEM" tests/` finds nothing; `test_install_system_*` write into a `tmp_path` `SYSTEM_DIR` that never holds an old unit, so the branch is not taken. Probes, over `tests/test_service.py`, the ledger, promote, settings and org tests (314 tests): replace the `present = [...]` line with `present = []` — `314 passed`; replace `if live is None or live:` with `if False:` — `314 passed`. So neither the refusal that protects a server holding sessions, nor the stop/unlink/`daemon-reload` that removes the old units, nor the *unreadable* case (`_server_sessions` returning None) is held; a change that stops the old server with sessions in it, or leaves the old unit to restart beside the new one, is green.

**Fix:** in `test_service.py`, with `SYSTEM_DIR` a `tmp_path` holding `agentorc-tmux.service`, `agentorc-watch.timer` and `agentorc-watch.service`, `subprocess.run` recorded and `_server_sessions` monkeypatched: (a) it answers `["ao-x"]` — `install_system` raises `RuntimeError` naming the old units and the session, the files are still there and no `systemctl` ran; (b) it answers `None` — the same refusal, saying *unreadable*; (c) it answers `[]` — `disable --now` names exactly the present units, the files are gone, `daemon-reload` follows, and a unit that is absent is not named.

**Done when:** each of the two probes in **Why** fails `tests/test_service.py`.

**Related:** TD-060 (#1505), TD-556.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-11 (PR #1521) — `test_install_system_removes_the_old_units_only_when_their_server_holds_no_session` holds the refusal for a server with a session and for one that cannot be read (files kept, no `systemctl`), and with an empty server the `disable --now` of exactly the present units, their removal and the `daemon-reload`. Both probes in **Why** fail it, as do `if live:` and dropping the `unlink`.

## TD-559: A seat or member held off by a session outside the team is a quiet slot line: the person sees no error, and the team's anchor work waits unseen

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, Paul's ask)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.9b *The anchor seat*, §6 rule 3 (the fill's occupancy gate), §4.5a rows *Inbox row: seat held*, *team header: seat held*, *on call: the anchor seat's words*; `seat_held` on the record; the Inbox's *Needs you* sources

**Why:** on 2026-10-11 a plain `claude` started at 14:29 in a VS Code terminal in `/home/kmaster/shiftlead`, outside ShiftLead. That made it the one agent in the main checkout (§9 invariant 2), so ao-grind's anchor seat never filled. Its record read `seat_held: {by: shiftlead-90, why: "held by shiftlead-90 (claude-code, outside shiftlead, idle)"}`. Its lane held TD-060 and six live checks, and three design entries (TD-290, TD-410, TD-457) were blocked on those checks. All the person saw was the seat's slot, *on call — the checkout is yours · …*, on a folded team. When Paul closed that session on 2026-10-12, the anchor started by itself (rule 3's fill, as designed). Paul: *show an error when a member's worktree (e.g. the anchor) is occupied by a non-team-member.*

**Fix:** design an error-weight signal for a seat or member whose fill (or start) is held off by a session that is not one of the team's: it names the holder and how long it has held the seat, and offers what to do. A Needs-you Inbox row, or a warning on the team header that shows while the team is folded, or both. Also decide whether it stays quiet while the holder is the person's own interactive session and the lane is empty, and goes up only once the lane holds work. **Done when** a held seat whose lane holds work is visible as an error without unfolding the team, naming the holding session.

**Related:** TD-558, TD-381, TD-457.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the designer; archived with its build TD-564, PR #1534) — a held anchor seat is a counted *Needs you* row past `SEAT_HELD_GRACE` and a mark on its team's header, design §4.5a *Inbox row: seat held* and *team header: seat held*, from `seat_held: {by, why, since}` (§6 rule 3).

## TD-564: Build TD-559: `seat_held.since`, the *seat held* Inbox row under Needs you past `SEAT_HELD_GRACE`, and the team header's mark

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-559's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5a *Inbox row: seat held*, *team header: seat held*; §4.5 screen 6 (*Needs you*); §6 rule 3 (`seat_held: {by, why, since}`); §4.9b *The anchor seat*; `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`seat_held` ~L1159), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_checkout_held` ~L2423, `_checkout_why` ~L2445, `_fill` ~L2495: where `seat_held` is written, and the lane reading ~L2270 that clears it), `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`create` with `held`: the Start's record), `src/sessionorc/agent_common.py` (`SEAT_HELD_GRACE`), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (`restart_mark` ~L102 as the model, `state_rows` ~L237, `inbox_sections`' dismiss ~L1739), `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`seat_held_words` ~L813), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/group_head.html` (the header: the on-call count's neighbour folded, the ✉ count's otherwise), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the header's delta), `docs/mockups/gen.py` (the row, drawn by TD-559), `tests/test_inbox_*.py`, `tests/test_ui_teams.py`, the anchor seat's tests (`seat_held`)

**Why:** TD-559: on 2026-10-11 a plain `claude` outside ShiftLead held ao-grind's anchor seat off TD-060 and six live checks for a day, and all the person saw was the slot's *on call — the checkout is yours · …* on a folded team.

**Fix:**
1. `seat_held` carries `since`: `_checkout_why` returns `{by, why}` as today and the writer (`_fill`, and the lane reading that keeps or clears it) sets `since` to `now` when `by` differs from the record's current `seat_held.by`, else keeps the record's; `create` with `held` writes `since` as the record's `created`. `why` may change under one `since` (the holder's state).
2. `SEAT_HELD_GRACE = 15 * 60` in `agent_common`; a `seat_held_mark(v, now)` in `inbox.py` beside `restart_mark`: None unless the view carries `seat_held` with `since` older than the grace; else `(since, text)` with the text of §4.5a — the age from `since`, the holder's words (`why` as the tick wrote it), the count and three ids of `seat_due.ids`, and the closing clause by `by` (`checkout`: *commit and push, or check out main, and the seat fills*; a session: *close it, or finish there, and the seat fills on the next tick*).
3. `state_rows` raises `base(v, "seat_held", text)` with `at: since`, `mark: "seat_held"`, `holder: by` where `by` is a record of this home (the view's `focus` target) else none; the template draws Open (to the holder's Focus, else the seat's), Dismiss (`dismissed:<since>` under the `sid|seat_held` key, the restart row's mechanism) and Snooze ▾.
4. The team header: the records' delta carries each seat's `seat_held` already; the header draws *· anchor held <age>* after the on-call count when a seat of the team is held past the grace, class the warning's amber, the row's text as its title; nothing otherwise.
5. Tests: `since` set on first read, kept across `why` changes, reset on a new `by`, written by a held Start; no row under the grace, a row past it, counted under *Needs you*; the row names a holder outside shiftlead by `occupants`' words and offers no holder Focus; Dismiss hides this `since` and a new holder's row returns; the row leaves when `seat_held` clears; the header mark drawn folded and gone when clear; the mockup regenerates.

**Done when** a held anchor seat whose lane holds work is a counted *Needs you* row past fifteen minutes, naming the holding session and the work, with Open / Dismiss / Snooze, and a mark on the folded team's header, both gone when the seat fills or nothing is due; and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-559 (the design), TD-558 / TD-563 (the Start line's held note), TD-381 (the anchor seat), TD-386 (`seat_held`), TD-103 (the restart row, the model).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1534) — `seat_held.since` is written by the fill's tick (kept across `why`, reset by a new `by`) and by a held Start (`created`); past `SEAT_HELD_GRACE` the Inbox's *Needs you* carries the counted *seat held* row (Open / Dismiss / Snooze) and the team header the amber *anchor held <age>* mark, folded or not; both checked on a scratch home (the PR's UI check) and held by tests in `test_anchor_tick.py`, `test_ui_inbox.py`, `test_ui.py`.

## TD-560: The ledger's undated *for you* entries get their own Inbox section, not due, drawn as every Inbox row is — its options and a Reply

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, Paul's ask)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 6 *Later*, *The ledger's entries that wait on you*; §4.5a rows *Inbox: Later section*, *Inbox row: ledger entry*, *Not due yet*; `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (`ledger_for_you`), `ledger_for_you.html`

**Why:** TD-367 made the ledger's *for you* entries (`Owner: paul`, `decision (paul)`) a fold of one-line links. It is counted nowhere and has no control, because an entry has no date and no asker, and the Inbox's counts mean *due now*. That design rejected counted rows and a section of their own. Paul, 2026-10-12: keep them out of *due*, but give them **a separate space in the Inbox** that is also the place for future items that are not pressing, and draw them with **the same interface as every Inbox item**: the options listed, a recommended answer, and a Reply.

**Fix:** design a not-due Inbox section, *Later* or similar, that holds the undated *for you* entries and any other non-pressing item, kept out of the due counts. Each row is drawn as a mail row is: its first paragraph, its options with the recommended one marked, and **Reply**. Decide where the options come from: an entry has none today, so either the ledger entry carries `**Options:**` and a default, or the Reply goes to the repo's techlead or anchor as an `ask` reply that the entry's owner writes back to the ledger. Decide also where a reply lands (the entry's Status, a board line, mail to the anchor) and how a dated item enters or leaves the section. This reverses part of TD-367's rejection; the history gets a dated line. **Done when** the design draws the section, its rows' controls, and the reply's path into the ledger, and a build entry is open.

**Related:** TD-367, TD-368, TD-561.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the designer; archived with its build TD-565, PRs #1537 and #1542) — the Inbox draws *Later* with the board's coming-up rows and the ledger's *for you* entries as full rows, an answer written as a decided board line, design §4.5 screen 6 *Later* and *The ledger's entries that wait on you*, §4.5a **Inbox: Later section** and **Inbox row: ledger entry**.

## TD-565: Build TD-560: the Inbox's *Later* section — the board's coming-up rows moved in, the ledger's *for you* entries as full rows with `Answers:`, Go with it, Reply and Open, an answer written as a decided board line

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-560's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 6 *Later*, *The ledger's entries that wait on you*, *The board's horizon* (*Coming up*); §4.5a rows *Inbox: Later section*, *Inbox row: ledger entry*, *Not due yet*, *the rail*; §4.4 *Repo facts*; `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (the entry parse ~L350–380: `added`, `answers`, `detail` on a *for you* entry), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (`INBOX_SECTIONS` ~L49, `RAIL_UNDER` ~L1829: `coming`/`unshown` under `later`; `ledger_for_you` ~L1987 → rows in a mail row's shape; `row_find` ~L1853), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/inbox.html` (a `sec-later` section between `sec-answered` and `sec-fyi`; `#boardhorizon` and `#ledgerforyou` move into it), `ledger_for_you.html` (the rows as `inbox_row.html` draws a board `decide` row: kind, name, badge, age, `body`, the answers' dashed group, the controls), `inbox_rail.html` / `app.js` (the *Later* line in *Urgency*, *ledger entries* in *Kinds*, the poll putting the section back), `src/sessionorc/agent_inbox.py` (the answer's RPC beside `_answer_orphan` ~L594: the second add's road, `board_edit.py`'s add with `Decided:`), `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py` (the section's blurb), `docs/mockups/gen.py` (drawn by TD-560), `tests/test_ui_inbox*.py`, `tests/test_ledger.py` (the parse), the board write-back tests

**Why:** TD-560: Paul, 2026-10-12 — the *for you* entries are a fold of links counted nowhere and with no control; he wants them out of *due* but in a space of their own in the Inbox, drawn as every Inbox item is, with the options, a recommended answer and a Reply.

**Fix:**
1. The reading: `ledger.py` carries, on a *for you* entry, `added` (the `Added:` date), `answers` (the `**Answers:**` line parsed as the board reader parses `Answers:`, cadence §3.5: a list and the `(default)` index) and `detail` (the **Why** and **Fix** paragraphs, at most `MAX_DETAIL_LINES` as the board's block); nothing on other entries, so the repo facts' size barely moves.
2. The section: `later` in `INBOX_SECTIONS` after `answered`; the board horizon's box and the ledger box move under it in `inbox.html`; the rail's *Urgency* lists *Later* with its count (the horizon's rows, the fold's once opened, and the ledger rows), `RAIL_UNDER` maps `coming` and `unshown` to `later`; the *Kinds* group gains *ledger entries*; the top bar, the Org rollup and *Needs you*'s counts unchanged. The section's info blurb says what it holds.
3. The row: `ledger_for_you` yields rows with `row: "ledger"`, `kind`, `name` (the repo), `team`, `at` (`added`), `pri`, `held`, `title`, `detail`, `answers`, `default`, `url`; the template draws them with `inbox_row.html`'s macros (the body's first paragraph is the title, *details* the detail, open when answers exist), the answers' dashed group, **Go with it** when a default exists, **Reply** (the Reply dialog, `about` the id), **Open**.
4. The answer: a `ledger_decide` RPC (home-owned; `modes.py`) taking the repo, the id and the words (an answer's text, or the Reply's) writes one head line at the top of the repo's open board items by the second add's road — `- [ ] decide <today> (person) — <title>. Context: <id>. Due: <today>. Answers: <the entry's, where any>. Decided: <words> (<today>).` — committed as `shiftlead: board decide <id> (person)`; refused with the add's own refusals (a dirty checkout, no board). The next reading lists the decided line; `ledger_for_you` leaves out an entry an open decided line's `Context:` names.
5. Tests: the parse (added, answers with a default, detail clipped; nothing on a non-*for you* entry); the section drawn only with rows, uncounted in the top bar and the rollup, listed in the rail with its count; the horizon's rows under *Later* and `RAIL_UNDER`; the row's shape and controls, the answers group with the default marked, Reply on every row; the RPC's line and commit message, the entry gone from the rows on the next reading; the mockup regenerates.

**Done when** the Inbox draws *Later* with the board's coming-up rows and the ledger's *for you* entries as full rows — answers, Go with it, Reply, Open — an answer lands as a decided board line that the next reading lists as a *Waiting on them* row, no number meaning *due now* moves, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-560 (the design), TD-367 / TD-368 (the fold it replaces), TD-220 / TD-281 (the horizon), TD-213 (the second add), TD-380 (a decided line is a work order), TD-561 (the subject line, whose ledger row's subject is the title).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PRs #1537 and #1542) — slice 1 (#1537): `ledger.py` reads `added`, `answers`/`default` and `detail` on a *for you* entry; the Inbox draws *Later* after *Answered for you* with the horizon's box and the ledger's rows in a mail row's shape, the rail's *Later* and *ledger entries*. Slice 2 (#1542): the row's answers (by index, the default marked), **Go with it** and **Reply** call `ledger_decide` (home-owned, the person's own), which writes `- [ ] decide <today> (person) — <title> Context: TD-n. Due: <today>. Answers: …. Decided: <words> (<today>).` at the top of the repo's open board items by the second add's road (`board.decided_line`, `board.add_decided`), committed as `shiftlead: board decide TD-n (person)`, and re-reads the repo's work orders; `ledger_for_you` leaves out an entry an open decided line's `refs` name; the poll's `#ledgerforyou` swap keeps a ringed row's ring and a refused write's words. Held by `tests/test_board.py` (`decided_line`, the third add, `ledger_decide`'s refusals and writes), `tests/test_ui_inbox_ledger.py` and `tests/test_ledger_derived.py`.

## TD-572: Typing into a Focus terminal lags — every page's events stream re-reads the whole fleet's groups on every delta

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** anchor
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5 *Live state*, §4.5a *card: compact*, *team card: wound down* note; `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`events`), `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (`HEADS_EVERY`, `SHAPE_KEYS`), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`connectEvents`, the Focus and Inbox pages), `tests/test_ui_events_light.py`

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12: *there is lag per keystroke in this (and the other focus) terminals … no lag when typing into the composer text box*. Measured on the live UI with three Focus tabs open: `shiftlead-ui` at a full core (888 s of CPU in 20 min, all on the event loop's thread), a static file's latency p50 3 ms, p90 770 ms, p99 2.4 s, max 3.2 s, and each `/events` stream ~0.9 MB/s — 72 messages in 15 s, ~190 KB each, because every session delta (a working pane's tail moves every second or two) carried `heads`: every team header and the rollup, read over the whole fleet, once per open page. A Focus tab held the same full stream as the Org page and used one record of it. The pty bridge's keystrokes share that loop, so each waited behind the renders; the composer is a plain text box and does not.

**Fix:** the groups ride on a delta only when it changes one of `SHAPE_KEYS` (state, team, controllers, name, seat, unattended), names a record the stream has not seen, or is the stream's first; any other delta marks them for one `groups` event at most every `HEADS_EVERY` (1 s), and a reading equal to the last one sent is not sent. `/events?light=1` (the Inbox) and `?light=1&focus=<id>` (Focus) send no card markup and no groups: the focus record's delta whole, another's as `{event, id, state}` only when a field of `SHAPE_KEYS` or `LIGHT_KEYS` (lane, report, claim, unseen, open work, declaration) moved, which is all those pages re-read on. One reading of the groups is read and sent at a time (`sending`), `dirty` cleared before the read; a reshaping delta always carries its groups; a flush whose read fails retries.

**Done when** a Focus tab's stream carries no groups and only its own session in full, the Org's carries the groups only on a shape change or once a second, and the tests in `tests/test_ui_events_light.py` pass.

**Related:** TD-176 (the groups on every delta), TD-058 (the `/events` handler's end).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1544) — the groups ride on a delta only on a `SHAPE_KEYS` change, a new record or the stream's first, else one `groups` event per `HEADS_EVERY`, never re-sent unchanged; the Focus and Inbox pages take `/events?light=1` (Focus with `focus=<id>`): no markup, no groups, another record only when it moves.

## TD-561: Every Inbox entry carries a subject line: a short headline, apart from the first paragraph, so the Inbox can be browsed by it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, Paul's ask)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.10 *A subject on every entry* (after *How a message to a person is written*), §4.5a row *subject*, §4.5 screen 6 *The message page*, §4.7 `ao msg`; the mail envelope

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12: *require all inbox items to include a subject line — that makes browsing them easier.* Today a row draws its first paragraph (TD-127: one to three sentences, *no summary field*). That rule rejected a second text on purpose, so a row has no short headline to scan by. Board lines mostly open with a bolded lead by habit, but the `Format:` line does not require one.

**Fix:** design a required `subject` on every entry filed to the person: mail (`ao msg --subject`, refused or warned when missing, with a length bound), board lines (a required lead in the `Format:` line, a dev-cadence change), the home's own entries (lapse notes, work rows), and TD-560's ledger rows (the entry's title). The Inbox row and the message page draw the subject first and the first paragraph under it, and the find box matches it. The briefs and presets say the rule. This reverses TD-127's *no summary field*; the history gets a dated line. **Done when** the design names the field, where each kind of entry gets it, how a missing one is treated, and how the row draws it, and a build entry is open.

**Related:** TD-127, TD-560.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the designer; archived with its build TD-566, PRs #1536 and #1543) — every entry the person reads carries a `subject`, design §4.10 *A subject on every entry*, §4.5a *subject*, §4.5 screen 6 *The message page*, §4.7 `ao msg --subject`.

## TD-566: Build TD-561: `subject` on every entry the person reads — `ao msg --subject`, derived and warned when missing, the home's rows' by kind — drawn first on the row, the message page and `ao inbox`, matched by the find

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-561's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.10 *A subject on every entry*, §4.7 `ao msg`, §4.5a *subject* row, §4.5 screen 6 *The message page*; `src/sessionorc/agent_mail.py` (`rpc_msg` ~L75: the `subject` parameter, the derivation and its warning line, a reply's inherited from its question ~L581, the `system` note ~L931), `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`MailEntry` ~L296: the `subject` field), `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`SUBJECT_CHARS`, `subject_of(text)`, beside the other caps), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao msg --subject` ~L3665; the warning beside `FIRST_PARA_WORDS` ~L2626; `cmd_inbox` ~L2902: the head line), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (`state_rows` ~L237 and the other row builders: `subject` by kind; `row_find` ~L1853), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/inbox_row.html` (the `body` macro ~L44: the subject line first), `inbox_entry.html` (the heading, the `title` block), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/board_horizon.html` / the board row (the head line's text as subject), `ledger_for_you.html` (TD-565's rows: the title), `src/shiftlead/briefs/*.md` (the message-shape line), `docs/briefs/techlead-context.md` and the repo's brief parts under `docs/briefs/` (the same line; a held path, this entry's), `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py` (the help's Inbox words), `docs/mockups/gen.py` (drawn by TD-561), `tests/test_mail.py`, `tests/test_cli.py` (`shape_warning`'s tests), `tests/test_ui_inbox*.py`

**Why:** TD-561: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *require all inbox items to include a subject line — that makes browsing them easier*; a row draws its first paragraph and has no headline to scan by.

**Fix:**
1. The envelope: `MailEntry.subject` (a string, at most `SUBJECT_CHARS` 80); `rpc_msg` takes `subject`; on a message to the person (or a `--source` reply) with none, `subject_of(text)` derives it — the text to the first `.`, `?` or `!` followed by a space or the end, else the first 80 characters, clipped at a word with an ellipsis — and the reply carries `warnings: ["no --subject: \"…\" stands as one"]`, printed by the CLI as the first-paragraph warning is; one past 80 is clipped and said. A `reply`, an outcome note and an *answered for you* entry copy their question's subject; a `system` note derives its own. A message to a session takes `--subject` too and derives nothing (a session reads the text).
2. The CLI: `ao msg --subject <line>`; `ao inbox` prints the subject on the entry's head line after the kind, before the status.
3. The rows: every row builder in `inbox.py` sets `subject` — mail from the envelope; a state row *<kind> · <what>* (*permission · Bash*, *question · grinder-ao-1*, *limited · ao-grind-anchor*, *stalled? · <name>*, *exited with unpushed work · <name>*); the restart row *restarts exhausted · <name>* / *restart held · <name>* / *restart wanted · <name>*; the seat-held row (TD-564) *anchor seat held · <team>*; the work row *lanes gained n entries · <team>*; the identity alarm *identity alarm · <name>*; the cadence and held rows *cadence check failed · #n* / *merged without its read · #n*; the promote row *promote · <repo>*; a board row the head line's text before `Context:`; a ledger row (TD-565) the title; a trail row its *how*. `row_find` includes it.
4. Drawn: `inbox_row.html`'s `body` opens with `<div class="subj">` — bold, `white-space: nowrap`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, the whole in `title` —, the first paragraph under it; `inbox_entry.html` heads with the subject and sets the tab title *<subject> · Inbox · ShiftLead*; the thread's rows show theirs.
5. The presets: the message-shape line in `src/shiftlead/briefs/*.md` and the repo's parts under `docs/briefs/` gains *and a `--subject`: the entry's headline in a few words, apart from the first paragraph*; the help's Inbox paragraph names the subject.
6. Tests: the derivation (first sentence; no sentence end; clipping at 80 at a word; the warning line present and absent); a reply inherits; a system note derives; each home row's subject by kind; the row draws it first and the find matches it; the message page's heading and title; `ao inbox`'s head line; the mockup regenerates.

**Done when** every row of the Inbox, the message page and `ao inbox` leads with a subject — mail's given or derived with a warning, the home's rows' by kind, a board row's its head line, a ledger row's its title — the find box matches it, the presets and briefs say `--subject`, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-561 (the design), TD-127 (the first-paragraph rule), TD-560 / TD-565 (the ledger row's subject), TD-564 (the seat-held row's).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PRs #1536, #1543) — slice 1 (#1536): `MailEntry.subject`, `mail.subject_of` / `clip_subject`, `rpc_msg`'s `subject`, its inheritance by a reply, an outcome and an *answered for you* entry, the *no --subject* warning, `ao msg --subject` and `ao inbox`'s head line. Slice 2 (#1543): `kind_subject` / `row_subject` in `inbox.py` — every state, restart, seat-held (*anchor seat held · <team>*), alarm, cadence, held, promote, team-start and board row's subject by kind, a trail row's *how*, a ledger row's title (drawn already as its first paragraph, so no line above it), mail's envelope or, for an entry older than the field, its first sentence; the `subj` line first on every row, the message page's heading and tab title; `row_find` adds it; the message-shape line in the five presets, and in the repo's own brief parts the one that carries the shape rule, `docs/briefs/techlead-context.md` (TD-573, a held path, so a PR of its own). Checked on a scratch home (#1543's UI check) and held by `test_mail.py`, `test_cli.py`, `test_ui_inbox.py`. Not built: *the help's Inbox paragraph* — §4.5a *The help text* is one paragraph per control and holds none for the Inbox, and `subject` is display only; and a warning for a `--subject` dropped on a reply, which the techlead's read of #1536 says nothing owes (the Reply dialog types none).

## TD-575: #1544's events-stream changes — the `gone` path, the `repos`/`doing` mark, the dedupe, and the flush's retry — are held by no test

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1544)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`events`: `fresh_heads`, `flush`, `follow`), `tests/test_ui_events_light.py` (its fake `subscribe` yields only `session` events)

**Why:** #1544 (TD-572) rewrote when the events stream sends the groups. `test_ui_events_light.py` pushes four `session` deltas and nothing else, so every branch the PR added for another event, and two more (the dedupe and the flush's retry), are held by no test. Probe: each change below, one at a time, then `pytest -q tests/test_ui_events_light.py tests/test_ui_waiting_wiring.py tests/test_ui.py tests/test_ui_stop.py tests/test_ui_teams.py` (the two `test_ui.py` model-name tests fail on a stale venv, `agentorc-0.0.1`, and are deselected): every one still passes.
- `gone` on a light stream sends `{**ev, **groups}` instead of `ev` alone (`if light: … continue` replaced by `if False:`), so a light page gets the whole fleet's groups it was promised not to.
- `gone`'s `fresh_heads(..., always=True)` without `always`: a `gone` whose reading equals the last one sent carries no groups, and the page keeps the card of the record that went in its team count.
- `repos`/`doing`: `if not light: dirty.set()` removed: the flush that replaces the old per-event `groups` message never fires after a `doing` line.
- `fresh_heads`'s dedupe (`key == last["key"]` → `False`): a reading equal to the last is sent again, which the module's own docstring says it does not.
- `flush`'s `except … dirty.set()` without the `dirty.set()`: one failed read and the groups wait for the next delta.

**Related:** TD-572 (#1544).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1556) — `tests/test_ui_events_paths.py`, a sibling of `test_ui_events_light.py` whose fake `subscribe` takes each test's events: a `gone` carries the groups unchanged on `/events` and is sent alone on `?light=1`; a `doing` and a `repos` event are passed through and followed by one `groups`; a reading equal to the last is not sent; a flush whose reading failed (`render_heads` raising once) sends on its next turn. Each of the five probes fails a test; the repo reading is dated days back so its ages hold still between two readings.

## TD-592: A `/clear` reads `working` until the next turn ends: `SessionStart` with source `clear` lands at the composer and fires no `Stop`

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** bug
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul; Paul: *this session has been sitting idle since I ran the /clear, but its chip says working here in the focus screen and in the org screen*)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/adapters/claude_code/hook.py` (`SESSION_START_AT_THE_COMPOSER`), design §4.2's state table.

**Why:** `/clear` fires `SessionEnd` (reason `clear`, ignored: the process lives on) and then `SessionStart` (source `clear`), which fell through to `STATE_EVENTS` and reported `working`. No turn follows a `/clear`, so no `Stop` reported `idle`, and the Focus and Org chips read `working` at an empty composer until the next turn ended, headed for `stalled?` at `STALL_AFTER` — the shape TD-155 fixed for `resume`.

**Related:** TD-155 (`resume`), TD-090 (`compact`), TD-283 (`startup` with no prompt).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1565) — `SESSION_START_AT_THE_COMPOSER = {"resume", "clear"}`; design §4.2's state table carries the row. Held by `test_a_clear_lands_at_the_composer`; TD-283's test now asserts `clear` → `idle`.

## TD-577: **Open shell here** replaces the page it was pressed on with the new shell's Focus; it should open in a new tab or window

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Blocked by:** TD-579
**Location:** design §4.5a *card: more ▾* (Open shell here), *Focus: Open shell here*, *card: Focus* and *Pop out* (the new-tab and window rules); `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the `shell-here` press sets `location.href` to the new shell's `/focus/<id>`, ~L983); `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/focus.html` (~L104), `card.html` (~L152)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12: *opening a shell should not overwrite the current window (should be new tab or new window)*. He pressed **Open shell here** from a session's Focus to run a command beside it, and the Focus he was working in was replaced by the shell's. Getting it back meant navigating back, and the terminal re-attached. The press always does this, from a card's *more ▾* as well as from Focus.

**Fix:** design it first, then build it:
1. Decide the target: a new tab, a popped-out window as **Pop out** opens one (row *Pop out*), or the browser's choice, with modifiers honoured as the **Focus** link honours them.
2. Decide the opening itself: the page has to open the tab or window synchronously in the click, before the `shell-here` RPC answers, or the browser blocks it as a popup. That means opening a placeholder and pointing it at `/focus/<id>` once the id comes back, and closing it, with the error shown on the pressing page, if the create is refused.
3. State in §4.5a that the pressing page stays where it was.
Then the build: `app.js`'s `shell-here` branch, and a test that the press no longer sets `location.href`.

**Done when** **Open shell here** leaves the page it was pressed on in place, and the shell's Focus opens in a new tab or window, from Focus and from a card.

**Related:** TD-572 (the Focus tabs' cost: more tabs are cheap since #1544).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the designer; archived with its build TD-579, PR #1563) — **Open shell here** opens the shell's Focus in a new tab (Shift, or a press in a popped-out window: a window as Pop out opens one), the pressing page stays, design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here* and *card: more ▾*.

## TD-579: Build TD-577: **Open shell here** opens the shell's Focus in a new tab (Shift, or a popped-out window: a window as Pop out opens one), the placeholder opened in the press and sent to `/focus/<id>` when the create answers; the pressing page stays

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-577's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here* (the rule) and *card: more ▾*, §4.5 screen 1 *+ New ▾*; `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the act handler's `shell-here` branch ~L983, which sets `location.href` after `await act(...)`; `AO.popOut` ~L380 and `AO.popFeatures` / `AO.popName` ~L368, whose window features and name the window form reuses; `AO.poppedId` ~L3697); `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/focus.html` (~L104) and `card.html` (~L152), the two buttons; `tests/test_ui.py` (~L1776, the Focus buttons), `tests/test_ui_org.py` (~L943), `tests/test_ui_popout.py` (the window form's neighbours)

**Why:** TD-577: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *opening a shell should not overwrite the current window (should be new tab or new window)*; the press replaced the Focus he was working beside, and getting it back meant navigating back and re-attaching.

**Fix:**
1. `app.js`: the `shell-here` branch moves ahead of the `await`. In the press: `window.open("", "_blank")` for a tab, or, when `ev.shiftKey` or `AO.poppedId` is set, `window.open("", "", AO.popFeatures(null))` for a window; the handler needs the event, so pass it from the click listener. A null result: `AO.toast("the browser blocked the tab — allow pop-ups for this page")` (the window's words for a window) and return before any RPC. Otherwise write the placeholder — `document.title` and one line, *opening a shell in <dir>…*, the dir from the button's `data-dir` (add it to both templates) — then `await act(id, "shell-here")`; on `res.id` set `w.name = AO.popName(res.id)` for a window and `w.location.href` to `/focus/<id>` (`?window=1` for a window); on a thrown refusal `w.close()` and let the handler's own error path show it. The pressing page never sets `location.href` for this act.
2. The templates: `data-dir="{{ s.dir }}"` on both buttons; the Focus button's `title` says *a shell session in this session's directory, in a new tab (Shift: a window)*.
3. Tests: the branch no longer assigns `location.href` (a source assertion on the act handler, or a node probe of it as `test_ui_popout.py` runs one); the templates carry `data-dir`; the Focus button's title names the tab. A browser-driven check is not expected — the act is `window.open`, which the suite cannot drive; the builder looks at it (design §4.9b: a press from a Focus tab, a Shift+press, and a press from a popped-out window, each leaving the pressing page in place) and names the look in the PR.

**Done when** **Open shell here** leaves the page it was pressed on in place and the shell's Focus opens in a new tab — a window as Pop out opens one on Shift or from a popped-out window — from Focus and from a card's *more ▾*; a refused create closes the placeholder and shows the refusal on the pressing page; the tests above pass and the builder's look is named in the PR.

**Related:** TD-577 (the design), TD-046 (Pop out), TD-572 (a Focus tab's cost).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1563) — `AO.shellHere` in `app.js` opens the tab or window in the press with the *opening a shell in <dir>…* placeholder, sends it to `/focus/<id>` (`?window=1` and its name for a window) when the create answers, closes it on a refusal; the buttons carry `data-dir` and the new title. Held by `tests/test_ui_popout.py` (`test_open_shell_here_opens_beside_the_page_it_was_pressed_on`, a node probe; `test_open_shell_here_never_moves_the_pressing_page`). The builder's look on a scratch home is the PR's UI check: a Focus tab, a Shift+press, a popped-out window and a card's *more ▾* each left the pressing page in place; a refused create closed the placeholder and toasted the refusal.

## TD-594: §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here* says the window is sized as the browser remembers for the session; the build opens it at the default size

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (docs-audit-ao-1, the auditor, covering #1561–#1567)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `docs/design/4.5a-controls.md` row *Focus | Open shell here* (the Shift / popped-out sentence); `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` `AO.shellHere` and `AO.popFeatures`

**Why:** The row reads *"Shift+press, or a press in a popped-out window, opens it as **Pop out** opens one instead — a chromeless window named `ao-focus-<id>`, sized as the browser remembers for the session (row *Pop out*)"*. Pop out remembers a size per session (`store.get(`win.${id}`)`), keyed by the id of the session being popped. `AO.shellHere` (#1563) opens the window **before** the create answers, so the new shell's id does not exist yet, and calls `window.open("", "", AO.popFeatures(null))`: always the default `popup,width=1184,height=860`, which `test_open_shell_here_opens_beside_the_page_it_was_pressed_on` asserts (`got["win"]["features"] == "popup,width=1184,height=860"`). Nothing is remembered for a session that did not exist; the sentence promises a size the code cannot read. (The window is also opened under no name and renamed to `ao-focus-<id>` after the create, which the row does say.)

**Fix:** reword the clause in the row: the window opens at Pop out's default size, and remembers its own from then on as any popped-out window does. No behaviour change, and no history line (a wording of the same fact).

**Done when** §4.5a's row says the window opens at the default size; `pdm run test` passes (the doc-bound tests read this table).

**Related:** TD-577, TD-579 (#1563), TD-046.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1581) — §4.5a's *Focus | Open shell here* row says the Shift / popped-out window opens at **Pop out**'s default size, the shell having no id to remember a size by until the create answers, and remembers its own size from then on as any popped-out window does (`app.js` stores `win.<id>` once its Focus loads with `?window=1`). Wording only; no behaviour change.

## TD-586: The `gate:` seam: a repo's merge gate is a command, `check_cadence.py` only its default

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-dc-decouple, with Paul)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/repoconfig.py`, `src/sessionorc/cadence.py`, the td flow's review stage, the review card

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12: dev-cadence must work for any session with no ShiftLead on the machine, and ShiftLead should recommend dev-cadence but not require it, without the two drifting. The [ADR 2026-10-12](decisions/2026-10-12-ledgerboard-dev-cadence-shiftlead.md) (decided by Paul the same day) puts the ledger and board formats in a third repo, `ShiftLead/ledgerboard`, read by both with no second parser. Today the gate is `scripts/check_cadence.py` or nothing, and nothing reads as "could not look".

**Fix:** per the ADR's *What ShiftLead requires*: `gate:` in `.shiftlead.yml`, a command that exits 0 for a mergeable PR (`{pr}` filled), judged by exit code alone; the default, when `scripts/check_cadence.py` exists, is that script with `--json` and its rows on the card; with none, the review stage never merges on its own and the card says "no gate: a person merges".

**Done when** a repo with `gate: "true"`, one with the default, and one with none each behave as the ADR says, with tests.

**Related:** [ADR 2026-10-12](decisions/2026-10-12-ledgerboard-dev-cadence-shiftlead.md); TD-588 (`{gate}` in the briefs), TD-591 (the missing-gate line).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1572) — `sessionorc.cadence.gate` reads `gate:` (set, defaulted to `scripts/check_cadence.py --pr {pr} --json`, absent); a set gate is run by `sh -c` in the checkout and judged by its exit code, one row *gate: <command, filled> exited <n>*; a repo with no gate is recorded once a PR as `verdict: none` — nothing run, nobody told — and `ao status -v` prints *no gate: a person merges*; `shiftlead.repoconfig` accepts the key. Tests: `tests/test_cadence_policy.py` (the three kinds, the exit code, the no-gate record and a gate gained later), `tests/test_repoconfig.py`. The briefs' `{gate}` is TD-588's, the seam state on the Repo page and in `ao doctor` TD-591's.

## TD-578: Focus: an editor button that opens the session's current transcript file in the person's editor, beside **Transcript**

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus header* **Transcript** (the page in a new tab), *Transcript* (the page's **VS Code** on the raw file), *Focus side panel, Session card* **editor** button (the directory), §4.5 screen 9 *Transcript*; §5 `person.open_in`; `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/focus.html` (~L106–110 the Transcript link, ~L286 the Session card's editor button), `src/shiftlead/ui/transcript.py` `transcript_editor` (the file link the Transcript page builds), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` ~L1385 (where it is built, for the Transcript page alone)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12: *add a button on our focus screen to open the current transcript in vscode/other (should have same file-open command as others). This will give the ability for a user to easily read/search the current transcript in their favorite editor.* Today the transcript file reaches the editor only through the Transcript page: Focus → **Transcript** (a new tab, a snapshot of the last twenty turns) → its **VS Code**. Reading or searching the whole of a live session's conversation is the editor's work, and the person is on Focus when they want it; the link itself already exists (`transcript_editor`, the `open_in` template with the file's path, §4.5a *Transcript*), so Focus lacks one press, not a mechanism.

**Fix:** design it first, then build it: a button on Focus that is the editor button's template (§5 `person.open_in`, the same form as the Session card's button and the Transcript page's **VS Code**) with the transcript file's path (`transcript_path`, §4.3) in place of the directory, on the record's host. The design round settles where it sits (the header beside **Transcript**, or the Session card beside the directory's editor button) and its label, and states it in §4.5a; the same absences as the Transcript page's button — `open_in: none`, another host's record, a record with no tool session id (a `shell`, a command run) — and it appears when the hook reports one, as **Transcript** does. Then the build: `focus.html`, the link built where Focus's `editor` is, a test that the href is the template with the file's path.

**Done when** a press on Focus opens the session's current transcript file in the person's editor through the same `open_in:` as every other file link, and the button is absent wherever the Transcript page's **VS Code** is.

**Related:** TD-166 (the Transcript page and its VS Code), TD-154, TD-095 / TD-525 (the editor button on the card and the Session card), TD-532 (a file link's two launches).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the designer; archived with its build TD-597, PR #1580) — the Focus header's **‹› VS Code** opens the session's transcript file in the person's editor, the Transcript page's own link beside **Transcript**, design §4.5a *Focus header* **‹› VS Code**, §4.5 screen 9, §4.2 `transcript`.

## TD-580: A shell the person opened and types into is refused the person's own acts (`ao promote`, …) because every ShiftLead pane reads as a session

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-12 (the designer) — (1) the person's own shell is a `shell` record, interactive (`unattended: false`), with no `role`, no team and an empty `controllers` list — what Open shell here, + New ▾ Shell and `ao shell` from outside a pane make; a session-made shell lists its creator as controller from birth, so none qualifies; `person_shell(record)` beside `PERSON_ONLY` is the one definition and `person_only` reads it; (2) the right is the record's state at each request, never kept: a mode flip, a controller added or a role loses it on the next call; (3) Paul's risk is written in §4.8a as the person's own doing — the pane's signals cannot tell a hand-started agent from the shell's prompt, no narrowing is designed (a first-process rule reads /proc per request and is defeated by `exec`), the log names the shell's id; (4) one gate, every `PERSON_ONLY` RPC alike, the act still recorded as the shell's, the identity table unchanged. §4.8 *The person's own shell is the person*, §4.8a *A process under the person's shell is the shell*, §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*. No mockup: nothing drawn changes. Built by TD-596. Was: Open.
**Blocked by:** TD-596
**Location:** design §4.8 *A person's own act is a named RPC, and the gate is one list*; §4.8a (identity: how the host agent tells which session is calling); §6 *Promote*; §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*; `src/sessionorc/agent_common.py` (`person_only` ~L287); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`is_person`, `PERSON_ONLY`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12, after `ao promote shiftlead` was refused in a shell he had opened with **Open shell here** (*error: ao-ao-paul-ao-paul-shell cannot run promote: a person's own act, refused to every session*): *A shell being directly controlled by the user should have permissions to promote/other without interference. I suppose the risk is that the user then creates an llm session there - but that's probably out of scope (and on the user).* Today the only place the person can run a person-only act from the terminal is a terminal outside ShiftLead, so the dashboard's own shell is no use for it.

**Fix:** design it first:
1. Decide which records count as the person's: an **interactive** (`attended`) `shell` session that the person created, with no role and no `unattended`. Name the fields that decide it, as §4.8a would read them.
2. Decide whether the right is the record's for its whole life, or only while it stays interactive. A flip to unattended, a role, or a manager as controller should lose it.
3. Decide the risk Paul named: an agent started inside that shell inherits its identity. Say it plainly in §4.8a as the person's responsibility (out of scope, Paul), or narrow the right (e.g. only to a process the shell itself ran, not its descendants) if §4.8a can tell them apart.
4. Make `person_only` read the decision in one place, so every person-only RPC follows it.
Then the build, with tests that a person's interactive shell may promote and an agent session, an unattended shell or a role's session still may not.

**Done when** `ao promote` (and every other person-only act) runs from a shell the person opened with **Open shell here** or **+ New ▾ Shell**, and is still refused to every agent session.

**Related:** TD-581 (the promote press under `auto`), TD-577 (Open shell here's tab), TD-077 (identity).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1583) — designed in #1575, built by TD-596.

## TD-596: Build TD-580: `person_shell(record)` beside `PERSON_ONLY` — a `shell` record, interactive, no role, no team, no controllers, passes every person-only RPC in `person_only`; the act recorded as the shell's; the list's test holds the exception

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-580's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Open
**Location:** design §4.8 *The person's own shell is the person*, §4.8a *A process under the person's shell is the shell*, §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*; `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`PERSON_ONLY` ~L118, `is_person` ~L176: add `person_shell(record)`), `src/sessionorc/agent_common.py` (`person_only` ~L287: takes the caller's record, or a lookup, and passes when `person_shell` does; the refusal's words), every RPC that calls `person_only` (the thirty of the list, `agent_*.py`; the call site hands the record — `self.sessions.get(caller)` or the home's view of a node's record, §4.4a *Acts across the link*, where the check runs at the node), `src/sessionorc/models.py` (~L902 `adapter`, ~L912 `unattended`, ~L974 `controllers`, ~L1057 `role`: the fields read), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (the refusal printed as the agent words it); `tests/test_person_only.py` (the list-to-code test), `tests/test_identity*.py` (an act from the shell's pane is logged as the shell)

**Why:** TD-580: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *A shell being directly controlled by the user should have permissions to promote/other without interference*; `ao promote shiftlead` from a shell opened with **Open shell here** was refused (*a person's own act, refused to every session*), so the dashboard's own shell could not do what a terminal outside ShiftLead can.

**Fix:**
1. `mail.person_shell(record) -> bool`: `record.adapter == "shell" and not record.unattended and not record.role and not record.team and not record.controllers` (the team field as the record names it; a seat is never a shell). Docstring: §4.8's sentence.
2. `person_only(caller, act, section, record=None)`: passes when `is_person(caller)` or `record is not None and person_shell(record)`; every call site hands the caller's record from the agent's sessions (a caller it does not know stays a session, refused as today); the refusal reads *a person's own act, refused to every session but the person's own shell (design §4.8)*. Across the link (§4.4a) the node runs the check with the record it holds, as it runs it today.
3. Nothing else: the identity verdict (§4.8a) is untouched, `by:` fields and the identity log keep the shell's id, `is_person` keeps meaning *no caller*; where an RPC writes `"person"` for `is_person(caller)` it writes the shell's id for a shell, as it does for any session.
4. Tests: `test_person_only.py` — for each RPC in `PERSON_ONLY`, a person's shell record (adapter `shell`, `unattended` false, no role, no team, empty controllers) passes and the refusal is absent; an agent session, an unattended shell, a shell with a controller and a shell with a role are each refused with the new words; a record not found is refused; the list-to-code test still holds both directions; a `promote` from the shell is recorded with the shell's id (`by`); `ao promote` from a session that is a person's shell prints the agent's reply, not the refusal.

**Done when** `ao promote` (and every other person-only act) runs from a shell the person opened with **Open shell here** or **+ New ▾ Shell**, is still refused to every agent session, an unattended shell, a controlled shell and a role's session, the act is logged as the shell's, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-580 (the design), TD-581 (the promote press under `auto`), TD-077 (identity), TD-577 / TD-579 (Open shell here's tab).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1583) — `mail.person_shell(record)`; `agent_common.person_only` takes this host's records and lets a person's shell by; the refusal reads *refused to every session but the person's own shell*; a shell's promote is recorded `by` the shell's id; `ao td add` asks the record before its client-side refusal. Held by `test_person_only.py` (the exception against the whole list), `test_promote.py`, `test_identity.py` (a request from the shell's own pane under `enforce`), `test_cli_teams.py`.

## TD-601: Build TD-582: the mail gate's cross-team edge on the `project` badge, its refusal's words, `ao --skill`'s and the briefs' lines on a peer's agreement

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-582's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.10 *The message gate is weaker than `control`* (*across teams, by project*) and *An agreement between peers*, §9 invariant 9; `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`message_edge` ~L267: a fifth edge after `team`, `if me.project and me.project == it.project: return "project"`, the docstring's list; `message_gate` ~L307: the refusal's words gain *its project*), `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`project` ~L979, read only), `src/shiftlead/skill.md` (the `ao msg` line *reaches only your controllers, your members, your team, …*: add *a session of your project*, and one line on a peer's agreement), `src/shiftlead/briefs/*.md` (the *mail from anyone else is information you weigh* line in grinder, manager, manager_on_call, anchor, designer: *a peer's agreement binds once written in the shared entry, the PR or the design — §4.10*), `docs/briefs/techlead-context.md` and the repo's brief parts under `docs/briefs/` (the same line; a held path), `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py` if it quotes the gate; `tests/test_mail.py` (the gate's tests)

**Why:** TD-582: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *a way to allow sessions from separate teams (or the same team) to coordinate via messages so that they can come to a consensus on solutions*; a session of one team messaging a session of another is refused today, and two peers who agree have agreed on nothing that binds.

**Fix:**
1. `message_edge`: the `project` edge after `team` — both carry the same non-empty `project`; the docstring names five edges and §9 invariant 9's exception for both badges.
2. `message_gate`'s refusal: *not one of its controllers, its members, its team, its project, or a controller of a session it controls (design §4.10)*.
3. `ao --skill` (`src/shiftlead/skill.md`): the reach line gains *a session of your project*, and under *Mail* one bullet — *An agreement with a peer is a `steer` (your default, a bound) or an `ask` with `--answer`s; it binds once you write it in the shared entry's Status, the PR or the design, citing the thread; a disagreement goes up your own path, never the peer's (§4.10 *An agreement between peers*)*.
4. The briefs' *mail from anyone else is information you weigh* line gains *— a peer's agreement binds once written down (§4.10)*, in each built-in brief and in `docs/briefs/` (a held path: the techlead reads it).
5. Tests (`tests/test_mail.py`): two sessions of different teams with the same `project` may message (edge `"project"`), on every kind; two with different projects, or one with no project, are refused with the new words; an empty `project` on both is no edge; the four existing edges unchanged; no copy goes to either side's controllers on a project-edge message.

**Done when** two sessions of different teams in one project can put a question to each other with `ao msg` and settle it on one thread, two of unrelated projects are still refused naming the rule, the skill and the briefs say what a peer's agreement binds, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-582 (the design), TD-039 (two controllers over one worker), TD-134 (the disagreement's tests), TD-462 (an `ask` to several).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1593) — `sessionorc.mail.message_edge` gains the `project` edge after `team` (both badges the same and non-empty); `message_gate`'s refusal names *its project*; `ao --skill`'s reach bullet gains *a session of your project* and when a peer's agreement binds; the built-in briefs (grinder, manager, manager_on_call, anchor, designer, hunter, auditor) and `docs/briefs/techlead-context.md` §5 say a peer's agreement binds once written down. `ao team --skill` (`team_skill.md`) says the mail gate keys on both badges. No copy rule changed: a copy is made only for mail `about` a record the sender controls. `tests/test_mail.py::test_the_project_badge_is_an_edge_across_teams_and_copies_nobody`.

## TD-582: Sessions of different teams cannot message each other, and nothing makes two peers' agreement bind: the mail gate has no cross-team edge and no shape for a consensus

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Blocked by:** TD-601
**Location:** design §4.10 *The message gate is weaker than `control`* (the four edges), *A disagreement, worked* and *A bounded exchange, counted by thread*; §9 invariant 9 (the one named exception, the team badge); §4.9 (`team` is one badge per session); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`message_edge`, `message_gate`); `src/shiftlead/briefs/grinder.md` and `manager.md` (*mail from anyone else is information you weigh*)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12, through Add entry: *There should be a way to allow sessions from separate teams (or the same team) to coordinate via messages so that they can come to a consensus on solutions. If there is not already a way to do this, lets set one up.* Within one team the way exists: §4.10's sideways edge lets any two sessions carrying the same `team` badge message each other, on every kind, and `ao --skill` names it. Across teams there is none. `message_edge` admits four edges — upward, downward, the shared `team` badge, a shared controlled target — and a session of one team that messages a session of another is refused with *not one of its controllers, its members, its team, or a controller of a session it controls*. The one two-team case the design has worked is TD-039's, two managers over one worker, and its exchange ends in a ruling (the first controller's `reply` binds the worker), not an agreement between equals. Two more things stand between a message and a consensus even inside a team: `team` is one string on the record, so a session is in one team only (§4.9), and every brief tells a worker that *mail from anyone else is information you weigh*, so two peers who agree have agreed on nothing that binds either — the agreement reaches no record, no ledger entry and no board line unless one of them writes it. The harm: two teams on one repo, or two grinders on one package, that have to settle a shared interface, a shared file, or which of two fixes lands, cannot talk, and the person is the only path between them.

**Fix:** design it first, in §4.10:
1. **The edge.** Decide who may message across teams: (a) any two sessions whose teams share a project (`org.yml`'s `projects:`); (b) only the two teams' techlead seats or managers, with members asking through their own seat as they ask the person (§4.9b); or (c) an edge the person writes in `org.yml` (`teams.<name>.talks_to:`). Each is one line in `message_edge`. The design says which and says why it is still not a general peer channel — §4.10 and TD-039 refused one on purpose — so this is either a deliberate widening of §9 invariant 9's exception or a new edge that keys on `project`, and the invariant is amended either way.
2. **The consensus.** Decide what an agreement between peers is. Either a shape in mail — an `ask` to the peer with `--answer`s, closed by a `reply` whose `answer` index is the choice, with a bound as a disagreement has, so a peer who never answers does not hold the other, and what happens at the bound (the asker goes with its default, or the question goes up each team's path) — or nothing new in mail and a rule that the agreement is written down (a ledger entry's Status, a line in the design, a PR) before either acts on it, since a brief holds a peer's word as information, never instruction.
3. **What it never does.** No message types into a pane, no peer acts on a peer (§9 invariants 5 and 11), the depth bounds hold, and the design says whether a cross-team thread is copied to each side's controllers the way a message `about` a session is, so a manager sees its member negotiating.
4. Then the build: `message_edge`'s new edge with its refusal naming the rule, `ao --skill`'s line, the briefs' sentence, and tests that two sessions of different teams may message along the edge and two with no edge are still refused.

**Done when** two sessions of different teams can put a question to each other with `ao msg`, settle it on one thread, and §4.10 says what the settlement binds and how a peer who does not answer is got past; a same-team pair needs nothing new, and the entry says so.

**Related:** TD-039 (two controllers over one worker, archived: its exchange is a ruling, not a consensus), TD-052 (mail), TD-462 (`conflict` folded into an `ask` to several), TD-134 (the disagreement's tests), design §4.9b (a team's questions go through its techlead).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the designer; archived with its build TD-601, PR #1593) — two sessions with the same non-empty `project` badge may message whatever their teams, mail only (design §4.10 *across teams, by project*, §9 invariant 9); a peer's agreement is a `steer` or an `ask` with `--answer`s and binds once written in the shared entry, the PR or the design; a disagreement goes up each side's own path (§4.10 *An agreement between peers*). A same-team pair needed nothing new: the `team` edge already held.

## TD-599: The Inbox's *Answered for you* group may repeat FYI: fold it in, or give it a **Dismiss all** of its own

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-12 (the designer; mockup `Inbox.dc.html`, shot `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-12-td599-answered-dismiss-all.png`) — **not redundant**: every *answered for you* row is an answer a session gave in the person's name, which the person may **Overrule** (a decision still theirs; no FYI row holds one), and folding a handful of them into FYI's twelve hours of system notes and closed mail would bury them; the team header's mark needs no group of its own, but the Overrule does. So the group stays, uncounted, and its heading gains **Dismiss all** by FYI's rule — one confirm with the number, the group's ids on screen only, never a row that arrived after the page was drawn, drawn only while the group holds a row. §4.5a *Inbox: Answered for you, Dismiss all*. Built by TD-602. Was: Open.
**Location:** design §4.5a *Inbox row: answered for you*, *Inbox: the FYI count, **Dismiss all***, *team header* **answered for you** count; §4.5 screen 6 (the sections' order); §4.9b *Everything answered for the person is told to the person*; §4.10 *The Inbox is a queue*; `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (`INBOX_SECTIONS`, `_answered_of`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/inbox.html` (`#sec-fyi`, `#dismissall`), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the Dismiss all handler reads `#rows-fyi` only); mockup `docs/mockups/Inbox.dc.html`

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12, through Add entry: *Lets evaluate if the "answered for you" section is redundant to fyi, and if so combine them. If not, lets add a "dismiss all" option on the "answered for you" section.* Both are uncounted, and an *answered for you* entry is an FYI by kind — a `note` filed from the answerer (§4.9b) — drawn in its own group after *Waiting on them*, with *Later* between it and FYI. What it has that an FYI row has not: **Overrule** (a reply to the asker on the question's thread, with a copy to the answerer, which hands the asker an outcome debt), the question set off as a quotation with its source, and the team header's **answered for you** count, a mark since the person last opened the group. What it lacks: FYI's **Dismiss all** reads `#rows-fyi` alone, so a run of a busy techlead's answers is cleared one **Dismiss** at a time. The harm: the person either reads a second "no action needed" group beside FYI, or clears it by hand row by row.

**Fix:** design it first, in §4.5a and §4.5 screen 6:
1. **The evaluation.** Say whether the group earns its place: what the person does with an *answered for you* row that they do not do with an FYI — **Overrule** is a decision on a teammate's answer, FYI rows hold none — and whether the team header's count needs a group to be "since last opened".
2. **If redundant:** the rows move into FYI, keeping their **Overrule**, quotation and source; the team header's count reads FYI's *new* mark or goes; `INBOX_SECTIONS` loses `answered`; the rail's *Urgency* group and the mockup follow.
3. **If not:** the group's heading gains **Dismiss all**, FYI's own rule — one confirm with the number, the ids on screen only, never a row that arrived after the page was drawn — a row in §4.5a beside FYI's.
4. Then the build, with tests that the chosen shape draws and that a dismiss sends only on-screen ids.

**Done when** §4.5a says which of the two it is, the Inbox draws it, and the person can clear the answered rows they have read in one press.

**Related:** TD-075 (step 2 built *Answered for you*), TD-079 (the Inbox as a queue, FYI's Dismiss all), TD-582 (another Add-entry draft by this seat, on cross-team mail).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1597) — designed in the round of TD-599 (§4.5a *Inbox: Answered for you, **Dismiss all***), built by TD-602.

## TD-612: `test_mail`'s adoption test gave its steer a one-second bound, and a slow runner's close and create outlast it

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (grinder-ao-1, met on #1604's CI)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `tests/test_mail.py` (`test_a_create_under_the_askers_name_adopts_its_orphaned_questions`)

**Why:** #1604, a docs-only PR, failed CI on Python 3.13 (run 38331441556) and passed on rerun. The test sent its `steer` with `bound=1`, closed the asker and created it again. On a slow runner that took longer than a second, so the tick's `_sweep_mail` lapsed the orphaned steer as closed before the create adopted it. The test then failed at `entries[steer]["closed_reason"] is None` with `orphaned: {how: closed}`. A flake like this fails unrelated PRs and teaches a reader to rerun rather than read.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1607). The steer carries `bound=600`, and the test's last `_sweep_mail` is handed `now + 601 s`, which lapses the steer by the clock the sweep is given. The test's `asyncio.sleep(1.1)` is gone.

**Related:** TD-463 (the CI flakes since 2026-10-03), TD-600 (the last flake fixed the same way: compare what the test means, not the clock).
