## TD-358: Apply never restarts a member that declared out of work: it resumes its old run, on its pre-flow brief, when its lane gains work

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-06 (the anchor, after Paul's first Apply on ao-grind)
**Owner:** anchor
**Kind:** live-check #1186
**Status:** Resolved. Built in #1186 (grinder-ao-1); the live check dropped by Paul, 2026-10-12 (below). Was: **Read 2026-10-12 (the anchor): the scratch-home route is the person's, so the check waits for Paul's Apply.** A team member must be an agent's session (`teams.py` refuses a shell profile, §4.9), and a Claude session in a scratch home needs a logged-in scratch `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — credentials, the person's tier — or `~/.claude`, which the scratch home's hooks would write into. Asked by steer `m-6a272ca2abcd` (default: keep waiting for Paul's next Apply). Also read: a member that declares out of work is now closed by the tick as `finished` about 18 minutes later (grinder-ao-2 declared 23:16Z on 2026-10-11, closed 23:34Z), and `_brief_restart` restarts no member the tick did not close for `brief`, `flow` or `cache`, so an Apply after that window restarts nothing — the window in which the check can be read is those minutes. **Paul, 2026-10-10 (with ao-paul): stop waiting for the event, cause it.** An Apply on a team whose idle members have declared out of work is a press anyone with a scratch home can make. The anchor runs the check on a scratch home (a short `AGENTORC_HOME`, a scratch team of two members on a throwaway repo, each declaring out of work, then `ao team flow --apply <team> <flow>`) and reads it as below, with that home's `AGENTORC_HOME` set for `ao status -v`. Or it asks Paul for an Apply on ao-grind while its members sit idle and declared. **Read 2026-10-09 (the anchor):** still no Apply — no session carries `relaunch` and none has a `why: flow` restart (`ao status --json`). **Read 2026-10-08 (the anchor, TD-426):** no Apply found since #1186 went live (none in the host agent's journal since 2026-10-06), so nothing to read yet. **Live 2026-10-06** (`ao promote status`: live a11bdf1 holds #1186's c79837bf; grinder-ao-1). Nothing to read yet: the check waits for the person's next Apply on a team whose idle members have declared out of work, an event no member can cause, so it is the anchor's. When it comes, read it as below. Built in #1186 (grinder-ao-1): `_brief_restart`'s guard passes a declared member whose record carries `relaunch`, design §4.9c *Switching* says so, and `tests/test_relaunch.py` holds the three cases. Left: the live check. Once #1186 is live (`ao promote status`), at the next Apply on a team whose idle members have declared out of work, read `ao status -v` (read only) within a tick of the press: each such member is restarted (`restarts` ends `why: flow`), its `{stage}` line names the flow's brief, and no member with unpushed work was restarted.
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_brief_restart`: `if s.out_of_work or s.restart_wanted: return`, before `why` is read), the mail that tells a member its lane gained entries; design §4.9c *Switching* (`docs/design/4.9c-flows.md`: an idle member is restarted by the tick under `why: flow`)

**Why:** On 2026-10-06 at 20:58 Paul pressed **Apply** on ao-grind. `rpc_relaunch` rewrote the launch records of grinder-ao-1, grinder-ao-2 and designer-ao-1 and marked each `relaunch`.
- Six minutes later (`ao --json status`, 21:04), grinder-ao-1 and designer-ao-1 read `idle`, with `out_of_work` and `relaunch` both set. By 21:25 all three had declared out of work: the host agent's lane news, which tells only a member with `out_of_work`, told each of them. grinder-ao-2 may still have been working at 20:58 (it landed a board line at 21:00:21).
- `_brief_restart` returns on `s.out_of_work or s.restart_wanted` before it reads `why`, so the tick restarted none of them.
- At 21:25, #1179 gave their lanes new entries, and the host agent told each of them: 5 entries to each grinder, 2 to the designer.
- Each picked the entries up in its old run: the panes date from 19:48, 20:20 and 20:01, before the Apply. They work on their pre-flow briefs (`grinder.stage.md`, and no stage for the designer), and the `td` stage briefs reach them only at a restart for some other reason.
- The design (§4.9c *Switching*, `docs/design/4.9c-flows.md`) says Apply *relaunches the idle grinders*, and that a hook-confirmed idle member holding no claim is closed and created again by the tick under `why: flow`. It does not say what happens to a member that has declared out of work. The code makes that case follow rule 2 (*it declared: rule 2 or the team's next start is what starts it*), which leaves a person's Apply waiting on the member's own word.

**Fix:**
- Say in §4.9c *Switching* what Apply does to a member that declared out of work. The anchor's reading, as written here: a person's Apply is the person's word, so `relaunch` restarts an idle, settled member whether or not it declared.
- Either let `why == "flow"` pass the `out_of_work` / `restart_wanted` guard (clearing them, since the new run starts fresh), or, when a member with a pending `relaunch` is told its lane gained work, restart it on the launch record instead of ringing the old run.
- The working member's case stays as designed: it is told on its `ao` replies.
- Tests:
  - an idle member that declared out of work is restarted under `why: flow` after a relaunch;
  - one with unpushed work is not;
  - a member without a `relaunch` mark keeps today's guard.

**Done when** an Apply on a team whose idle members have declared out of work restarts them on their stage briefs within a tick (their `{stage}` line names the flow's brief), and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-355 (the mark that outlives the Apply), TD-309 (archived: *Switching*), TD-334 (archived: rule 7's retry), TD-310 (the move that surfaced it).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (Paul, with ao-paul): the live check is dropped, not read. The fix is merged and tested (#1186: `_brief_restart` passes a declared member whose record carries `relaunch`; `tests/test_relaunch.py`, design §4.9c *Switching*). The guard now passes a declared member with a pending `relaunch` (`s.out_of_work and not s.relaunch`), so the case the check would watch is the case the tests hold. Separately, once a whole team has declared and that holds for `FINISHED_SETTLE` (10 min), rule 9 closes its idle, settled members as `finished` (about 18 minutes after the declaration in the one case seen), and their next start replays the current launch record. A team with one member still working closes nobody, so that path narrows the exposure but does not remove it; the tests are what the drop rests on. Causing the Apply on a scratch home would need a Claude login lent to it, which Paul judged not worth it. A recurrence gets a new entry.

## TD-603: Board lines have no identifier: the person quotes a line's text to refer to it in chat, a reply or a session

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (ao-paul, at Paul's ask)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-12 (the designer; mockup `Inbox.dc.html`, shot `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-12-td603-board-line-id.png`) — **derived, not written**, against the anchor's lean: every board line's id is the `board:<key>` the work orders already use (sha256 of `item_key()`, eight hex), which survives every edit a tool makes — the tick, `Closed:`, `Decided:`, `Due:`, replies appended — the very edits the lean feared; only a reword changes it, and the write-back already refuses a reworded line as moved. A written `UA-NNN` would need a counter shared by every writer of a board (sessions by hand, the write-back, the person, dev-cadence without ShiftLead) — two sessions adding at once take one number, as TD ids collided twice on 2026-10-12 — and a new line shape: a ledgerboard major and every consumer's sync. So no format change, nothing proposed to dev-cadence or ledgerboard, every old line has one. Drawn on every board row (copied on a click), printed by `ao board show` and `ao repo`, taken as `key` by the write-back's RPCs and `ao board edit --key`. §4.4 *A board line's id*, §4.5a *board row: id*, §4.7 `ao board show`. Built by TD-607. Was: Open.
**Location:** the board's `Format:` line (`docs/user_attention.md`; cadence §3.3's entry format, dev-cadence's; ledgerboard's once TD-584/TD-585 land); the board reader (§4.4 *Board write-back*); `board_reply` (`src/sessionorc/agent_inbox.py`) and Done / Snooze, which reach the line through `board.write_back` (`src/sessionorc/board.py`, `_find`: the line number, then the line's whole text); the Inbox's board rows and the Due strip (§4.5a)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-12: *should we add identifiers to the user attention items — that way I don't have to quote it to reference it?* Mail already has one (`m-6a272ca2abcd`) and a ledger entry has `TD-NNN`; a board line has only its date, its session and its words. To point a session at a line, or to ask about one in chat, the person pastes its head ("A team member must be a Claude session…"), and the line's whole text is also what a Reply, a Done or a Snooze finds the line by (`board.py` `_find`), so a session that rewords a line loses the person's reference to it and the press is refused as moved.

**Fix:** design first.
- Choose the id: written into the line at creation (a short `UA-NNN`, numbered per board like TD ids and never reused, the archive included), or derived (a short hash of date, session and the first words, which a reword changes). The anchor's lean: written, since a derived one is not stable under the edits a line gets (replies appended, *Closed:*).
- Where it is written: the `Format:` line is cadence's (dev-cadence) and the board's parser is to be ledgerboard's (TD-584/TD-585), so the change is proposed there, and lines written before it stay valid without one.
- Where it is drawn and accepted: the Inbox's board row and the Due strip show it; a Reply, a Done and a Snooze find the line by it before its text; `ao` and the SessionStart nudge print it; a person can type it in chat (`UA-12`) and a session can find the line by it (`grep`).
- Mockup of the row with the id.

**Done when** every new board line carries an id, the Inbox and the Due strip draw it, a reply or a close can name a line by it, and old lines without one still read.

**Related:** TD-584 / TD-585 (ledgerboard), TD-126 (a board reply's outcome), TD-587 (`ao board edit`).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1606) — designed in TD-603's round (§4.4 *A board line's id*, §4.5a *board row: id*, §4.7 `ao board show`), built by TD-607.

## TD-607: Build TD-603: every board line's id is its derived `board:<key>` — drawn and copied on every board row, `ao board show`, `ao board edit --key`, and `key` on the write-back's RPCs

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-603's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Built
**Location:** design §4.4 *A board line's id*, §4.5a *board row: id*, §4.7 `ao board show` / `ao board edit --key`; `src/sessionorc/workorders.py` (the `board:<key>` derivation ~L27–45, `PREFIX`, `_item_key`: make it the one function every board row and RPC uses, not only decided lines), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (each board row's `key`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/inbox_row.html` and the Due strip's and Repo page's board-row templates (the id in the head line, a click to copy), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the copy; every board press sends `key`), `src/sessionorc/agent_inbox.py` (`rpc_board_edit` ~L247, `rpc_board_reply` ~L404: an optional `key`; Decide is one of `board_edit`'s actions, no RPC of its own), `src/sessionorc/board.py` (`_find` ~L331: by key first over the open items, then line and text as today; the refusal's words), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao board show`, `ao board edit --key` once TD-587's verb exists — before it, `show` alone; `ao repo`'s board lines print the id), `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py` (the row's id); `tests/test_board.py`, `tests/test_workorders.py`, `tests/test_ui_inbox*.py`, `tests/test_cli.py`

**Why:** TD-603: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *should we add identifiers to the user attention items — that way I don't have to quote it to reference it?*

**Fix:**
1. One derivation: `workorders.key_of(line) -> "board:xxxxxxxx"` from the board reader's `item_key()` (ledgerboard's once TD-585 lands), used for every item the Inbox, the Due strip, the Repo page and `ao` read; the work orders keep using it.

3. The write-back: `board_edit` (every action: snooze, done, decide) and `board_reply` take an optional `key`; `_find` tries the open item whose key it is first (origin's tree, then the checkout's lines, as it reads today), then the line and text; with a `key` and no match, refused *no line board:<key> on the board — reworded or closed*. The page sends `key` with every press.
4. The CLI: `ao board show <board:key> [--repo]` prints line number, text and detail block (`--json`: `{key, line, text, detail, open, source}`), exit 1 with the refusal when none; `ao repo` prints the id on each board line it lists; `ao board edit --key` when TD-587 has built the verb.
5. Tests: the key is the same before and after a snooze, a reply, a decide and a close; differs after a reword; the row draws it; a press with `key` finds a line that moved; a press with a stale `key` is refused with the words; `ao board show` finds and refuses; the mockup regenerates unchanged.

**Done when** every board line shows its `board:<key>` on the Inbox, the Due strip and the Repo page, a click copies it, `ao board show` finds the line by it, the write-back's presses find the line by it, old lines need nothing, and the tests above pass; the builder's look (design §4.9b) is named in the PR.

**Related:** TD-603 (the design), TD-380 (decided lines as work orders, the key's first use), TD-587 (`ao board edit`), TD-584 / TD-585 (ledgerboard's `item_key`).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (PR #1606) — `workorders.ref` is every board line's id, and `workorders.show` finds a line by it on origin's board after a fetch, else the checkout's, open or closed, with the reader's detail block. `board._find` tries the open line whose id it is first, then the line and its text. A press that names only an id is found by it, and edits the line as it is now. An id no open line holds is refused as *no line board:<key> on the board — reworded or closed*. `board_edit` and `board_reply` take `key`; the page sends it with every press on a board row and draws it on the row (`.boardkey`, a click copies it). `ao board show` and `ao repo`'s due lines print it. `ao board edit --key` waits for TD-587's verb, written on its Fix. No help-list paragraph: the row's `title` is §4.5a's words. Held by `tests/test_board.py`, `tests/test_workorders.py`, `tests/test_ui_board.py`; the scratch-home look is the PR's UI check.

## TD-457: New work in a finished member's lane waits for the whole team to wind down: one live seat keeps it from winding down, and the only road back is a full team restart

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-08 (ao-paul, Paul asked why the grinders did not pick up TD-428)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-09 (the designer, PR #1334): §6 rule 8 *A member that finished while its team runs on* — (1) a crew member closed after declaring `out_of_work`, its team not wound down, whose lane gains an id its `lane_seen` lacks, is rule 8's news: the same `work_waiting` mark after `WORK_SETTLE`, and under `start` the home replays that member alone (its launch record, `why: work`, the ids, the five bounds; `ask` draws the row naming the member, its **Start** replaying the named members through a `work_start` RPC; `off` nothing); what a start replays is read at the start — a wound-down team whole, a running team's named members alone; rule 6's *told by neither rule* sentence replaced; (2) a seat still holds a wind-down, and rightly — (1) makes the reading moot for a member's lane; (3) `on_work` defaults to `start` (§5, rule 8's listing; the picker's *(default)*, `ON_WORK`'s comment, `agent_tick.py`, `agent_notify.py`, `settings_page.py` and the help paragraph are the build's); (4) no hold on rule 9's finished pass: the closed member is (1)'s on the next tick. §4.5a's row says the running-team form. The build is TD-466.
**Blocked by:** TD-466
**Location:** design §6 rule 6 (*An exited or closed member is not written to*), rule 8 (*Work for a team that wound down*, the **wound down** reading), rule 9 (*Finished is the home's reading*); §5 `teams.<team>.on_work`; `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`on_work` default `"ask"`, the finished pass, the work pass), `src/sessionorc/agent_notify.py`, `src/sessionorc/work.py` (`wound_down`)

**Why:** on 2026-10-09 at 03:32Z (2026-10-08 23:32 local) the tick closed grinder-ao-1, grinder-ao-2 and designer-ao-1 as *finished* (rule 9: each had declared out of work on an empty lane). Two minutes earlier, at 03:30Z, TD-428 merged (#1295), a pickable build in the grinders' lane — so the finished pass closed two members whose lane had just gained work on `origin/main`, before rule 6 had told them (the ledger read is the home checkout's file, which counts an entry only once that checkout holds it; a race the finished pass does not look for). After the close nobody was told and nothing started: rule 6 never writes to a closed member, and rule 8 waits for the team to read *wound down*, which needs none of its unattended sessions live — and the anchor seat was working (TD-426, #1311), so ao-grind read *1 live*. §6 says so on purpose: *A finished member its manager closed while the team runs on is told by neither rule: its lane's new work waits for the team's next wind-down.* So a team with a long-running seat (the anchor, an auditor) can hold its members' new work indefinitely, and even when it does wind down the road back is a full Start of every member and seat (or Paul's Inbox row first, under `on_work: ask`) — clumsy where one member's lane gained one entry (Paul, 2026-10-08: *restarting a full team (and waiting for a stop) seems clumsy vs just telling a member when new work arrives*).

**Decided by Paul, 2026-10-08:** the default of `on_work` becomes **`start`** (it is `ask` in §5, `agent_tick.py` and `agent_notify.py`); he switched ao-grind to `start` the same day.

**Fix:** design, in §6, (1) **restart the one member**: when a finished member's lane gains work while its team runs on, the tick replays that member's record (rule 8's replay, `why: work`, under the team's `on_work` — `start` replays it, `ask` asks with a row naming the member, `off` does nothing), so the member that owns the lane comes back alone and is told what arrived; the sentence quoted above goes; weigh it against *a restart is not a start* (§6 — a replay under the person's standing word, as rule 8's is); (2) **seats do not hold a wind-down**: whether rule 8's *wound down* should read over members only, a live seat not counting — or whether (1) makes that unnecessary; (3) the `on_work: start` default in §5, its Settings picker's *(default)* label (`settings.html`), and the code defaults (`agent_tick.py`, `agent_notify.py`, `settings.py`'s `ON_WORK`, `ui/settings_page.py`); (4) the race: whether the finished pass should first read the lane against `origin/main` (or wait a settle after the checkout's pull) before closing a member as finished. Then a build entry. **Done when** the design says what happens to a finished member's lane gaining work while a seat runs, and the build entry is open.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-12 (the anchor) — designed in #1334 (§6 rule 8 *A member that finished while its team runs on*), built by TD-466 in #1340 and #1353, and read live the same day with TD-466 (archived below): ao-grind's members were started member by member on new work.

## TD-055: Rename to the glossary's decided words — `lead`, `director`, the `control` grant, `round`, and the retired synonyms

**Priority:** Medium
**Added:** 2026-09-16 (raised by Paul)
**Owner:** paul
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Partly done — the words were decided 2026-09-16 and recorded in `docs/glossary.md` (widened the same day after a Fable review of the whole vocabulary). **Step 1 landed 2026-09-17** (docs and briefs, text only): live `docs/design.md`, `docs/briefs/`, `src/shiftlead/briefs/*.md` and `src/shiftlead/skill.md` say *lead*, *director* (`docs/briefs/orc-of-orcs.md` → `director.md`), *the host agent*, a lead's *round*, *send*, *policies*/*lead* and *org*/*command session*. Deliberately left for steps 2 and 3, because they are code values the text must keep matching until the code changes: the role value `orchestrator` (`role: orchestrator`, `briefs/orchestrator.md`), the grant `orchestrate`, and `<orc>` in `ao control <orc>` and the card's *under `<orc>`* chip. Also left as written: the UI label **show command runs** (a code string; the §4.5a row must match the control), live session and brief names (step 4), the historical `tdgrind` supervisor script, `nudge_user_attention.py`, prior-art product descriptions in §3, and every dated record (§10, `docs/decisions/`, the archive). **Step 2 landed 2026-09-17**: the preset is `lead` (`repoconfig.PRESETS`, `agentorc/briefs/lead.md`, `org.DEFAULT_LEAD_ROLE`), and `repoconfig.ROLE_ALIASES` keeps `orchestrator` resolving for one release — as `--role`, a team's `role:`, and a `roles:` key in either config layer — with one stderr line per process; a team start records the new name even from an old definition. Design §4.5a/§4.8/§4.9/§4.9a/§5 and the glossary say `lead`; source comments that used *orchestrator* for the position were reworded. Paul's live `~/.agentorc/org.yml` still says `role: orchestrator` and a `roles: orchestrator:` overlay: it keeps working through the alias and prints the line — renaming those keys is his (board). **Step 3 landed 2026-09-17**: the grant is `control` (`models.GRANTS`), with `models.GRANT_ALIASES` reading `orchestrate` for one release — a stored record is normalised on load and rewritten (the host agent logs it), `set_grants` / `create` accept it, `--grant` and `ao grant`/`ao revoke` accept it and print a line, and a `grants:` in `.agentorc.yml` or an `org.yml` team says so once; the gate and the UI check `has_control`, which reads either name, so a UI or CLI newer than the running host agent still recognises its records. `ao control <controller> add|remove`, the card's *under `<controller>`* chip, the no-controller hint, the UI's Grants checkbox and notes, design (§4.5a, §4.7, §4.8, §4.9, §4.10, §5, §9), the skill file and every brief say `control`. **Skew, until the host agent restarts:** a `control` sent by the new client is refused by an agent still running the old code (`unknown grant control`) — `ao team start` of a team with a lead, `ao new --role lead`, `ao grant … control`; restart the host agent before those (board). Step 4 (live session and brief names) is Paul's and not done. ~~**What remains after the alias release:** delete `ROLE_ALIASES` and `GRANT_ALIASES` and their tests.~~ **Done by TD-107 (2026-09-22, PRs #440 and #442)**, which removed the aliases outright rather than after a release — so the *done when* below that asks old words to keep working with a deprecation line is superseded: they are unknown words now (design §4.8 *Role names*). Step 4 is done for the teams that run (TD-076 step 4a, 2026-09-20); **what is left of this entry is the one brief never launched, `docs/briefs/guardians-orchestrator.md`** — its name and its words (it still says *lead* for the manager), Paul's to change when the guardians team is first stood up. **The mockups were renamed 2026-09-20** with TD-074's step 6 redraw: the artboards say `lead` and `control`, in the role badges, the Focus headers and the notes. The session *names* they show (`orchestrator-ao-1`) are step 4's and stay as they are. **Next:** what is left is `docs/briefs/guardians-orchestrator.md`, Paul's when that team stands up.

**Location:** `src/shiftlead/repoconfig.py` (the built-in `orchestrator` role, the commented example), `src/shiftlead/org.py` (`DEFAULT_LEAD_ROLE = "orchestrator"` and its example), `src/shiftlead/briefs/orchestrator.md`, `src/shiftlead/teamrun.py`, `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao control`'s positional `orc` and its help text, the `<orc>` in `cmd_control`'s docstring and in the no-controller hint at `cli.py:478`, `--grant`), `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`GRANTS`) and `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_set_grants`, `_gate`), `src/shiftlead/skill.md`, `src/shiftlead/ui/` (the Grants checkbox, the "under `<orc>`" wording, any user-facing "orchestrator"), `tests/`, `docs/design.md` (every live use — not §10 or other dated history), `docs/briefs/`, `CLAUDE.md`

**Why:** "orchestrator" meant a team lead in about 200 places while the top coordinator was "orc-of-orcs"; bare "the agent" meant the host daemon in about 70 places of a design whose ADR calls an AI session an *agent*; *tick* meant both the host agent's loop (in code) and a lead's loop (in briefs); and *nudge*, *supervisor* and *fleet* each gave one thing a second name. Paul, 2026-09-16: *"having the names nailed down will reduce confusion"* and *"make the names as intuitive as possible, and keep a single genre when appropriate."* The glossary's rule: organisation words are workplace words, mechanism words are plain and tool-native, no third genre (doorbell the named exception).

**Fix, in order — each its own PR:**

1. **Docs and briefs** (text only). In `docs/design.md` live text, `docs/briefs/`, `src/shiftlead/briefs/*.md`, `src/shiftlead/skill.md` and `CLAUDE.md`: *orchestrator* as a position → *lead*; *orc-of-orcs* → *director* (`docs/briefs/orc-of-orcs.md` → `director.md`); bare *the agent* for the daemon → *the host agent*; a lead's *tick* → *round*, while the host agent's stays *tick* (including §4.10's "the agent's next pass" → "the host agent's next tick"); *nudge* → *send*; *supervisor* → *lead*, or *policies* where §6's mechanism is meant (the historical "tdgrind supervisor" script keeps its name); *fleet* → *org* or "every live session"; *command run* as a noun → *command session*; "run N" never written; the lead brief's "your reach is your members" → "your members are …"; §5's `name: orc` example → `name: lead`. Dated history (§10 entries, `docs/decisions/`, the archive, old board lines) is left as written. **Already done 2026-09-16:** §4.10, the §4.5a mail rows, invariants 5, 11 and 13 (invariant 9 checked and needed nothing), and TD-052 (the mail design worked on that day).
2. **The role preset.** `orchestrator` → `lead` in `repoconfig.py`'s built-ins, the brief template file, tests, and any `.agentorc.yml` or team definition that names `role: orchestrator`. Accept `orchestrator` as a deprecated alias for one release, printing a line that names the new word.
3. **The grant.** `orchestrate` → `control` in the grant list, the gate's check, `--grant`, role `grants:`, the UI checkbox and `ao --skill`. Records and configs already carrying `orchestrate` are read as `control` for one release (normalised on load, so the record is rewritten with the new value), with a deprecation line. CLI help and hints stop using `<orc>`: `ao control <controller> add|remove …`.
4. **Live session and brief names** (`orchestrator-ao-1`, `guardians-orchestrator`) — Paul's call, since renaming a live session changes what its members' `controllers` name; do it at the next planned restart, not mid-run.

**Not in scope:** record field names (`controllers`, `capabilities`, `role`, `lane`, …), state names, `ao` verbs, package and command names, and code variable names such as `fleet` — the glossary keeps all of them deliberately.

**Done when** no live text in `docs/design.md`, `src/` or the briefs uses *orchestrator* for a position, bare *agent* for the daemon, *tick* for a lead's loop, or *nudge*/*supervisor*/*fleet* in prose; `ao new --role lead` and `ao grant <id> control` work; and `--role orchestrator`, `orchestrate` in a config and `orchestrate` on an existing record still work with their deprecation line.

**Related:** `docs/glossary.md`; ADR `docs/decisions/2026-09-13-org-teams-projects.md` (the Org/Team/Project/Role vocabulary this extends); design §4.8 (role presets, grants, *Orc-of-orcs is not a special case*), §4.9 (team definitions), §6 (policies), §9 invariants 1, 9 and 11.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-09 (an anchor-side session, at Paul's request; landed 2026-10-12 by the anchor, PR #1388) — what was left, `docs/briefs/guardians-orchestrator.md`, was retired unlaunched to `docs/briefs/archive/`; guardians' team is stood up from guardians-devenv (`docs/briefs/team-setup.md`, its TD-028) in the manager / techlead / member shape, so no old word remains to rename.

## TD-624: §4.4's *red* and *holds* definitions are narrower than the code's: five failed conclusions and a commit status's `FAILURE`/`ERROR` read red, and a superseded record holds nothing (TD-618)

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-13 (docs-audit-ao-1, the auditor, covering #1619–#1628)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done 2026-10-13 (grinder-ao-1) — both sentences of §4.4 say what the code tests, `fold_checks`' docstring and TD-618's step 1 match, the history carries the line. Was: Open.
**Location:** `docs/design/4.4-host-agent.md` *Repo facts* (the `checks` sentence, ~L35) and *A red PR nobody holds is a work order* (*A live record holds it*, ~L421); `src/sessionorc/reports.py` `RED_CONCLUSIONS` and `RED_STATES`; `src/sessionorc/workorders.py` `holds_pr`

**Why:** the design says what the code does not stop at, in two places, and #1620's body names the first as "left for a design touch" without a ledger line.
- *Red.* §4.4 *Repo facts*: `checks` is "*red* when any check concluded failed, cancelled or timed out". `reports.py` has `RED_CONCLUSIONS = frozenset({"FAILURE", "CANCELLED", "TIMED_OUT", "ACTION_REQUIRED", "STARTUP_FAILURE"})` and `RED_STATES = frozenset({"FAILURE", "ERROR"})` for a commit status's words; `fold_checks`' docstring repeats the design's three, and TD-618's *Fix* step 1 names four (`ACTION_REQUIRED`, no `STARTUP_FAILURE`). So a PR whose check needs an approval, or whose runner never started, becomes a `pr:<n>` order after `ORPHAN_AFTER`, which no line of the design says.
- *Holds.* §4.4: a live record holds a PR "when it is not `exited` or `closed`, carries no `out_of_work`, and either…". `holds_pr` (#1620) also returns False for `record.superseded_by`. A superseded session's claim on a red PR therefore does not keep it off the list, which the design does not state.

Both are behaviours the PR built and the design left unwritten; neither is a bug as far as the code goes, the design is the side that is short. (`probe`: `grep -n "ACTION_REQUIRED\|STARTUP_FAILURE\|superseded" docs/design/4.4-host-agent.md` has no hit in the PR-reading paragraphs.)

**Fix:** in the same two places, say it in the present tense: *red* also on `ACTION_REQUIRED` and `STARTUP_FAILURE` and a commit status's `FAILURE`/`ERROR` (and correct `fold_checks`' docstring and TD-618's step 1 to match), and a superseded record holds nothing; one dated line in `docs/design-history.md` under §4.4 naming TD-618 slices 1–2 (#1617, #1620). Run the doc-bound tests before pushing.

**Done when** §4.4's two sentences name what `RED_CONCLUSIONS`, `RED_STATES` and `holds_pr` test, and the history carries the line.

**Related:** TD-618 (the build), TD-613 (the design), #1617, #1620.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (PR #1634) — §4.4 *Repo facts* names `checks`' red as a check run's `FAILURE`, `CANCELLED`, `TIMED_OUT`, `ACTION_REQUIRED` or `STARTUP_FAILURE` or a commit status's `FAILURE`/`ERROR` (`reports.RED_CONCLUSIONS`, `RED_STATES`); *A live record holds it* says a superseded record holds nothing (`workorders.holds_pr`). `fold_checks`' docstring and TD-618's Fix step 1 say the same. The dated line is under §4.4 of `docs/design-history.md`. On the way: the ledger's tail carried two unclosed `<!-- Entry template:` fragments left by rebase resolutions (the template itself sits under the summary table); removed.

## TD-615: Build TD-614 (1): the boards are the host agent's reading — `boards` on the repo reading, `BOARD_EVERY`, at once after a write-back, work orders derived from it; the UI and `ao` read it and run no reader

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-614's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done (grinder-ao-2, 2026-10-13): slice 1 (#1624, grinder-ao-1) the host agent's half; slice 2 (#1633) the readers' — the UI, `ao repo` and `ao board show` read `boards` and run no reader. Was: Slice 1 of 2 (grinder-ao-1, 2026-10-12): fix steps 1–3 and their tests, the host agent's half (`src/sessionorc/**`) — `boards` on the repo reading (`workorders.read_boards`, each item with its `key`), `BOARD_EVERY` reading a board only when its file or the day moved and the ledger left unread on that pass, the `REPOS_EVERY` pass fetching, `_reread_board` after every write-back reading the write-back's tree as origin's board, the work orders `workorders.orders` over it. Left: slice 2, steps 4–5 and their tests (`src/shiftlead/**`: `read_boards`, `board_argv`, `BOARD_TTL`, `_board_due` go; the Inbox, `ao repo`, `ao inbox` and `ao board show` read `boards` — each item's `key` is the id the row now derives with `workorders.ref`). Was: Open.
**Location:** design §4.4 *Each reading has one owner* (*The boards*), §4.5 screen 6 (board items), §4.7 `ao board show`; `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (the repo reading ~L2895–2910: `workorders.read` every `REPOS_EVERY` — becomes the board read, kept as `boards`, with the orders derived), `src/sessionorc/workorders.py` (`read` ~L112: return every item, the orders a filter over them), `src/sessionorc/agent_common.py` (`REPOS_EVERY` ~L269: add `BOARD_EVERY = 60.0`), `src/sessionorc/agent_inbox.py` (after a write-back, ~L786: re-read that repo's board at once and push `repos`), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`read_boards` ~L372 and its cache ~L819–840 go: the Inbox reads `boards` from the `repos` reading), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (`board_argv` ~L644 and `BOARD_TTL` ~L496 go; the origin note derived from the reading's fields), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`_board_due` ~L1494, called ~L1697 for `ao repo`, which runs the repo's reader `--due-only` — goes; `ao repo`, `ao inbox` and `ao board show` read `boards`); `tests/test_workorders.py`, `tests/test_ui_inbox*.py`, `tests/test_agent*.py`

**Why:** TD-614: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *should we have the host agent run it and maintain counts somewhere to reduce burden even further? are there other centralizations we should make as well?*; the board was read on three clocks by three processes, the counts rendered per page every 20 s, the card views per client. This slice is the board: the host agent's reader every `REPOS_EVERY`, the UI's every `BOARD_TTL`, and `ao`'s own, three runs of one file.

**Fix:**
1. The repo reading gains `boards`: the board reader's items (every open item with line, `board:<key>`, due, answers, decided, refs, session, detail block, the checkout's and origin's, and the origin-note facts the Inbox draws today), read every `BOARD_EVERY` (60 s) without a fetch and with one on the `REPOS_EVERY` pass; a failed read keeps the last good items with `error` and `failed_at`.

3. A write-back (Snooze, Done, Decide, Reply, the add) re-reads that repo's board at once and pushes `repos`.
4. The UI reads `boards` from the `repos` RPC and the `repos` events it already takes; `read_boards`, its cache, `board_argv` and `BOARD_TTL` go; the Inbox, the Due strip and the Repo page draw from it unchanged.

## TD-625: The Pull requests card's month counts stop at 1000: GitHub's search returns at most 1000 results, so a month of ~1500 PRs reads *999* or *1000+*

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-13 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/reports.py` (`pr_reading`, its second `_gh_prs` read and `truncated`),
`src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (the facet's `prs`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/team_summary.html` (the
*closed* block's `+`), design §4.4 *Repo facts* (**Pull requests**).

**Why:** Paul (2026-10-13): *the count for PRs in the Pull Requests card seems to top out at 999 or
1000+ — fix it to show the actual counts.* The windows come from one `gh pr list --state all --search
updated:>=<a month ago> --limit 1000` read, and `gh pr list --search` goes through GitHub's search,
which returns at most 1000 results whatever the limit: on 2026-10-13 that read gave 1000 PRs while
GitHub counts 1533 (`search(query: "repo:… is:pr updated:>=2026-09-13") { issueCount }`). So the
month's *opened* and *closed* are a floor drawn as a number (with a `+` on *closed* alone), raising
`limit` changes nothing, and the 7-day window is complete only because the read is newest-first.
`recent` — the month's PRs that the Repo page and TD-608's *completed* join by number — is cut the
same way.

**Fix:** take the counts from GitHub's own totals, not from a list's length: per window, one GraphQL
`search(type: ISSUE) { issueCount }` for `is:pr created:>=<start>` and one for `is:pr closed:>=<start>`
(a merge is a close) — six small queries per remote, on the same five-minute read; the qualifiers
take a timestamp, so the windows stay rolling. Keep the list for `recent`, and where it must be
whole, read it in date slices each under 1000 (or say in the reading that `recent` is the newest
1000). Drop `truncated` and the `+` once the counts are totals, and change §4.4's sentence in the
same PR. **Done when** the card's month reads the number `issueCount` gives, and a test feeds a
month of more than 1000 PRs and gets its count.

**Related:** TD-176 (the two reads), TD-608 (*completed* joins `recent`), TD-611 (the PR count in the polls).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (PR #1637) — `reports._gh_counts` reads the six window counts as GitHub's `issueCount` in one `gh api graphql` request; a count that could not be read is the reading's `error`; the month's list stays for `recent`, which says `recent_cut` when it fills its 1000; `truncated` and the facet's `+` are gone; §4.4 *Repo facts* says so. `tests/test_repo_facts.py::test_a_month_past_the_search_cap_counts_every_pr_and_says_recent_is_cut` feeds 1500.

## TD-626: The host agent's board read after a stopped fetch carries no *fetch skipped* note, so the Inbox draws no *origin could not be reached*

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-13 (grinder-ao-2, found building TD-615 slice 2)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/workorders.py` `read_boards` (the `--fetch` run at `FETCH_TIMEOUT`, then the plain `_report`); design §4.5 screen 6 *Boards are read against origin* (the *unreached* note)

**Why:** until TD-615 the UI's own read marked each board of the plain read that followed a stopped or failed fetching run with `fetch_note` *fetch skipped (<why>)*, so the row carried the note *origin could not be reached (…): showing the checkout's board as of its last pull*. The host agent's `read_boards` falls back to the plain read the same way but leaves `fetch_note` as the plain read gives it (none), so a dead remote past our 45 s bound is drawn as if the board matched origin. The reader's own bound on its fetch still says *fetch skipped*; only ours is silent.

**Fix:** in `read_boards`, when the `--fetch` run gave no report and the plain one did, set each board's `source` to None and `fetch_note` to `fetch skipped (<why>)` — *timeout* for our bound, else the run's failure in words — as the UI's `read_boards` did; a test that a stopped fetching run's boards carry it and that `ui.inbox.origin_note` draws *origin could not be reached* from them.

**Done when** a fetching read stopped at its bound yields boards whose rows draw the *unreached* note, and the test above passes.

**Related:** TD-615 (where the UI's own read went), TD-221 (the origin notes).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (PR #1644) — `workorders._report` says why a run gave no report (*timeout* for our bound, else the exit and stderr's last line), and `read_boards` marks the plain read after a stopped or failed fetching run `source: None`, `fetch_note: fetch skipped (<why>)`; `tests/test_workorders.py::test_a_stopped_fetching_read_marks_the_plain_reads_boards_unreached` draws *origin could not be reached* through `ui.inbox.origin_note`.

## TD-632: §4.5a's Git card *changed files* keeps a deletion as text by its code `D`, but `GitInfo.files` also carries `MD` and `AD` for a file deleted from the worktree (TD-627)

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-13 (docs-audit-ao-1, the auditor, covering #1629–#1639)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `docs/design/4.5a-controls.md` *Focus side panel, Git card: changed files* (what is not a file stays text); `docs/technical_debt.md` TD-628 Fix step 2; `src/sessionorc/gitinfo.py` `git_info` (`1 XY …` lines, `parts[1].replace('.', '')`)

**Why:** #1636 designed that a link is drawn for each path but "**a deletion (`D`)**", "since there is nothing to open", and TD-628's step 2 says "Text, with a hover, for a `D` line". `git_info` keeps the porcelain's two letters with the dots removed, so a file deleted in the worktree after an index change is not `D`. Probe, a scratch repo with `a` and `d` staged-modified/added and then removed from the tree, and `b` removed with `git rm`: `git_info(dir).files` is `['MD a', 'D b', 'AD d']` (`git status --short`: `MD a`, `D  b`, `AD d`). Two of the three are deletions with nothing to open, and a builder who reads the design's letter as the code (`code == "D"`) draws `a` and `d` as links to a path that is not there; one who reads it as "a `D` in the code" has to find that out from the porcelain, since the design names neither `MD`, `AD` nor `RD` (a rename deleted afterwards, which `2 RD …` carries with its new path).

**Fix:** decide and say it in §4.5a's present tense: a path is text when the worktree side of its code is a deletion (a `D` anywhere in the code, or the file is absent), as a rule the build can test with `MD`, `AD`, `RD` and `D`; amend TD-628's step 2 and test list to match. The design only.

**Done when** the row says which codes are a deletion and the TD-628 test list names `MD` and `AD`.

**Related:** TD-627 (the design), TD-628 (the build), #1636.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (the designer, PR #1648) — §4.5a *Focus side panel, Git card: changed files* says a deletion is a code whose last letter is `D` (`D`, `MD`, `AD`, `RD`), a file deleted and made again listing as `D` and `??`; TD-628's step 2 and tests name them.

## TD-629: A permission answered in the terminal comes back as *needs you* when the hook's wait runs out: the timeout re-raises a pending the session has already moved past

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-13 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-entry-4)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_hook.py` (`HookMixin._await_permission`, its `except TimeoutError`),
`src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_apply_event`, `_permission_waiting`), `src/shiftlead/adapters/claude_code/hook.py`
(`translate`'s `PermissionRequest` branch, `describe_tool_input`); design §4.2 *Permissions are answered
through the hook, not through keystrokes*.

**Why:** Paul (2026-10-13): *we seem to be in a bad state with our "needs you". I answered a question
in the terminal (for dc-paul) but shiftlead does not seem to handle that properly* — screenshots
`~/.shiftlead/attachments/ao-shiftlead-entry-4/paste-20261013-091136.png` (the Org: dc-paul *NEEDS
YOU*, the team's *Answer needed (1)* and the Org's *1 needs you*) and `paste-20261013-091200.png`
(dc-paul's Focus: the turn done at 9:01, the composer empty, the header still *NEEDS YOU*). dc-paul's
transcript and record tell it: its `AskUserQuestion` went out at 14:56:25Z and reached the
`PermissionRequest` hook, so the host agent's `_await_permission` began its 600 s wait; Paul answered
in the terminal seconds later, the session ran on and stopped at 15:01:13Z; at 15:06:26Z — the
question's time plus 600 s, the record's `since` — the waiter timed out and its `except TimeoutError`
set `needs-you` with a `question` pending **unconditionally**, over the record's later `idle`. Nothing
that happened in between ends the waiter: a later hook event clears the record's pending but leaves the
future live, so `_permission_waiting` stays true for the full ten minutes. The harm: every permission
or question answered in the terminal, the road §4.2 promises works beside the buttons, rings again ten
minutes later as a false *needs you* — on the card, the team's *Answer needed*, the Org's count, and
the Telegram notice — and it stays up until the session's next hook event, so the person learns to
doubt the one state that means *you*. A second fault rides on it: an `AskUserQuestion` that reaches
`PermissionRequest` is drawn by `describe_tool_input`'s JSON fallback, *AskUserQuestion: {"questions":
[{"question": …*, where the `PreToolUse` road draws the question's text.

**Fix:** a later hook event of the same session ends its waiter: a tool event, a `Stop`, a
`UserPromptSubmit` or a `SessionEnd` arriving while a waiter is live resolves it as answered in the
terminal (the trail's word, `_ended_by`), and the timeout sets the terminal's `question` only when the
record's pending is still that waiter's (`tool_use_id`). `describe_tool_input` draws an
`AskUserQuestion` by its first question's text, as `translate`'s `PreToolUse` branch does. §4.2's
paragraph says what a terminal answer ends, in the same PR. **Done when** a test answers a permission
by a later `PostToolUse` and `Stop` and, past the wait, the record reads `idle` with no pending and
the trail *answered in the terminal*; a test times out a permission nobody answered and still gets
the `question`; and an `AskUserQuestion` permission's pending text is its question.

**Related:** TD-201 (a subagent's tool no longer clears `needs-you`), TD-088 and TD-308 (`_ended_by`'s
words), TD-079 (the attention trail).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (PR #1664) — a later hook event ends a live permission waiter as answered in the terminal: the asked call's tool event (`tool_use_id` on Claude Code's tool events), or one naming no call (`Stop`, a prompt, `SessionEnd`); a parallel tool's event ends nothing and the buttons stay up; the timeout sets the terminal's question only while the record's pending is still that waiter's; an `AskUserQuestion` permission reads as its first question. §4.2 *Permissions are answered through the hook* says it.

## TD-617: Build TD-614 (3): per-session views once per delta fanned out to every stream; PR marks once per repo on the `repos` push; Focus's members from its stream (TD-611 slices 3–4 in this form)

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (the designer, TD-614's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1660
**Status:** Built — slice 1 (#1645, the one subscriber and `fan_step`), slice 2 (#1651, PR marks per repo on `repos` and Focus's first load; no session view carries `pr_marks`), slice 3 (#1660, 2026-10-13, grinder-ao-2: `fan_kin` sends a Focus page its own record's delta when one of its controllers or members moves or goes; app.js reads no `/api/sessions`). Left: the live check, once #1660 is live (`ao promote status`): read `shiftlead-ui`'s CPU (`systemctl --user status shiftlead-ui` / `ps -o %cpu`) with several pages open against the figures before TD-614, and count `/api/sessions` GETs in `journalctl --user -u shiftlead-ui` over an hour with a Focus page open — none from Focus. It holds → archive with `**Resolved:**`.
**Location:** design §4.4 *Each reading has one owner* (*Per-session views*), §4.5 *Live state*; `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`events` ~L3381–3570: one fan-out per delta — `view()`, `compact_in`, `render_card` and `fresh_heads` computed once and handed to every connected stream, the light streams taking their parts; `api_sessions` ~L2359), `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`pr_marks` ~L327: out of the session view, into a per-repo map sent on load and with `repos`), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (cards look PRs up by repo; Focus's `refreshMembership` ~L4370 reads its stream's fleet, no `/api/sessions`); `tests/test_ui_events*.py`, `tests/test_ui_focus*.py`

**Why:** TD-614: Paul, 2026-10-12 — *should we have the host agent run it and maintain counts somewhere to reduce burden even further? are there other centralizations we should make as well?*; the board was read on three clocks by three processes, the counts rendered per page every 20 s, the card views per client. This slice is the views: every delta was rendered once per connected tab, and each session view repeated its repo's PRs.

**Fix:**
1. The stream: a single subscriber to the host agent computes, per delta, the session's view, its compact form, its rendered card and (when shaping) the heads, once, and fans the result to every connected client queue; a light stream takes `{id, state}` or its own session's whole delta from the same result.
2. PR marks: a per-repo map `{repo: {number: mark}}` on the page's first load and on each `repos` push; the session view drops `pr_marks`; a card resolves its PRs from its repo's map.
3. Focus: members from the `focus=` stream's fleet; no `/api/sessions` on a peer's delta.
4. Tests: with three connected streams one delta runs `view()` once (a counter); the session view carries no `pr_marks` and the page's map does; Focus issues no `/api/sessions` on a peer's delta; the Org's cards render as before.

**Done when** a delta is computed once however many pages are connected, no session view carries PR marks, Focus reads no `/api/sessions`, the UI's CPU falls with the number of tabs no longer multiplying it, and the tests above pass; a re-measurement of `shiftlead-ui`'s CPU and `/api/sessions` requests per hour after the promote is the live check.

**Related:** TD-614 (the design), TD-611 (its slices 3 and 4, built here), TD-572.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (grinder-ao-2; the live check of #1660) — it holds. #1660 (`7796087`) went live at 18:52 MDT and the UI restarted at 19:18 and again at 19:50 (`abbaddd`). Read from `journalctl --user -u shiftlead-ui` 18:52–19:53, with four Focus pages and the Org page open throughout: no `GET /api/sessions` at all (a Focus page's only reads its own `/api/sessions/<id>/inbox`, 3 each, one per load), where 17:00–18:52 under the build before it logged 538. `shiftlead-ui`'s CPU (`ps -o time`): 1 min 52 s in the first 16 min (≈12 % of a core) with those five pages, and 11 s in the 3 min after the 19:50 restart (≈6 %), where TD-611 measured a full core (888 s in 20 min) with three Focus tabs; the tabs no longer multiply it.

## TD-639: Build TD-637: `done … --pr` reads the PR's required checks at the declaration — refused on a failure, *checks pending* while running; the repo reading keeps each base branch's required set

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-13 (the designer, TD-637's round)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.8 *A `done` with a PR is told what its checks read*, §4.7, §6 rule 10; `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_progress` ~L2485: on `status == "done"` with `pr`, the read and the verdict before anything is written; `--slice` too), `src/sessionorc/reports.py` (the repo reading: `required: {<base>: [names]}` from `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/branches/<base>/protection/required_status_checks` and `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/rules/branches/<base>` — the `required_status_checks` rules — on `REPOS_EVERY`; a read that fails keeps the last), `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`ProgressEntry`: `ci: str` — `pending` / `unknown`; not `checks`, which rule 10's record field and the PR reading already use), `src/sessionorc/cadence.py` (rule 10: a `ci: pending` entry read on its cadence like any `done`, its read at the head clearing `ci`), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (the refusal printed as the agent words it; the reply's *checks unknown*, *closed unmerged*, non-required names), the card's report line (`src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py`: *done · checks pending*); `tests/test_progress*.py` or `tests/test_agent*.py`, `tests/test_reports.py`, `tests/test_cadence*.py`

**Why:** TD-637: Paul, 2026-10-13 — *an agent should not say its done if its PR is not green*; a `done` is accepted today and checked afterwards, on rule 10's cadence.

**Fix:**
1. The required set: on the repo reading's `REPOS_EVERY` pass, per base branch the open PRs name, the union of the protection's required contexts and the rulesets' `required_status_checks` (`parameters.required_status_checks[].context`); a protection 404 (*Branch not protected*) is none from it, an empty list when the rulesets require none too; a 403 or other failure keeps the last with its error; a base never read is absent.
2. The declaration: `done` with `pr` reads `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergedAt,headRefOid,baseRefName,statusCheckRollup` from the record's repo root, in a thread (`asyncio.to_thread`), bounded by `GH_TIMEOUT`; merged → accept; a required check red by `reports.fold_checks`'s rule (`RED_CONCLUSIONS` for a run, `RED_STATES` for a status), a required name matched on a run's `name` or a status's `context` (with none required, any run; with the base's set never read, any run and *required set unknown* in the reply) → refuse with *PR #<n>'s required checks failed on <sha7>: <names> — fix them and report done again*, nothing written; one not completed → accept with `ci: pending`; else accept; a read that fails, times out or finds no `gh` → accept with `ci: unknown` and the why in the reply; non-required failures named in the reply; closed unmerged → accept, said. `--slice` on a PR that is not merged → refused, *a slice is a merged PR — #<n> is open* (`_slice` ~L2540 checks nothing today).
3. Rule 10: reads a `ci: pending` entry as any `done`; its read at that head clears `ci`; a later failure is its first *fail*, told as today.
4. The card's report line: *done · checks pending* while the entry carries `ci: pending`.
5. Tests: a failed required check refuses and writes nothing — a run's `FAILURE` and `STARTUP_FAILURE`, a status's `FAILURE` and `ERROR`; a failed non-required one accepts and names it; pending accepts with `ci: pending`, and rule 10's read at the head clears it; merged accepts with no rollup read; no checks accepts; a `gh` failure or timeout accepts with *unknown*; a base never read takes every run; `--slice` on an open PR is refused; the required set read from protection and from rulesets, a protection 404 empty, a 403 keeping the last.

**Done when** `ao progress done <ref> --pr <n>` is refused in words while a required check of the PR's head has failed, is marked *checks pending* while one runs, is accepted merged, green or with no CI, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-637 (the design), TD-618 (the open PRs' `checks`, which can fold by the same required set), TD-640 (the cadence script's row), docs/decisions/2026-10-13-hermes-agent.md.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-13 (PR #1670) — `done … --pr` reads the PR's checks at the declaration (`reports.pr_view`, `reports.at_done`) against its base's required set: refused naming the failed required checks and the head, `ci: pending` while one runs (the report line's *· checks pending*, cleared by rule 10's read at the head), `ci: unknown` on a read the home could not make, non-required failures named; `--slice` refused on a PR not merged; the PR reading keeps `base`, `required` and `required_error`.
