**Why:** the Inbox already lists every entry that waits on the person (`Owner: paul`, or blocked by `decision (paul)`) under *Later*, with its answers, **Reply** and **Open**, but an entry the person means to work themselves has no way in from there: they go to the Org, find the repo's team, open the + card's form, and type the name, lane and prompt. Paul, 2026-10-14: *it allows the user to work out of the inbox instead of having to jump around*. Today six entries are `Owner: paul` in this repo alone (`ledger.py --list --owner paul`).

**Fix:** a **Start session** button on the ledger row (not a separate *Your TDs* list: the row and its source exist). One press, a form only on doubt, as **Resume** is: an interactive session (the person's, `unattended: false`) on the repo's servicing team (the row's team badge), in a new worktree named for the entry (`td-676`), lane the id, its opening prompt naming the entry; then its Focus opens. When it cannot be silent — no team, a live holder of the name, a host not connected — the press lands on the New session form filled in, with the reason. While a live record holds the entry (the row's *held by <name>*), the button reads **Open session** and focuses that one. The design round settles the opening prompt's words, whether a `decision (paul)` row gets the button too, and the name's form.

**Done when** a press on a ledger row in the Inbox starts the person's session on that entry, on its team, named for it, and opens its Focus, or opens the filled form saying why not; and a second press while that session lives opens it instead of starting another.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (the designer) — designed 2026-10-14 (§4.5a *Inbox row: ledger entry: Start session / Open session*, §4.5 screen 6), built by TD-678 (#1751), archived.

**Related:** TD-367 and TD-560 (the rows), TD-565 (drawn as full rows in *Later*).

## TD-622: #1563's `AO.shellHere` — the *tab* wording of the blocked-pop-up toast, the close on a create that answers without an id, and the placeholder's directory fallback — are held by no test

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-12 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1563)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`AO.shellHere`), `tests/test_ui_popout.py` (`SHELL_PROBE`, `test_open_shell_here_opens_beside_the_page_it_was_pressed_on`)

**Why:** #1563 (TD-579) has a node probe and a source-shape test, and its docstring says *a blocked open creates nothing and says so* and that the placeholder *reads "opening a shell in <dir>…"*. Probe: each change below, one at a time, then `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src pytest -q tests/test_ui_popout.py`: every one still passes (7 passed).
- `const what = asWindow ? "window" : "tab";` → `const what = "window";`: the probe blocks only the window form (`AO.shellHere("a", "/repo/x", true)`), so a blocked *tab* — the plain press, the common one — saying *the browser blocked the window* is read by no test.
- `if (!res || !res.id) { …w.close()…; return res; }` removed: a create that answers without an `id` leaves the placeholder tab open at *opening a shell in …* for good; the probe's `AO.act` returns an id or throws, never `{}`.
- `dir || "this session's directory"` → `dir || "x"`: the probe always passes `/repo/x`, so the fallback sentence (a card whose `data-dir` is empty) is never drawn.
The window's `w.name` assignment, by contrast, is caught.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1754) — `SHELL_PROBE` blocks a plain-press tab (the toast names *the tab*), answers a create with `{}` (the placeholder closed, `href` untouched) and presses with an empty `dir` (the placeholder names *this session's directory*); each of the three mutations above now fails `test_open_shell_here_opens_beside_the_page_it_was_pressed_on`.

**Fix:** extend `SHELL_PROBE`: a blocked open with `asWindow` false (the toast names the tab, nothing created), an `AO.act` that answers `{}` (the placeholder closed, no `href` set), and a press with an empty `dir` (the placeholder names the session's directory). **Done when** each probe above fails a test.

**Related:** TD-577, TD-579 (#1563).

## TD-679: Ready to close has no row for the agent itself: a working session's checklist reads all ✓, and the card's *more ▾* **Close** is enabled on it

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.2 (the `ready_when` checklist), §4.5a *card: Close session*, *Focus header: Close session* and *more ▾*, *Focus side panel* (the Ready to close card); `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`ready_to_close`, `ready_ok`, `not_ready`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/card.html` (*more ▾*'s **Close**), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/focus.html` and `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the side panel's `#checks`, `readyNow`, `ready`), `src/shiftlead/repoconfig.py` (`DEFAULT_READY_WHEN`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-14: *Ready to Close on Focus sessions should also consider whether the agent is currently working. A session with the agent mid-work is not ready to close.* The checklist (`cards.ready_to_close`) reads only git, subagents, outcomes, mail and members, never the session's state. So the Focus side panel's Ready to close card shows every row ✓ on a session that is `working`, while its **Close session** stays disabled with no row that says why. The page hides the mark and the buttons outside `idle` and `exited` by a separate test (`readyNow` and `ready` in app.js, `state in ('idle', 'exited')` in focus.html), and that test is not one of the checks. Where that test is missing, a working session reads as ready: `ready_ok` is the checks alone, so the card's *more ▾* **Close** (card.html) is enabled on a `working`, `needs-you`, `stalled?` or `limited` session whose tree is clean and pushed. One click there kills an agent mid-turn and reaps its worktree. §4.2 says the checklist is evaluated when a session goes `idle` or `exited`, but names no check for it.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1757) — `cards.ready_to_close` reads the agent first: *agent not working* on `idle`/`exited`, else *agent working — wait or Wrap up* or *agent <state>*, so `ready_ok`/`not_ready` carry it and the card's *more ▾* **Close** is disabled with the reason; the separate `idle`/`exited` tests in `focus.html`, `app.js` (`readyNow`, the side panel's `ready`) and the card caption are gone. §4.2 gains the row. Tests: `test_ready_to_close_reads_the_agent_itself_first`, `test_focus_offers_close_only_when_the_checklist_passes`.

**Fix:** add a check for the agent's own state to the checklist, first in the list: it passes on `idle` and `exited`, and fails on any other state, naming it (*agent not working* / *agent working — wait or Wrap up*, the state's own word for `needs-you`, `stalled?`, `limited`). Then `ready_ok` and `not_ready` carry it, so the card's *more ▾* **Close** is disabled with the reason on every surface. The page's separate `state in ('idle', 'exited')` tests (focus.html, app.js `readyNow` and `ready`) become the check's own result, so there is one test. The design changes in the same PR: §4.2's list gains the row. Like the outcomes, mail and members rows it is unconditional, so it needs no name in §5's `ready_when` (which `ready_to_close` does not read today). Leave out a record with no agent, which is closed without the checks (§4.5a *A record with no agent*), and a seat, which is never *ready to close* (§4.5). Test: a `working` view with a clean, pushed tree has `ready_ok` false and the new row in `not_ready`; an `idle` one passes.

**Done when** a working session's Ready to close card shows a ✗ row saying the agent is working, and no surface (the card's *more ▾*, the Focus header, the side panel) offers Close on it as ready. The team header's *n ready to close* already counts only `idle` sessions and is unchanged.

**Related:** TD-156 (the Focus screen's Close session), TD-080 (the one pushed measure), TD-666 (a record with no agent).

## TD-683: `ao team --skill` leaves out what a repo's own session needs before its first team

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the session `ao-dc-decouple`, lessons from the ledgerboard split; Paul agreed the lesson the same day)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/team_skill.md`; its tests (`tests/test_briefs_layout.py` bars repo literals in it)

**Why:** Paul is about to have the pneuma-ops, ledgerboard and guardians-devenv sessions each stand up its repo's first team. The recipe takes them from definition to `ao team start`, and `ao doctor` already reads all three repos as ready. Four things are missing or wrong for a session doing this for the first time:
(1) No step checks the repo first. `ao doctor`'s **repos** line and `ao repo init` (TD-591) are the readiness check, and the recipe names neither.
(2) An empty ledger refuses the start. ledgerboard has 0 open entries, so a `free-pick` team there is refused (*every member's lane holds nothing to pick*), and the recipe does not say what a repo with little work should run: an on-call manager alone, or one member and `--anyway`.
(3) A public repo's `.shiftlead.yml` publishes its team definition, including profile and session names. The recipe's **Which file:** lead-in should say to keep a public repo's team in `org.yml`.
(4) The closing section is headed *For a Claude session told to do this*, though a session may be another tool's.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1760) — `team_skill.md` gains step 0b *Is the repo ready?* (`ao doctor repos`, `ao repo init`), *A repo with little or no work* after `lane:` (an on-call manager alone or one member, either started with `--anyway`, since the anchor seat's lane is read too), *A public repo's team goes in `org.yml`* in *Which file*, and the close headed *For an agent session told to do this*; `test_the_recipe_covers_a_repos_first_team` pins the four.

**Fix:** a step 0b, *Is the repo ready?*, with `ao doctor` and `ao repo init`; a sentence on a small repo's team after `lane:`; the public-repo sentence in *Which file*; the heading made tool-neutral.

**Done when** `ao team --skill` prints step 0b, the small-repo sentence, the public-repo sentence and the tool-neutral heading.

**Related:** TD-591, TD-588.

## TD-684: Build TD-681 (1): a sync PR the home does not merge is the team's `pr:<n>` order at once, first in the pick order; the Inbox row where no team services the repo

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-681's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.4 *A sync PR is the team's at once, unless the home merges it*, §4.5a *Inbox row: red PR*; `src/sessionorc/reports.py` (`pr_reading`, `_gh_prs`: the sync flag and `sync_since`), `src/sessionorc/workorders.py` (`red_prs`, `pr_order`), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_red_prs`), `src/shiftlead/teamrun.py` (`pr_orders`, the pick order `ao repo` prints), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (the red PR row), `src/shiftlead/briefs/anchor.md` and `grinder.md`

**Why:** TD-681's design. On 2026-10-14 two green sync PRs sat in repos where no session ran, and ShiftLead's #1728 sat red until a session added a step by hand. The red-PR rule waits `ORPHAN_AFTER` for red PRs and never orders a green one, so nothing gave these PRs an owner.

**Fix:** in `reports.pr_reading`, a sync PR is one whose `branch` starts `cadence-sync-` and whose changed files include `docs/cadence-sync.lock`. The files are read only for a candidate branch, once per head, whole (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls/<n>/files --paginate`, never `gh pr view --json files`, which is capped), and the flag is kept on the row as `sync: true`. The row also carries `isCrossRepository` as `fork` and, for a sync PR, **`sync_since`**: the first reading that saw it open, kept from `old` as `red_since` is. In `sessionorc.workorders`, an unheld sync PR is a `pr_order` marked `sync: true` from the first reading that sees it, with no `ORPHAN_AFTER`, whatever `checks` says except *pending*. Until TD-685 lands no PR is merged at the home, so the order's `Context` is the URL plus the failing checks, *conflicting*, *draft*, or *green: review and merge it*. The holders' test and the lanes stay as for a red PR. The idle holder's told-once note and its passing-over after a second `ORPHAN_AFTER` key on `sync_since` in place of `red_since`. `ao repo`'s pick order lists sync orders before every entry and every other order. The *Inbox row: red PR* takes a sync PR in a repo no team services at once, green or red, with the reason in its line, and it leaves when the PR merges, closes or is held. The anchor's and grinder's briefs each gain one sentence: *a `pr:<n>` order marked sync is taken before the lane's entries: read its reason, fix it on the PR's branch if it needs a step, review it as any PR of yours, merge it at the gate.* The anchor brief also names `pr:<n>` orders where it lists the lane word's work orders. This is `src/sessionorc/**`, so the techlead reads it (§4.9b).

**Done when** an open `cadence-sync-*` PR touching the lock, green or red and held by no live record, is a `pr:<n>` order marked sync on the reading that first sees it, and is first in `ao repo`'s pick order. A pending one is not an order. In a repo no team services it is the Inbox's red PR row with its reason. Both briefs carry the sentence. Tests cover the four `checks` states, held vs unheld, an idle holder of a green sync PR told and then passed over, a sync PR with more than 100 files whose lock is past the hundredth, and the pick order.

**Related:** TD-681 (the design), TD-685 (the home's merge, which narrows this order to what it does not merge), TD-613 and TD-652 (the red-PR order and its holders).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (grinder-ao-1, PR #1762) — the open PR reading marks a `cadence-sync-*` PR `sync` when `docs/cadence-sync.lock` is among its files, read whole through `gh api …/pulls/<n>/files --paginate` once per head (`sync_head`), and carries `sync_since` and `fork`. `workorders.red_prs` orders an unheld sync PR from the first reading, any `checks` but *pending*, marked `sync` with its `reason` (failing checks, *conflicting*, *draft*, else *green: review and merge it*) as its `Context`; an idle holder is told and passed over on `sync_since`. Sync orders are first in `teamrun.lane_entries` and in `ao repo` (counted as *n sync PR to land*); the Inbox's *red PR* row draws one as *`<repo>` #<n> · sync · <reason>*; the anchor's and grinder's briefs carry the sentence. Held by `tests/test_workorders.py`, `tests/test_repo_facts.py`, `tests/test_ui_red_prs.py`; the PR's UI check read the row. The home's merge stays TD-685.

## TD-689: Build TD-688 (1): every file button is a file link — `editor_file_link`, the file form with `:1` through `AO.openFile`, the checkout first where the file lies in one; a test over the templates

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-688's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.6 *A file button is a file link*, §4.5a rows *Repo page: Open ledger*, *Settings page: Open file*, *Focus header: ‹› VS Code*, *Transcript*; `src/shiftlead/ui/uiconf.py` (a new `editor_file_link` beside `editor_link` and `editor_file`), `src/shiftlead/ui/common.py` (the template global), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html`, `settings.html`, `group_head.html`, `new.html`, `transcript.html`, `focus.html`, `inbox_row.html` (**Open board**), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (the board rows' `editor`, built with `vscode_url` and `:line` today), `src/shiftlead/ui/transcript.py` (`transcript_editor`), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the `a.editor` click handler, `AO.openFile`)

**Why:** TD-688's design. Paul, 2026-10-14: **Open ledger** fails in VS Code while a pane path's link works. Every file button but the pane's is `editor_link`'s folder form with a file's path in it, so the ssh-remote form opens nothing usable. Five of the seven are not `a.editor`, so they navigate the tab.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1765) — `uiconf.editor_file_link` and `common.editor_file_link` (with `checkout_of`, the inner of nested registry checkouts) build every file button; the `file_link` macro (`templates/file_link.html`) draws Open ledger, every Open file, Open board at the item's line, the Focus header's `#ftranscript_editor` and the Transcript page's VS Code; `tests/test_ui_editor_links.py` walks the templates and renders the Repo and Settings pages under each form.

**Fix:**
- **The helper.** `uiconf.editor_file_link(path, *, local, remote, reach, folder_url, line=1)` builds the forms and answers `{label, url, folder, wait}` or None under `open_in: none`. `url` is `editor_file`'s form filled with the percent-encoded path, then `:<line>` on a `vscode` form; a template's `{line}` is filled with it. `folder` is `editor_link`'s link for the registry checkout whose real path holds the file, or None outside every checkout. `wait` is `person.file_link.wait`. The registry lookup lives in the `common.editor_file_link(path, folder=True)` global, since `uiconf` has no registry. That global finds the checkout, builds its `editor_link`, and fills the host. The transcript passes `folder=False`.
- **The helper's folder.** With `person.file_link.folder_first: false` the helper answers no `folder`, so the press is one launch. `wait` is in seconds.
- **The macro.** A `file_link(l, text, title)` macro in a shared template draws `<a class="editor {{ cls }}" data-file-link href="{{ l.url }}" data-label …>`, with `data-folder` and `data-wait` when `l.folder` is set. `cls` is the button's own classes (`btn sm ghost` where it has them), kept, since the Inbox's `o` and Enter keys find **Open board** by `a.btn` (`app.js`).
- **The templates.** `repo_part.html` (Open ledger), `settings.html` (every card's Open file), `group_head.html` (the team header's), `new.html` (`fromfile`), `transcript.html` (**VS Code**) and `inbox_row.html` (**Open board**) call the macro. For **Open board**, `inbox.py` builds the row's link with `editor_file_link(board, line=<the item's line>)` in place of `vscode_url` plus `:line`, so it opens the checkout first and lands at the item.
- **The Focus header's ‹›.** `focus.html` always draws `#ftranscript_editor` through `file_link`, with an empty `url`, the marker, `hidden`, and the person's editor label from the page (`s.editor`'s label, `editor_link`'s). The page's JS fills only `href` and `data-label` from the record's `transcript_editor`, and never sets `data-folder`. `transcript_editor` returns `editor_file_link(path, folder=False)`, so `{label, url, wait}` and no folder. The `or s.editor` fallback goes, so the button is never the folder form. TD-657's two **Open file** buttons use it when they are built (the Director card's by TD-662, the *preferences proposed* row's by TD-663).
- **The press.** The existing `a.editor` handler sends two launches with `data-folder` and one without, so `app.js` needs no change beyond the Focus header's fill.
- **The test.** `tests/test_ui_editor_links.py` walks `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/*.html`. It fails on any control whose text is **Open file**, **Open ledger** or **Open board**, or that is `#ftranscript_editor` or the Transcript page's **VS Code**, unless the control is drawn by `file_link` and carries `data-file-link`. It also fails if the Session card's folder button `#feditor` carries `data-file-link`. It also renders the Repo page and the Settings page under the three `vscode` forms (local, ssh-remote, container) and a template, asserting the file form with `:1` and the folder: the checkout for the ledger and a `.shiftlead.yml`, none for `~/.shiftlead/hosts.yml`.
- The help text, if any button's changes, goes with `help.py` here.

**Done when** **Open ledger**, **Open board** (at the item's line), every **Open file** and the transcript buttons open the file in VS Code on the local, ssh-remote and container forms (the ledger in the repo's window), and the template test holds them.

**Related:** TD-688 (the design), TD-532 (two launches), TD-536 (`person.file_link`), TD-662 and TD-663 (TD-657's **Open file** buttons).

## TD-691: Build TD-688 (3): a path in the Transcript page's turns is a link, by the same `paths` RPC and press

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-688's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.6 *A path in a transcript is a link too*, §4.5a *Transcript*; `src/shiftlead/ui/transcript.py` (the route's folder link), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/transcript.html`, `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the pane's path shape and `fetchPaths`, `AO.fileUrl`, `AO.openFile`), the `/api/sessions/<id>/paths` route

**Why:** TD-688's design: Paul asked for links in transcripts, and the Transcript page links no path today.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1767) — the route serves `data-paths` (`transcript.transcript_paths`: the file form, the session's folder link, the wait) where **VS Code** is drawn; `AO.transcriptBlock` asks on a block's first hover through `AO.pathsAsker` (eight runs per ask, one in flight, answers kept for the page's life, a run left out asked again) and `AO.pathLinksHtml` draws each resolved run as an `a.editor` opened on Ctrl or Cmd alone; `tests/test_ui_transcript_paths.py`.

**Fix:**
- **The shape.** The pane's path shape is factored into one function the Transcript page also calls, over a turn's text, a tool line's input and a tool result's text, as they render.
- **The ask.** Each turn block, on its first hover, asks `/api/sessions/<id>/paths` once with its runs, eight at most per ask (more runs, more asks). One ask is in flight at a time, and each run's answer is cached for the page's life. Each run that answered is wrapped in an `a.editor`. Its `href` is `AO.fileUrl` of the editor's file form, and its `data-folder` and `data-wait` are the record's folder link, as `AO.recentFiles` builds them. The route (`transcript.py`) passes that link beside the transcript's own file link: `editor_link` for the record's `dir`, or none under `open_in: none` or with `folder_first: false`, in which case the press is one launch. A block is asked once, and a failed ask leaves it as text.

- **Tests:** in the page's JS tests, a turn with a resolving path and one without, a block asked once on its first hover, a run met twice asked once, and no ask before a hover.

**Done when** a path in a transcript turn that the host resolves is a Ctrl+click link opening the file as the pane's does.

**Related:** TD-688 (the design), TD-690 (the bound it reads), TD-501.

## TD-686: Build TD-682 (1): the reading tells a run that never started from a red one — `checks: not_run` with its reason; no order, no `red_since`; the `done` refusal and the promote's checks say *never ran*

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-682's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.4 *CI that never started is the person's, not a lane's*, §4.8 *A `done` with a PR is told what its checks read*, §6 *Promote* (**checks**); `src/sessionorc/reports.py` (`fold_checks`, `pr_reading`, `_gh_api`), `src/sessionorc/workorders.py` (`red_prs`, `red_holders`), `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`_pr_checks`, near *required checks failed on*), `reports.at_done`, `src/sessionorc/promote.py` (`read_checks`), and the other readers of `checks`: `src/shiftlead/teamrun.py` (`red_prs`), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py`, `src/shiftlead/ui/repo.py`, `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py`

**Why:** TD-682's design. On 2026-10-14 every Actions job in ContractMatch/samscrape failed without starting, for billing. The reading called the PRs red, and `ao repo` gave samscrape's #1097 to a lane that could do nothing.

**Fix:** this is `src/sessionorc/**`, so the techlead reads it (§4.9b).
- **The jobs.** These are read only in a repo whose `origin` is GitHub. In `pr_reading`, for each open PR `fold_checks` calls *red*, take the failing CheckRuns whose `detailsUrl` matches `/actions/runs/<run>/job/<job>`, in order, fifty at most. For each one, read `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/actions/jobs/<job>` and, for a `completed` job with `steps: []` and an empty `runner_name`, `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/check-runs/<job>/annotations`. Stop at the first job that started. A PR past the cap with none started stays *red*. Keep the verdicts on the row by job id (`jobs: {head, read: {<job>: {started, reason}}}`): a job is read once, a new head replaces the map, a Re-run's new attempt (new job ids on the same head) is read afresh, and an unreadable job is not kept.
- **Never started.** A job never started only when it is completed, has no steps and no runner, and an annotation begins *The job was not started because*. That message is the reason. `kind` is *billing* when it names *account payments* or *spending limit*, else *other*. With no such annotation the job is a real failure (a job cancelled while queued looks the same otherwise).
- **The fold.** A PR whose failing items all are Actions jobs that never started gets `checks: not_run`, even with checks still pending. A failing `StatusContext`, a failing non-Actions check run, or a job of any conclusion that fails the three-part test keeps it *red*. A PR turning `not_run` loses its `red_since`, unless it is conflicting, which keeps `red_since` from the conflict so `red_prs` orders it by the conflict alone. The PR carries `not_run: {reason, kind, runs}`, `runs` being the run ids. With one real failure beside them it stays *red*, and the not-started names are left out of `failing`. A job read that fails is no evidence.
- **Every reader of `checks`.** `not_run` is its own word. `red_since` is set only for *red* or conflicting PRs, so `not_run` gets none. `workorders.red_prs`, `red_holders` and `teamrun.red_prs` read it as not red. `ui/inbox.py`'s red PR row leaves it out. `ui/repo.py` and `ui/org.py` count it apart and draw it *CI never ran*. A test walks every switch on `checks` with `not_run` and asserts none falls through to red, green or pending.
- **The declaration.** `_pr_checks` takes the reading's `jobs` for that head when it holds it. Otherwise it reads the failing required checks' jobs alone, bounded as above. `at_done` puts a required check that never started in a `not_run` list beside `failed`. A real failure still refuses as today and wins. `not_run` alone refuses with §4.8's words, naming the PR, the head and the person.
- **The promote.** `promote.read_checks` classifies main's head the same way, from the check runs of `commits/<sha>/check-runs` (a check run's id is its job's), the verdict cached per sha. Its return widens to carry a structured `checks_not_run: {reason, kind, runs}`, kept on the promote reading beside `checks`. All failing runs never started → *unknown — CI never ran: <reason>*. A real failure beside them → *failed*. No failure and some pending → *pending*.
- **`workorders.ci_not_run(repos)`.** In `sessionorc`, it groups, by `origin` owner (a GitHub login, `[A-Za-z0-9-]+`, else the repo is left out), every open PR reading `not_run` and every default branch whose promote reading carries `checks_not_run`. Owners are compared and keyed in lower case. TD-687's row and Telegram line read it.
- **Tests**, against a recorded fixture of the API's answers for #1097's jobs (0 steps, no runner, the billing annotation):
  - a billing PR;
  - another reason;
  - a cancelled-while-queued job with no annotation, which reads red;
  - a failing commit status beside a not-started job, which reads red;
  - a conflicting `not_run` PR becoming an order after `ORPHAN_AFTER`;
  - a Re-run's new attempt on the same head, read afresh;
  - a mix with one real failure;
  - fifty-one failing jobs with none started;
  - an unreadable job;
  - a new head read again;
  - `red_prs` making no order;
  - the `done` refusal from the cache and from its own read;
  - the promote's three cases;
  - `ci_not_run` grouping two owners and leaving out a non-GitHub origin.

**Done when** a PR whose Actions jobs all failed without starting reads `checks: not_run` with its reason and is neither an order nor *red* anywhere. A `done` on it is refused naming the person. The promote reads *unknown — CI never ran*. A PR with one real failure stays red.

**Related:** TD-682 (the design), TD-687 (the row), dev-cadence#TD-115 (the same mapping in `forge.py`, for the cadence check), TD-613 and TD-637.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1766, slice 1; PR #1768, slice 2) — slice 1: the reading tells an Actions job that never started (`checks: not_run`, `not_run: {reason, kind, runs}`, verdicts kept as `jobs` by job id per head), every reader of `checks` and the pages. Slice 2: `reports.at_done`/`done_verdicts` and `_checks_at_done`'s `not_run` refusal in §4.8's words, an `ask`'s *checks never started* line, `promote.read_checks`' third value `checks_not_run` (cached per sha; a rollback's read keeps main's), and `workorders.ci_not_run(repos, promotes)` for TD-687. Left for the next design PR on §4.5a (the techlead's note on #1766): the *team card: Repo facet* row describes *· n red* but not *· n CI never ran*.

## TD-687: Build TD-682 (2): the Inbox row *CI not starting*, one per account — Open, Re-run, Snooze, told on Telegram

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-682's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5a *Inbox row: CI not starting*, §4.4 *CI that never started is the person's*, §4.10 *Told on Telegram when nobody is looking*; `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (beside the red PR row), the Inbox page's template and `app.js`, the home's RPCs (`src/sessionorc/agent_serve.py`, a `ci_rerun` call), `src/sessionorc/agent_notify.py` and `notify.py` (the told list, `_notify_snoozed`), the spells at the home

**Why:** TD-682's design. The cure for CI that does not start is the account's billing, which only the person can fix. Today nothing tells them, and once the bill is paid nothing re-runs the PRs.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1770, PR #1772) — slice 1 (#1770, grinder-ao-1) built the home's `ci_spells`, `ci_rerun`, the run-status reads and the Telegram line; slice 2 (#1772, grinder-ao-2) the Inbox row: `inbox.ci_not_run_rows` from `ci_spells`, one row per spell keyed `ci_not_run:<owner>`, **Open** the billing page (`billing_url`, `gh api users/<owner>` once per account), **Re-run** `ci_rerun` through `/api/person`, *re-run asked <age>* while its runs are pending, **Snooze ▾** by time; the help list's three paragraphs; `tests/test_ui_ci_not_run.py`.

**Fix:**
- **The row.** One row per owner in `workorders.ci_not_run` (TD-686), under *Needs you*, counted, worded as §4.5a words it, each PR and each *main* a link. Its **spell** is kept at the home (`ci_spells: {<owner>: {since, clear, rerun: {at, runs}}}`). It runs from the first grouping until `CI_SPELL_CLEAR` (2) successful readings in a row group nothing for the owner and no run a Re-run asked for is still queued or running. A failed reading counts for nothing.
- **Open.** The owner's billing page: `https://github.com/organizations/<owner>/settings/billing` for an org, `https://github.com/settings/billing` for a user, told apart once with `gh api users/<owner>` `type`.
- **Re-run.** The person's press, joining §4.8's person-only list and served by the home alone (a node forwards it, §4.4a), refused to a session as `inbox_delete` is: `ci_rerun {owner}` runs `gh run rerun <run> --failed` from each repo's root for every run the row's PRs name, bounded as the other `gh` calls are. It answers how many runs were asked and how many `gh` refused, records them on the spell, and the row reads *re-run asked <age>* while any of them is queued or running. Their status is read with `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/actions/runs/<run>` on the same tick as the reading, bounded. A failed status read counts as pending, and a pending run resets the spell's clear count.
- **Snooze ▾.** By time alone, kept under `ci_not_run:<owner>` in the attention store.
- **Telegram.** `agent_notify.py` reads `ci_not_run` and the spells at the home, and tells a row once per spell under `NOTIFY_HOLD`, with a fixed line naming the owner and the count. A snoozed row is not told (`_notify_snoozed` knows the `ci_not_run:<owner>` key). It joins the told list and its test.
- **Help.** The help text for the row is written with `help.py` in this build, not in the design (§4.5a's help list is bound to it by `tests/test_help.py`).
- **Tests**: the row from a reading with two PRs in one org and one in another; a *main* entry; the billing link for an org and for a user; **Re-run** refused to a session and run for the person with a stubbed `gh`; the row standing while the re-run's runs are pending and not told again when they read `not_run`; a new push that reads pending for one reading and then `not_run` again, told once; a failed reading not ending the spell; a snooze running out inside the spell, not told again; the snooze; the told line.

**Done when** an account whose PRs (or a default branch's head) read `not_run` shows one *CI not starting* row with them and the billing link, told on Telegram once per spell. **Re-run** asks GitHub to re-run their failed jobs. The row leaves when its spell ends: two successful readings group nothing, and no re-run is pending. `ci_rerun` is in §4.8's person-only list.

**Related:** TD-682 (the design), TD-686 (the reading), TD-613 (the red PR row it sits beside), TD-092 (Telegram).
