## TD-682: CI that never started shows as a red PR nobody holds, and the person is not told

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the session `ao-dc-decouple`, lessons from the ledgerboard split; Paul agreed the lesson the same day)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-14 (the designer; no mockup: one Inbox row, drawn as the red PR row is) — §4.4 *CI that never started is the person's, not a lane's*. The reading reads each failing GitHub Actions job of a PR it would call red, once per head. A job with no steps and no runner never started, and its reason is its *The job was not started because…* annotation (*billing* when it names payments or a spending limit). A PR whose failing runs all never started reads `checks: not_run`. It gets no `red_since`, is no `pr:<n>` order, has no red-PR row, and its idle holder is not told. A sync PR that is `not_run` waits. A `done` is refused naming the reason and the person (§4.8), and the promote's checks read *unknown — CI never ran* (§6). ShiftLead does this in its own fold, so it does not wait on dev-cadence#TD-115, which maps the same run for the cadence check. The person gets one *Inbox row: CI not starting* per account, under *Needs you*, counted and told on Telegram (§4.10), with **Open** (the billing page), **Re-run** (`gh run rerun --failed`, the person's press) and **Snooze ▾**. It leaves when its spell ends: two successful readings group nothing for the account (no `not_run` PR, no default-branch head that never ran) and no run a **Re-run** asked for is pending. That row replaces the entry's `act` board line, since §4.4 *Board write-back* says no policy adds one. Built by TD-686 and TD-687. Was: Open.
**Blocked by:** TD-686, TD-687
**Location:** the reading of a repo's red PRs (`ao repo`, TD-652's holders), the home's board writes (§4.4 *Board write-back*), §4.4 *A red PR nobody holds is a work order*, design §6

**Why:** On 2026-10-14 every Actions job in ContractMatch/samscrape stopped starting: *recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased*. `ao repo` read samscrape's sync PR (#1097) as *1 red PR nobody holds*. The cause was a fix only the person can make (the org's billing). No team could act on it, and no line told the person. A session found it by reading the run's annotations.

**Fix:** design first. Once dev-cadence#TD-115 reads such a run as *never ran — billing or spending limit*, ShiftLead's PR reading carries that reason. The home then writes one `act` line per account (org), not one per PR, to the board of a repo it affects: *GitHub Actions does not start in <org>: billing or spending limit (PRs …)*. The line is closed when a run in that org starts again. This changes §4.4's work-order rule for these PRs: a PR is red only because its runs never started, so it is not a `pr:<n>` order for a team. No team can fix it, and the `act` line is how the person hears about it.

**Done when** a refused-for-billing run gives the person one `act` line naming the org and the PRs it holds, and the line closes itself when CI runs again.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (the designer) — designed 2026-10-14 (§4.4 *CI that never started is the person's, not a lane's*), built by TD-686 (#1766, #1768) and TD-687 (#1770, #1772), both archived.

**Related:** dev-cadence#TD-115, TD-652, TD-681.

## TD-688: The "open in editor" buttons on a file (Open ledger, every Open file, the transcript's raw file) send a folder link and fail on a remote editor; and a path in the pane links only inside the checkout

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-14 (the designer; no mockup: nothing drawn changes but an underline on hover in the Transcript page's text, as the pane's) — §4.6 *A file button is a file link*. One helper, `editor_file_link(path, folder)`, builds every button that opens one file: **Open ledger**, **Open board** (at the item's line), every **Open file** (Settings, the team header, New session, TD-657's two) and the transcript's **‹›**/**VS Code**. Each is the editor's file form with `:1`, drawn as an `a.editor` and pressed through `AO.openFile`. The folder goes first when the file lies in a registered checkout (the ledger, a `.shiftlead.yml`). A file under `~/.shiftlead` is one launch, as is the transcript. A test over the templates holds every such control to it. §4.6 *A path in the pane is a link*: the bound is now a regular file the session's user can read on the record's host, the real path judged (a symlink out answers). `PATHS_PRIVATE`, the credential paths, stays text, and a read-only Focus keeps the links (its viewer is the person, and the RPC tells no more than the user's own stat). §4.6 *A path in a transcript is a link too*: the Transcript page links paths in its turns through the same RPC and press. Built by TD-689, TD-690 and TD-691. Was: Open.
**Blocked by:** TD-689, TD-690, TD-691
**Location:** design §4.6 *A path in the pane is a link* and *The press is two launches* (TD-532), §4.5a rows *Repo page: Open ledger*, *Settings page: Open file*, *Org: team groups* (the team header's **Open file** on its definition's source, `group_head.html`), *New session*, *Focus header: ‹› VS Code* and *Transcript: VS Code*, and the not-yet-built *Director card*'s and *Inbox row: preferences proposed*'s **Open file** (TD-657), §5 `person.open_in` and `person.file_link`; `src/shiftlead/ui/uiconf.py` (`editor_link`, `editor_file`), `src/shiftlead/ui/common.py` (`editor_link`, the template global), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html:40`, `settings.html:21,27`, `group_head.html:103`, `new.html:9`, `transcript.html:17`, `focus.html:118`, `src/shiftlead/ui/transcript.py` (`transcript_editor`), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`AO.openFile`, `AO.fileUrl`, the `a.editor` click handler), `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`_resolve_paths`, `rpc_paths`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-14: *Pressing "Open ledger" in the repo page seems to attempt to open the file in vscode but fails, whereas I seem to recall others working (e.g. files linked in a transcript).* The links that work are a path in the pane (TD-501) and the Session card's recent files (TD-525). Both build the editor's **file form** with the line after the path (`AO.fileUrl`: `:1` where none was printed). They open it as **two launches**, the session's folder and then the file (`AO.openFile`, TD-532), so the file lands in the worktree's window. Every other file button is built by `editor_link`, which is the **folder** form with a file's path put in it: no `:line`. VS Code opens a remote path as a file only when it ends in `:digits` (TD-524), so on the ssh-remote form the press opens nothing usable. Those buttons are **Open ledger**, the Settings page's and the team card's **Open file**, the New session form's **Open file**, and the transcript's raw-file button on the transcript page and in Focus. Five of the seven lack the `editor` class, so they navigate the tab itself instead of going through `AO.openEditor`'s hidden frame, and no folder launch goes first. The two transcript buttons have the class. They are one launch on purpose: §4.5a *Focus header: ‹› VS Code* says the file is the tool's, not the worktree's. They still send the folder form with no `:line`. One person pressing two buttons that look alike gets two behaviours. Paul's second ask: *add links in our transcripts to any file that is actually available on the corresponding machine (e.g. ~/.bashrc would not have a link currently).* Today `_resolve_paths` answers only a regular file under the record's `dir` or `repo`, the *in our repo* bound §4.6 names as Paul's, so `~/.bashrc`, a file in `~/.claude`, or a sibling repo's file is text.

**Fix:** a design round first, then the build entries it calls for.
- **One form for every file button.** Every button `editor_link` now builds for a file takes the editor's file form with its line. So do TD-657's two **Open file** buttons once they are built. The press is §4.6's *two launches*, the folder launch first and then the file, except where the design keeps one launch, as for the transcript (`first: false`, the file form alone). The design names the folder each one opens first. For **Open ledger** that is the repo's checkout, "open worktree then file" in Paul's words. For a file outside any checkout (`~/.shiftlead/settings.yml`, a transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`) the design picks between the file alone (`first: false`) and its directory. The server hands each button its folder link and its file link, as `AO.recentFiles` builds them; `editor_link` stays the folder button's alone.
- **A check that keeps them alike**: a test that every `‹›`/**Open file** control in the templates is an `a.editor` built from the file form, so a new one cannot fall back to the folder form.
- **The bound on a pane path.** §4.6's *a regular file under the record's `dir` or its `repo`* becomes *a regular file on the record's host the session's user can read*: the same `paths` RPC, still a stat that opens nothing, with `~` as the session's user's home. The round settles three things. Does a read-only Focus still get these links? A wider bound tells such a viewer which paths exist on the host. Does a symlink out of the checkout now resolve? Do any paths stay text whatever the stat says (`~/.ssh`, a secrets file)?

**Done when** every file button on the pages opens the file in the person's editor by the same two launches as a pane path, on the local, ssh-remote and container forms, held by a test over the templates. A path in the pane or the transcript that names a readable file on the session's host outside its checkout (`~/.bashrc`) is a link under the bound the design writes.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (the designer) — designed 2026-10-14 (§4.6 *A file button is a file link*, *A path in the pane is a link*, *A path in a transcript is a link too*; #1764), built by TD-689 (#1765), TD-690 (#1774) and TD-691 (#1767), all archived.

**Related:** TD-501 (a path in the pane is a link), TD-524 and TD-526 (the line after the path), TD-532 (two launches), TD-535 and TD-536 (the recent files, `person.file_link`), TD-148 (the Settings page's **Open file**).

## TD-694: Build TD-692: a reconnect reloads once, never in a loop — an `error` is not up, the reload bound and its banner, the stream's `page=`, the UI's two log lines

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-692's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5 *Browser mechanics* (*A reconnect reloads once, never in a loop*), §4.5a *every page: reload-loop banner*; `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`connectEvents`, `setDown`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/base.html` (the banner: one element under the top bar, shared by every page; a popped Focus draws it at the top), `src/shiftlead/ui/common.py` (`log`, `static_url`), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`events`)

**Why:** TD-692's design. On 2026-10-14 three of Paul's tabs reloaded every second or two from 16:28 to 18:22, about 90 `/events` opens a minute, and the UI logged nothing. The suspect: `events` sends `{"event": "error"}` and closes when its stream fails, and `connectEvents` takes that message as *up*. A page whose stream fails each time it opens then reloads on its second socket, every time.

**Fix:**
- **Reproduce first, on a scratch home** (a short `SHIFTLEAD_HOME`, never the live one): open Focus and the repo page in headless Chromium (`~/ao-shots/pwlib`). Make `events` fail at its start (a test double for `h.counts.join` or `fan.join` that raises), then restart the UI and the agent in each order, and promote. Record what closes the socket: before its first real message (`error`), or after a real one (a stream that comes up, then closes). Record also whether a plain reload keeps the loop going where a hard refresh does not. Put the finding in the PR body. If the cause is not the `error` shape, say so on TD-692 before building past it.
- **`error` is not up.** `connectEvents` handles an `error` event itself, before the page's handler: `AO.toast(ev.text)` once per page load, on every page with a stream: the Org, the repo page, Focus, a popped Focus (today only the Org's handler toasts it; the repo page and Focus drop it). It runs before `setDown(false)` and the reload check. The stream stays not up: no `setDown(false)`, no `streamsUp`, no reload, and `reconnected` is left as it was. The Org's own `error` branch goes. `delay` goes back to 500 ms at the first message that is not `error`, not in `onopen`: today an accepted-then-closed socket resets it each time, so a failing stream reopens every half second.
- **The bound.** Each reload on a reconnect is recorded in `sessionStorage` under `ao.reloads:<path>`, as a list of times. Before reloading, the page drops the times older than 60 s. If 3 are left, it does not reload. It clears `reconnected`, draws the banner once, and dispatches that message and every later one as a stream that was up all along. Otherwise it appends the time, sets `ao.reloading:<path>`, and reloads. At load, a page that finds `ao.reloading:<path>` removes it and keeps the list. A page that does not find it clears the list. Every read and write is wrapped in try/catch; storage that throws counts nothing, and the page reloads as before.
- **The banner.** It has §4.5a's words and **Reload**, which clears the list and reloads.
- **`page=` and `at=`.** The stream's query carries the `v=` value of the `app.js` link the page loaded, read from its script tag, and `location.pathname`. `events` keeps both in the `Stream` it builds.
- **The open-rate warning.** `events` counts the accepts per client address (`ws.client.host`) and `at` over 60 s. Past 20, it writes one `log.warning` line (`common.log`, `uvicorn.error`) in §4.5's words, at most once per address and path every 10 minutes. The counts and both limiters are in-process state of the UI app, kept beside `fan`. `at` and `page` come from the client: both are cut to 100 characters, keyed on the cut values, and logged with `%r`; a missing `ws.client` counts as `""`. Each accept drops the counter's times older than 60 s and the limiter's marks older than 10 minutes, so the tables stay small. *this UI serves* is the `v=` value of `static_url("app.js")`.
- **The exception log.** The `except Exception` in `events` logs its exception with the traceback (`log.exception`, the same logger), at most once a minute. Today only that path is silent: the shared subscriber's failures are already logged by `Fanout` (*the events stream failed*), which keeps no limit and stays as it is.
- **Tests:**
  - a page whose stream sends only `error` and closes does not reload, and toasts the text once on the Org, the repo page and Focus;
  - a stream that sends only `error` reconnects with growing delays (500 ms, 1 s, 2 s … capped at 10 s);
  - `error`, a close, then a real message reloads once;
  - a stream that sends a real message, then closes, each time: three reloads in 60 s hold back the fourth and draw the banner;
  - after a held-back reload, later messages patch the page and draw no second banner;
  - **Reload** clears the count;
  - a load the page did not make clears it too;
  - storage that throws reloads as before;
  - the warning is written past 20 opens from one address and path, once in 10 minutes, naming the path and both hashes; 20 opens spread over two paths write nothing;
  - a failing stream logs its traceback, at most once a minute.


**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1786) — reproduced first on a scratch home (a UI whose `fan.join` raises): the Org, the repo page and Focus each reloaded about twice a second, two `/events` opens a load, nothing logged — the `error` shape. Built: `connectEvents` takes `error` as not up (toasted once a load; the backoff put back at the first real message), the reload bound in `sessionStorage` (`ao.reloads:<path>`, `ao.reloading:<path>`, counted once per reload) and the banner in `base.html`; `?page=&at=` on the stream; `fanout.OpenRate` and `Every`, the open-rate warning and the handler's traceback in `events`. `tests/test_ui_reload_loop.py`. The reproduction and the UI check are in the PR body.
**Done when** the reproduction is in the PR body and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-692 (the design), TD-372 (a close the page caused by leaving), TD-539 (the build chip), TD-062 (a promote restarts both units).

## TD-692: An open page can reload itself about once a second for hours, and only a hard refresh ends it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (session `promote_check`, from Paul's report that ShiftLead had looked down for 30 minutes)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-14 (the designer; no mockup: one banner, drawn as the down banner is) — §4.5 *Browser mechanics* *A reconnect reloads once, never in a loop*. A stream is up at its first message that is not `error`, so a stream that fails each time it opens never reloads the page. Reloads on a reconnect are counted in `sessionStorage` by path; a fourth within 60 s is held back and the reload-loop banner (§4.5a, **Reload**) says why. The stream carries `?page=<hash>` (its `app.js`'s `v=`); the UI logs one warning for a client opening `/events` from one path more than 20 times in 60 s, naming the page's hash and its own, and logs the exception behind the `error` the `events` handler sends itself, at most once a minute (the subscriber's already is). `connectEvents` toasts an `error` on every page. The reproduction on a scratch home is the build's first step. Built by TD-694. Was: Open — Owner was `grinder` until 2026-10-14, which put a `design-first` entry in no lane (the design lane is `[design-first, owner:designer]`, design §4.9c); the design round is the designer's.
**Blocked by:** TD-694
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` `connectEvents` (*a reconnect reloads the snapshot once*); design §4.5 *Browser mechanics*

**Why:** On 2026-10-14 Paul's laptop showed ShiftLead as down for at least 30 minutes, though Tailscale was connected. On kmaster both units were up and answering 200s, and the route port refused nothing from the laptop. In the UI's journal, three open tabs (`/repo/shiftlead`, Focus `ao-shiftlead-ao-connect`, Focus `ao-shiftlead-ao-dc-decouple`) each loaded the page, opened `/events`, and loaded the page again a second or two later. Together that was about 90 `/events` opens a minute, from 16:28:31 until Paul's hard refresh at 18:22:56. The loop lasted through five restarts (16:33, 16:59, 17:26, 17:57 and 18:18), each one an `auto` promote. Nothing in the journal flags it, and no error was logged. It began with no restart or promote at 16:28. After the hard refresh it fell to 0–14 opens a minute.

**Suspect, not proven:** `ws.onmessage` reloads when `reconnected` is set, and `onclose` sets it. If a socket closes before its first message and the next one gets a message, each fresh page reloads once more. The comment above `onopen` names that shape for a down agent. A plain reload kept the loop going and a hard refresh ended it, so a cached subresource (`app.js`, or the HTML that names it) is part of it.

**Fix:** design first (§4.5 *Browser mechanics*).
- **Reproduce** the loop on a scratch home: open Focus and the repo page in headless Chromium, restart the UI and the agent in each order, and promote. Record what closes the socket before its first message.
- **Bound it.** A page that has reloaded on reconnect more than N times in M seconds stops reloading. It shows the down banner with a **Reload** button and says why. A `sessionStorage` count keyed by path does it.
- **Make it visible.** The UI logs one warning when the same client reloads in a loop. A promote's restart is the usual trigger, so the warning names the build the page came from (`this page: <sha7>`, §4.5a build chip).
- **Tests:** the bound (a page stops after N reloads in M seconds) and the warning.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (the designer) — designed 2026-10-14 (§4.5 *Browser mechanics*, *A reconnect reloads once, never in a loop*; #1782), built by TD-694 (#1786), archived.

**Related:** TD-372 (a close the page caused by leaving is no outage), TD-539 (build chip: *this page* differs from the agent), TD-062 (promote restarts both units).

## TD-695: `test_a_pass_that_covers_the_repo_holds_a_green_pr_back_and_one_that_cannot_does_not` flakes: the promote's own sync task may run a pass inside the test

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (grinder-ao-1, from grinder-ao-2's note m-ff4ef0883a87)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved. Seen once on py3.12 in PR #1779's run 38671055081, at `tests/test_sync_pass.py:286` (*no login: no cover, the team's*); it passed on rerun.
**Location:** `tests/test_sync_pass.py` (the cover test, lines ~277–286), `src/sessionorc/agent_promote.py:60` (`_sync_task`), `src/sessionorc/agent_sync.py` (where `_sync_ran` and `_sync_login` are used; declared at `agent.py:723-725`)

**Why:** A flaky test in the sync pass (TD-685 slice 2, #1771) costs every PR a rerun. The likely cause is that the `agent` fixture is a running host agent: its promote watch starts `_sync_pass` as a background task (`agent_promote.py:60`) on a full reading. The first tick is a full reading, because `_promote_read_at` starts at `-inf`. After that, `PROMOTE_EVERY` is 300 s, so the race is between the fixture's first tick and the test body, never a repeating one. `_sync_pass` walks `self._repos`, which the test has just set. That first-tick task could run between the test's `_sync_ran.clear()` (with the login cleared) and its assert, re-reading the login through the `gh` fake and setting `_sync_ran[ROOT]` again. A second cause to rule out is `_red_prs` reading a stamp the background pass moved.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1787) — the race was the first tick's full reading, still in flight when the test began on a slow runner: its `_sync_pass` task ran beside the test's pass and set `_sync_ran` again after the test cleared it (reproduced by slowing `promote.survey` 20 ms). `tests/test_sync_pass.py`'s module-level `agent` fixture awaits that first task and holds a never-done future in `_sync_task`, so the watch starts no pass during any test of the module. The check of the module's other tests found a second race of the same kind: each tick's `_refresh_repos` drops the test's `ROOT`, which no registry lists (a test that sleeps through a tick loses it), so the fixture holds `_repos_task` the same way. 800 runs of the test under 0–50 ms of delay, and every integration test of the module, pass.

**Fix:** reproduce it first (`pytest --count` or a loop of the one test under `-p no:randomly`). Then either stop the promote's watch from starting a sync task in these tests (a fixture that sets `_sync_task` to a done task, or a monkeypatched `_sync_pass` guard), or make the test assert on a pass it awaits alone. Check the other `agent_sync` integration tests for the same race.

**Done when** the test passes 200 runs in a row, and the fix names the race it closed.

**Related:** TD-685 (the sync pass).

## TD-698: Build TD-693 (3): a design entry archives with its last build — the td flow's briefs say so, and the designer's says when it is the fallback

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-693's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*; `src/shiftlead/flows/td/build.md`, `src/shiftlead/flows/td/design.md`, `src/shiftlead/briefs/grinder.md`, `src/shiftlead/briefs/designer.md`; `docs/briefs/designer-ao-1.md` (a held path, `docs/briefs/**`)

**Why:** TD-693's design. A design entry needed a PR of its own to archive it once its builds were archived (#1755, #1777, #1780). Also, `design.md` says a design *ends when its entry is archived with the build entries*, which is no longer how a design is left: it stays *Designed*, blocked by its builds.

**Fix:**
- **`build.md`** (and `grinder.md` where it says how an entry is archived): when the entry your PR archives is the last build still in the ledger on `origin/<default>` of a design entry's `Blocked by:`, and that `Blocked by:` names builds alone (no `decision (…)`, no other repo's item), move that design entry to the archive in the same PR. Give it a `**Resolved:**` line naming each build and the PR that merged it (`gh pr list --state merged --search "TD-n in:title"`). Read it again at the rebase before the merge.
- **`build.md`'s opening** (*those are yours once it is archived*) becomes: once the design entry names them in its `Blocked by:`.
- **`design.md`**: a design ends when its entry reads *Designed* and its `Blocked by:` names its builds. This replaces *a design ends when its entry is archived with the build entries*. It archives with its last build. A design entry in your lane whose builds are all archived is the fallback, and you archive it as an item of its own.
- **`docs/briefs/designer-ao-1.md`**: the same sentence, in the round's last step. That file is a held path, so the techlead reads it.
- **Tests:** the briefs' doc-bound tests, where any read these lines, and `tests/test_briefs_layout.py`.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1790) — `flows/td/build.md` says a design's builds are yours once its entry names them in `Blocked by:`, and that the last build's PR archives the design entry with a `**Resolved:**` naming each build and its PR; `flows/td/design.md` says a design ends at *Designed* with its builds in `Blocked by:`, archives with its last build, and the fallback is the designer's; `flows/build/build.md`, `flows/build-review/build.md` and `briefs/grinder.stage.md` (no flow) archive the design entry with its last build too; `docs/briefs/designer-ao-1.md` says the same in *What a round produces here*. The template `grinder.md` is unchanged: it archives only live checks' and looks' entries.

**Done when** the briefs say it and the next design whose last build merges is archived in that build's PR.

**Related:** TD-693 (the design), TD-682 / #1777 and TD-688 / #1780 (archive-only PRs).

## TD-696: Build TD-693 (1): the home hands out ledger ids — `td_next`, `ids.json`, `ao td next`, and every filer's rule

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-693's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.4 *A ledger entry's id is handed out by the home*, §4.7 *Entries*; `src/sessionorc/` (a new `agent_ids.py` mixin beside `agent_spend.py`, `paths.py` for `ids.json`, `ledger.py`'s `ids_in`, `modes.py`'s `offline_refusal`, a new method set and its reason; `agent_serve`'s node branch already forwards on any reason, a person's call included, and is not changed), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao td next`, the `td` group's help), `src/shiftlead/briefs/entry.md` (*The number*), `src/shiftlead/briefs/designer.md`, `src/shiftlead/briefs/grinder.md`

**Why:** TD-693's design. Every filer took main's highest id plus one, so two filers at once collided and one renumbered across a rebase (TD-651 → 653 → 656 on 2026-10-13; TD-693 → 694 on 2026-10-14).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1794) — `src/sessionorc/agent_ids.py`'s `rpc_td_next`: the open PRs' added headings, then main's ledger and archive after a fetch, then `ids.json`'s `last`, under one lock per origin in a 45 s budget; `modes.IDS` forwards it from a node and refuses it offline; `ao td next` in `cli.py`; the entry, designer and grinder briefs take their numbers from it; `tests/test_td_next.py`.

**Fix:** this touches `src/sessionorc/**`, so the techlead reads it (§4.9b).
- **`td_next(repo, count)`**, a host-agent RPC, under one `asyncio.Lock` per repo, with no `person_only` check. `by` is the dispatcher's authenticated caller (§4.8a), never a parameter. A node forwards it to the home and refuses it offline (§4.4a's table): `td_next` gets its own set in `offline_refusal`, checked beside `HOME_EDITS` and before the `caller is None` return (else a person's call is served on the node and `ids.json` splits per host), refused in *ids.json is the home's* words. `offline_refusal` returns the reason, and `agent_serve`'s node branch already forwards on it, and is in neither `HOME_EDITS` (whose `PERSON_NODE_BOUND` would refuse a person's call from a node) nor `identity.READS`, so the verified caller reaches it. The whole call has a 45-second budget from its arrival, the wait for the lock included: a lock not taken by 30 s refuses (*busy, ask again*); the PRs are read a few at a time until 30 s, and those not read are `unread: budget`; the fetch has until 45 s and refuses past it. Every `gh` and `git` call runs through `asyncio.to_thread` or an async subprocess, killed at its deadline (`ledger._git` is a blocking `subprocess.run`). It takes the repo by its registered name, never a path, which on a node is the node's; a name registered roots of different origins share is refused naming them (not `rpc_entry_add`'s first match), and an origin `owner/repo` is accepted; roots of one origin are one repo, so the first of them serves (unlike `Registry._find`, which refuses any second hit). The CLI factors out `cmd_td_add`'s repo resolution and its `_main_checkout` default only, never its session refusal, and sends the registry's own spelling of the name (`Path(raw).expanduser().name`, the `raw` key `cmd_td_add` keeps, mapped back from the resolved root when `--repo` is not given, so a symlinked checkout keeps its registered name), or the origin's `owner/repo` when that name is shared:
  1. list the open PRs (`gh pr list --state open --limit 200`; a failed list, or one that fills 200, is one `unread` line), then read each one's `+## TD-NNN:` lines from `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls/<n>/files --paginate` (the ledger's and the archive's patches), collecting as `unread` each PR whose listing fails or is cut at 3000 files, or whose ledger file has no `patch`;
  2. then fetch `origin/<default>` in the checkout, refusing with the reason when the fetch fails or leaves no `origin/<default>` ref, so a PR merged between the two reads is in main;
  3. read the highest id in the ledger and its archive at that ref (`ledger.ids_in`). The ledger is `.shiftlead.yml`'s `ledger:` and the archive `ledger.archive_path` of it, never `Registry.LEDGER`'s default; step 1 matches the PRs' files on the same two paths;
  4. take the highest of those and `ids.json`'s `last`, and give the next `count` ids (1 to 10);
  5. write `last` and append to `given`, `{id, by, at}`, keeping the newest 200; `ids.json` and the lock are keyed by the origin, `owner/repo` for GitHub (ssh and https alike) and the lowercased URL otherwise, and `by` is the dispatcher's `caller`, or `person` when there is none.
  `ids.json` is written whole, through a temp file and a rename, as `spend.json` is.
- **`ao td next [--repo] [--count] [--json]`**: prints the ids one a line; `unread` goes to standard error, and into `--json` as `{repo, ids, unread}`. The repo defaults as `ao td add`'s does. It is open to every session and the person. The `td` group's help stops saying *a person's own* for the group; the wording is the `td` parser's `help=` in `cli.py` (`help.py` holds no `td` text).
- **The filers' rule.** In `entry.md`, *The number* becomes `ao td next`, with the old rule (main, the archive, every open PR's diff, re-read before the merge) as the fallback when `ao` is not there or refuses. `designer.md` and `grinder.md` point new entries at it. A build's own entries (the designer's) take `--count`.
- **Tests:**
  - two concurrent `td_next` calls give different ids;
  - a PR that merges between the PR read and the fetch is counted;
  - `by` is the caller, whatever the call carries;
  - a node forwards the call, a person's included, and refuses it offline;
  - PRs not read by 30 s are `unread: budget`, and the ids still come;
  - a lock not taken by 30 s refuses *busy, ask again*;
  - a name two checkouts of different origins share is refused, and `owner/repo` picks one; two checkouts of one origin are served by `owner/repo`;
  - a symlinked checkout is sent by its registered name;
  - two checkouts with one origin, one cloned by ssh and one by https, share one counter;
  - three calls on one repo at once all answer inside the client's timeout;
  - a person's call on a node, its checkout at another path, reaches the home and is served by name;
  - a repo with a custom `ledger:` reads that file and its archive;
  - an open PR's added heading raises the floor;
  - a PR whose files cannot be read is named in `unread`, and the ids still come;
  - a failed fetch refuses;
  - `last` beats a lower main, so a given id that is never used is never given again;
  - `given` keeps 200;
  - `--count 3` gives three ids in a row.

**Done when** two sessions asking at the same moment get different ids with no rebase, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-693 (the design), TD-585 (ledgerboard is ShiftLead's parser), TD-219 (`ao td add`).

## TD-699: #1786's *held-back reload takes the stream as its own* — `reconnected = false` in `connectEvents` — is held by no test (test audit)

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1786)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `tests/test_ui_reload_loop.py` (`test_three_reloads_in_a_minute_hold_back_the_fourth_and_draw_the_banner`, `test_after_a_held_back_reload_later_messages_patch_and_no_second_banner`), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`connectEvents`' `onmessage`, the `reconnected = false;  // held back` line)

**Why:** Design §4.5 *A reconnect reloads once, never in a loop* says of a held-back reload: "The page then takes the stream as its own: it clears its *reconnected* mark, draws the *reload-loop banner* once, and patches from that message on." Delete the one line `reconnected = false;  // held back: this stream is the page's own from here on` in `app.js` and `pdm run pytest -q tests/test_ui_reload_loop.py tests/test_ui_counts.py` still passes (21 passed): the PR's scenario 5 (`out.after`) sends its next messages inside the 60 s window, where `reloadOnReturn()` is held back again whether or not the mark was cleared. With the line gone, the mark stays set and the first message that arrives after the recorded times age out (more than 60 s on) reloads the page — a reload the design says the page no longer makes on that stream — and the line was the only thing between a held-back page and one more reload. Not shown by the tests: a message more than `AO.RELOADS_WINDOW` after the held-back one, on the same stream, must patch and not reload.

**Fix:** extend the probe in `tests/test_ui_reload_loop.py` after scenario 5: `advance(61000)`, `say(REAL)`, and assert `reloads` is still 3 and `handled` grew. Check it fails with the line deleted.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1797) — the probe's scenario 5b (`advance(61000); say(REAL)` on the same stream) and `test_a_held_back_page_keeps_the_stream_past_the_window` assert the message patches with no fourth reload; with the `reconnected = false` line deleted it fails (reloads 4).

**Done when** that assertion exists and fails against the reverted line.

**Related:** TD-692 (the design), TD-694 (the build, #1786).

## TD-697: Build TD-693 (2): the Repo page draws a design's builds under it, with each build's state

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-693's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 11 *Technical debt* (*Its builds*), §4.5a *Repo page: its builds line*; mockup `RepoPage.dc.html` (the *Blocked* list); `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (`entries`: `blocked_ids`; the reading: `archived`), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (the Repo page's Technical debt lists), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/` (the repo page), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.css`

**Why:** TD-693's design. A design's builds name nothing back, and the page groups nothing under the design. To learn that TD-686 and TD-687 build TD-682 you read each entry.

**Fix:**
- **The reading grows** (`src/sessionorc/**`, so the techlead reads it, §4.9b). `entries` carries each entry's whole `Blocked by:` ids as `blocked_ids`, archived ones kept; `blocked_by` stays what still blocks. The repo's ledger reading carries as `archived` only the archived ids some entry's `blocked_ids` names (never the whole archive, which would ride every `repos` push), read from the archive text `ledger.reading` already holds, not from `Registry`'s resolver, which reads other repos at `origin/<default>`.
- **A design's builds.** For each `design-first` entry whose `blocked_ids` is not empty, take those ids in order (`blocked_ids` is `ledgerboard.parse_blocked` of the entry's `blocked_raw` with the `#` items dropped, each through `ledger._norm` so `TD-42` and the archive's `TD-042` match; an archived id counts as a build), each with its state:
  - *archived* when its id is in the archive's ids;
  - else *in review #n* from its holder's claim `pr` or `review_pr`;
  - else *held by <name>*;
  - else *open*;
  - and *blocked by TD-n* when another of the design's builds is in its `blocked_by` (what still blocks, never `blocked_ids`; only its items matching `TD-\d+`, each through `_norm`, since `blocked_by` also holds decisions, `<repo>#` items and unreadable ones).
  When all are archived, the line reads *every build archived — archive this entry*. A build's row gains *builds TD-n* after its owner, from the same pass.
- **The line.** One `.sub`-sized line under the design's row, ids as the page's row links (§4.5a *Repo page: links*). An archived id is plain text. It is drawn in whichever list holds the design row (*blocked*, mostly).
- **Verify on a scratch home** before the PR (the grinder brief's rule for `src/shiftlead/ui/`), with a shot in the PR body.
- **Tests:**
  - the line's order and every state;
  - a design whose builds are all archived still lists them, as *archived*;
  - `archived` holds only ids some `blocked_ids` names;
  - a `Blocked by:` written `TD-42` matches the archive's `TD-042`, in `blocked_ids` and in a build's `blocked_by` alike, and a `<repo>#TD-n` item is not in `blocked_ids`;
  - *every build archived* when none is left;
  - a build's *builds TD-n* link;
  - no line on an entry whose `Blocked by:` names no build.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1793) — the ledger reading carries `blocked_ids` per entry and `archived` (the archived ids some `blocked_ids` names); `design_builds` in `ui/repo.py` draws a design's *builds:* line under its row (*archived* · *in review #n* · *held by <name>* · *open*, *blocked by TD-n*; *every build archived — archive this entry*) and a build's *builds TD-n* back-link; checked on a scratch home, shots `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-14-td697-builds-*.png`.

**Done when** a design entry's row on the Repo page shows its builds and their states, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-693 (the design), TD-652 (*held by*), TD-228 (pickable from `Blocked by`).

## TD-693: A new TD id is the highest on main plus one, so concurrent filers collide; a design's builds show nowhere as its group; a design entry needs its own archive PR after its builds

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (session `ao-paul`, from Paul's question about subtask ids such as TD-682a; he agreed the three parts below the same day)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-14 (the designer; mockup `RepoPage.dc.html`, the *Blocked* list's builds line; shot `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-14-td693-builds-line.png`) — §4.4 *A ledger entry's id is handed out by the home*: `ao td next [--repo] [--count]` (§4.7) asks the home's `td_next`, which gives the next id above the ledger and archive on `origin/<default>`, every open PR's added `## TD-NNN:` headings, and the last id it gave, recorded in `ids.json` under one lock. An id is never given twice and never expires; an unused one is a gap, which cadence §2.2 does not forbid. A session with no home keeps the old rule. Subtask ids are not taken (ledgerboard's format). §4.5 screen 11 *Its builds*: a design entry's row carries *builds:* with each build's state (*archived* · *in review #n* · *held by <name>* · *open*, *blocked by TD-n*), and a build's row says *builds TD-n* (§4.5a). §4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*: the last build's PR archives the design entry in the same commit; a design entry left behind is pickable and its designer's, as before, and the person's in a repo with no team. Built by TD-696, TD-697 and TD-698. Was: Open.
**Blocked by:** TD-696, TD-697, TD-698
**Location:** design §4.9c (flows), §4.5 (the ledger and Repo pages), §6 (the home's policies), §4.7 (CLI); `scripts/ledgerboard.py` is read, never changed

**Why:** Three costs of the `td` flow, as it ran on 2026-10-14:
- **Ids collide.** Nothing assigns them. Every filer (designer, grinder, auditor, a person's session) takes main's highest number plus one, then greps open PRs' diffs. Two filers at once take the same number, and the later one renumbers across a rebase (TD-651 → 653 → 656, 2026-10-13).
- **A design's builds are not shown as its group.** A design entry's `**Blocked by:**` names its builds, but no page groups them under it, and a build names nothing back. You learn that TD-686 and TD-687 build TD-682 by reading each entry.
- **A design entry costs one more PR.** It stays open until its builds are archived, then a PR archives it alone (#1755, #1777, #1780).

Paul considered subtask ids (TD-682a, TD-682b) to fix the first two. They are not this entry's fix. The id format is ledgerboard's (`HEADING_RE`, `ROW_RE`, `ID_ITEM_RE` and `XREPO_ITEM_RE` match `TD-` plus digits, and `_num` takes the part after the dash as an int), so it would mean a spec change and a release through dev-cadence into every consumer, and ShiftLead's own `sessionorc/ledger.py` parses the number as an int. A suffix would only stop collisions among a design's builds, and it would repeat what `Blocked by` already says.

**Fix:** design first, in three parts, none of which changes the ledger format. (The ask as filed; the *Status* line says what the design settled: an id never expires, and the last build's PR archives the design entry.)
1. **The home reserves ids.** A command (e.g. `ao td next <repo>`) returns the next free id for a repo and records it (`ao td` is already the person's verb for handing an entry to the techlead, §4.7, and allocates nothing). Free means above main's highest, every open PR's added headings and every live reservation. Every filer's brief and the cadence's filing rule use it. An unused reservation is a gap in the numbers, which is allowed ("never reused" still holds). The design settles where the reservation lives, when it expires, and what a session with no home does (today's rule, as the fallback).
2. **The pages group builds under their design**, read from `Blocked by`: the Repo page's ledger list, and wherever a design entry is drawn. Each build shows its state (open, built, archived) beside it.
3. **A design entry archives itself** when its last build archives. The home's policy writes the archive commit, or the build's own archive PR carries the design's archive as well. The design picks one and says who owns it in a repo with no team.

**Done when** two sessions filing at the same moment get different ids with no rebase, a design entry's page shows its builds and their states, and no PR exists only to archive a design entry.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 — built and archived with its last build (§4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*): TD-698 (#1790, the td flow's briefs), TD-696 (#1794, `td_next` and `ao td next`), TD-697 (#1793, the Repo page's builds line).

**Related:** TD-585 (ledgerboard is ShiftLead's parser), TD-228 (pickable from `Blocked by`), TD-682 / #1777 (an archive-only PR).

## TD-701: Ready to close reads a squash-merged branch as unpushed when its upstream is `origin/main`, so a finished seat cannot be closed

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.2 (*branch pushed*); `src/sessionorc/gitinfo.py` (`_unpushed`), `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`ready_to_close` ~L1047)

**Why:** `docs-audit-ao-1`'s Focus, 2026-10-14 21:53 MDT (Paul's screenshot, `~/.shiftlead/attachments/ao-shiftlead-ao-paul/paste-20261014-215450.png`): *✗ branch pushed (vs origin/main)*, Git *td632-git-card-deletion-code · 1 unpushed vs origin/main · 1 ahead · 147 behind · clean*, so the seat would not close. Its one commit, `5f7161ab`, is #1643's head, merged 2026-10-13T15:46Z by squash, and its branch deleted from origin. The branch was cut with `git switch -c … origin/main`, so its upstream is `origin/main`; a squash leaves the commit on no remote-tracking ref, and `_unpushed` counts it. Every worker and seat that cuts its branch this way and merges by squash reads *not pushed* once the remote branch is deleted.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-14 (PR #1800) — `gitinfo._not_in_upstream`: rule 2 counts only the commits ahead whose patch the upstream lacks (`--cherry-pick --right-only`), and reads 0 when `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the upstream and `HEAD` is the upstream's tree (a squash of several); `test_a_squash_merged_branch_tracking_origin_main_reads_pushed` holds both halves of *Done when*.

**Fix:** a commit whose content is in its upstream, or that is the head of a merged PR the reading already holds, is not unpushed: count only commits whose patch is absent from the upstream (`git cherry` / `--cherry-pick` over the range), and failing that, a branch whose PR is merged at the same head is pushed.

**Done when** a test holds a branch with upstream `origin/main`, one commit squash-merged into it under another sha, and its remote branch gone, reading 0 unpushed; and a commit that never reached the remote still reads 1.

**Related:** TD-700, TD-080 (one measure, computed by the host agent).

## TD-700: A `prs` or `every` seat that comes due while it is still running sits idle forever: the tick fills only an ended seat and closes only one with nothing due

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1798
**Status:** Done — built by #1798 (grinder-ao-1, 2026-10-14), read live by grinder-ao-2 on 2026-10-15. Before that read: `_seat_done` reads a `prs` or `every` due as the next fill's, and the test half of *Done when* passes. To read once #1798 is live (`ao promote status`): an auditor seat (`ao-shiftlead-docs-audit-ao-1` or `ao-shiftlead-test-audit-ao-1`) whose `seat_due` came while it ran is, once idle and pushed past `SEAT_IDLE_GRACE`, closed by the tick (`closer: {by: tick, why: seat}`) and filled on the next one (`ao status --json`: `restarts[-1].why == "fill"` within a tick of its going idle, `seat_count` starting again).
**Location:** design §6 rule 3, §4.9b *Seats with a trigger*; `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_seat_pass` ~L2315, `_seat_done` ~L2353, `_seat_due` ~L2400)

**Why:** ao-grind's two auditors stopped running for two days with nobody told. `ao status --json`, 2026-10-14: `ao-shiftlead-docs-audit-ao-1` created 2026-10-13T15:26:54Z, `seat_due: {at: 2026-10-13T16:15:47Z, by: prs}`, `seat_count.prs: 100`, idle since 2026-10-14T00:00Z; `ao-shiftlead-test-audit-ao-1` created 2026-10-12T21:00:36Z, `seat_due` at 22:27:10Z, idle the same. Each came due 49 and 87 minutes into its run, as ten PRs merged under it. `_seat_pass` fills a seat only when it is `exited` or `closed` with `seat_due` set, and closes an idle one only when `_seat_done` — which is `not s.seat_due` for a `prs` or `every` trigger. A seat due while it runs is therefore never closed, so never filled. Paul's Close of test-audit on 2026-10-14 ~21:50 MDT let the tick fill it at once (`restarts[-1]: {why: fill, at: 2026-10-15T03:52:03Z}`). Its symptom on the page: no auditor line in the Doing feed (TD-702 is the other half).

**Fix:** a `prs` or `every` seat that is idle, has run, and is pushed closes as a done seat does, and the standing `seat_due` fills it on the next tick — the due that came during the run is the next run's cause, as the anchor's `work` trigger already reads it (`_seat_done`'s `work` branch). The count the run covered is not counted twice: `seat_count` is read from the fill on.

**Done when** a test holds a `prs` seat whose `seat_due` is set mid-run: idle and pushed, it is closed and then filled, and `_seat_done` says so; and on the live copy an auditor that came due mid-run is filled again within a tick of its going idle.

**Related:** TD-701 (the close it needs can be blocked), TD-702, TD-386 (the anchor's `work` trigger), TD-660.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — the live check holds (grinder-ao-2, read-only, `ao status --json`, `ao promote status`, the auditor's transcript, `gh pr list`). `ao-shiftlead-docs-audit-ao-1` (`seat: {trigger: prs, after: 10}`) was filled at 04:05:14Z, finished its turn at 04:06:04Z and sat idle with its run open. Its tenth merged PR after the fill was #1798 itself, at 05:22:43Z, so it came due mid-run under the code without the fix. The live copy moved to 16972df, which holds #1798, and the record then reads `restarts[-1]: {why: fill, at: 2026-10-15T06:10:24Z}`, `created: 06:10:24Z`, `seat_due: null`, `seat_count: {prs: 0, at: 06:15:24Z}`. The tick closed the idle, due seat and filled it, and the count starts again from the fill. Nobody pressed a Close this time. Paul's Close of test-audit at 03:52Z was the only way out before.

## TD-705: Build TD-702: the doing log keeps each doer's newest five beside the team's last fifty

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-702's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1803
**Status:** Done — built by #1803 (grinder-ao-1, 2026-10-14), read live by grinder-ao-2 on 2026-10-15. Before that read: `sessionorc.store.kept` is the store's and the page's one keep rule, and every listed test passes. To read once #1803 is live (`ao promote status`), a day after: the `doing_log` RPC's ao-grind ring (or the Repo page's Doing section, a headless GET) holds the auditors' newest lines (`ao-shiftlead-docs-audit-ao-1`, `ao-shiftlead-test-audit-ao-1`) beside the grinders' fifty, and the team card's chips name them.
**Location:** design §4.8 *the doing log*, §4.5 screen 11 *Doing*, §4.5a *team card: Answer needed / Doing* and *Repo page: doing filters*; `src/sessionorc/store.py` (`DoingLogStore`: its load, `append` and compaction), `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (the comment ~L736, `rpc_doing_log`'s docstring ~L854), `src/sessionorc/paths.py` (`doing_log_file`'s docstring), `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (`DOING_KEPT`), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (the `DOING_KEPT` import ~L298, the `doing` event's ring ~L3833), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html` (the Doing section's *i* text ~L100, which says *the last fifty*)

**Why:** TD-702's design. The ring kept a team's last fifty calls, and ao-grind's three busy members filled it in under a day, so the auditors' lines (31 in `doing.jsonl`) never showed.

**Fix:** this touches `src/sessionorc/**`, so the techlead reads it (§4.9b).
- **One keep rule**, `kept(ring, now, keep=50, per_doer=5, quiet_days=30) -> ring`, in `sessionorc` (beside `DoingLogStore`, whose constructor gains `per_doer` beside `keep`): the union of the ring's last `keep` and, for each `id` whose newest call is younger than `quiet_days`, its newest `per_doer`, in time order. The ring's append order is kept: *newest* is the latest position, and `at` is read only to judge quiet. An entry with no `id` is one doer of its own (`""`); one whose `at` cannot be read counts as quiet. `now` is the home's clock at load and at each `append` (the UI passes its own; a few seconds' difference is harmless). `DoingLogStore` applies it at load, on `append` and when it compacts `doing.jsonl`. The UI's copy of the ring (the `doing` event in `ui/app.py`, `del ring[:-DOING_KEPT]`) applies the same function, and `DOING_KEPT` and its import go. Every comment and docstring that says *the last fifty*, and `repo_part.html`'s *i* text, say *the last fifty and each doer's newest five*.
- **Nothing else changes**: `doing_log`, the `doing` event, `doing_rows` and `doing_chips` read the ring as they do. The feed is newest first, so a seldom doer's lines sit at their age.
- **Tests:**
  - three busy doers' 60 calls keep a fourth doer's 5 older ones;
  - a doer's 6th-newest call beyond the 50 goes;
  - a doer quiet for 30 days keeps nothing beyond the 50;
  - load, append and compaction agree, and a `doing.jsonl` written under the old rule loads with the quiet doers' lines back (the 31 auditor lines are in the file today);
  - an entry with no `id`, and one with a garbage `at`, are kept without a crash;
  - `tests/test_repo_facts.py`'s `test_the_doing_log_keeps_the_last_calls_per_team_and_compacts_its_file` (`keep=3, compact_at=8`) passes unchanged, since its `at` values (`str(i)`) are unreadable and so quiet; the `per_doer` tests write real instants (`now_iso()`'s form);
  - in `tests/test_ui_events_paths.py`, beside its `doing` event test, the UI's ring (`st.doing` in the stream, read back through its `groups` output) after a `doing` event equals the store's.

**Done when** an auditor that calls `ao doing` once a day stays in its team's feed and chips while busier members call hourly, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-702 (the design), TD-176 (the doing log), TD-700 (why the auditors also stopped writing).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — the live check holds (grinder-ao-2, read-only: `ao repo --json`, `ao promote status`, headless GETs of `/` and `/repo/shiftlead`, about 06:30Z, with #1803 live). ao-grind's ring holds 99 lines. At the read the team's last fifty reached back only to 04:16:10Z (04:18Z a few minutes later, as new lines came in), and every doer's newest five ride beside them. The auditors' lines older than the fifty are kept: test-audit's from 03:52Z and 2026-10-12, docs-audit's from 2026-10-13. Under the old rule none of these showed. The Repo page's Doing chips read *docs-audit-ao-1 (5)* and *test-audit-ao-1 (5)*, and the team card's Doing feed on `/` draws the auditors' lines at their age (21m, 2h, and the 10-13 ones). The read came within hours of the promote, not a day after. The ring had already passed fifty, so the per-doer rule was already what kept those lines.

## TD-702: The Doing feed keeps the team's last 50 lines, so a member that reports less often (an auditor) drops out of it within a day

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — built by TD-705 (#1803, live check #1810). Designed 2026-10-14 (the designer; no mockup: the feed's rows are drawn as before) — §4.8 *the doing log*: the team's last fifty calls and, beside them, each doer's newest five (the call's record `id`); a doer with no call in 30 days keeps nothing beyond the fifty. The feed is the kept calls in time order, newest first; the Repo page's chips offer every doer kept. One keep rule, in `sessionorc`, used by the host agent's ring and the UI's copy alike. Built by TD-705. Was: Open.
**Blocked by:** TD-705
**Location:** design §4.8 *the doing log*, §4.5a *team card: Answer needed / Doing*, *Repo page: doing filters*; `src/sessionorc/store.py` (`DoingLogStore`, `keep=50`), `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (`DOING_KEPT`, `doing_rows`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-14: *I do not see any "doing" entries from our auditors — lets make sure they report what they are doing.* They do report: `~/.shiftlead/doing.jsonl` holds 31 lines from the shiftlead auditors, the last at 2026-10-13T15:28:25Z. But the ring keeps a team's last 50 lines, and ao-grind's last 50 (from 2026-10-14T23:10Z) are the two grinders' and the techlead's alone: three busy members fill it in under a day, so a seat that runs every ten PRs is never seen. The filter chips (`doing_chips`) can only pick from what the ring kept.

**Fix:** decide what the feed keeps so every member is visible — e.g. the ring keeps each doer's newest few beside the team's last 50, or keeps per member — and how the feed and its chips draw a member whose newest line is old.

**Done when** the design says what the doing log keeps per member, and a build entry carries it.

**Related:** TD-700 (why the auditors also stopped writing), TD-176.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — built, and archived by the designer as the fallback (§4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*): its one build TD-705 (#1803) archived in #1810 without it. `sessionorc.store.kept` keeps the team's last fifty and each doer's newest five; the live check read the auditors' lines kept beside ao-grind's fifty, and the Repo page's chips name them.

## TD-713: `test_link.py`'s mail-across-the-link test races its own 2-second reconnect: the *unreachable* refusal is not raised on a slow runner

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (grinder-ao-2, a CI failure on #1810, a ledger-only PR)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `tests/test_link.py` (`test_mail_crosses_the_link_both_ways_and_a_wait_from_the_node_wakes_on_it`, ~L1024–1033)

**Why:** CI run 38693877522, test (3.12), on #1810: `tests/test_link.py:1032: Failed: DID NOT RAISE AgentError`. 1 failed and 2906 passed; 3.13 passed on the same commit. The test closes the node's link (`node._home_mux.close("the lid closed")`) with `link.BACKOFF_FIRST` and `BACKOFF_MAX` set to 2.0, then waits for the home to read it unreachable and makes two calls, a `msg` and a `get`. Only then does it expect `as_w.call("inbox")` to be refused as *unreachable*. On a slow runner those steps take longer than the 2-second backoff, the link is back first, and the `inbox` succeeds. The fix is in the test, not the link.

**Fix:** keep the link down until the refusal has been read. Either hold the reconnect (a backoff far longer than the steps, or a patched dial that waits on an event the test sets after the `pytest.raises`), or take the refusal before the home-side asserts. The test still checks the return afterwards (`until(... != "unreachable")`, `home_reachable`).

**Done when** the test cannot pass its *unreachable* step only by timing: with a sleep of 3 seconds put before the `inbox` call, it still raises.

**Related:** TD-463 (the CI flakes since 2026-10-03).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — grinder-ao-2. The cause was wider than the entry read: the node's dialer takes `first` and `top` once, when the node starts (`agent_link._dial_home`, under the fixture's 0.05 s / 0.2 s), so the test's 2.0 s patch held nothing. Measured: the backoff after the close was 0.05 s, and the refusal was read 0.107 s after it, so the test passed only while spawning the dial command took longer. Five tests in `tests/test_link.py` set the constants this way (holds of 1, 2, 2, 2 and 5 s). Each now calls `shut_the_lid(node, monkeypatch)`, which patches `link._dial_once` (looked up afresh on every redial) to wait on an event the test sets once it has read what it needs. A 3 s sleep before the `inbox` call still raises. All 67 tests pass, and the file runs in 68.6 s against 69.5 s on main.

## TD-672: `ao connect tailscale` fails on a home's first run: its one 15-second probe ends before Tailscale has fetched the first HTTPS certificate (about a minute live)

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (ao-connect, Paul's first `ao connect tailscale` on kmaster)
**Owner:** anchor
**Kind:** live-check #1730
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.7 `ao connect` (*The probe*); `src/shiftlead/connect.py` (`PROBE_AFTER`, `PROBE_WAIT`, `probe`, `connect_tailscale`)

**Why:** the first `tailscale serve --https=443` on a tailnet name has no certificate yet; tailscaled starts fetching one from Let's Encrypt (dns-01 through Tailscale's control plane, its `tls-cert-pending` health warning standing meanwhile) the moment the handler is added, and a rollback cancels that fetch. On kmaster, 2026-10-14, Paul ran `ao connect tailscale --allow eyecantell@github`: the handler was added at 09:14:41, the probe went out 10 s later with a 15 s budget, and failed with *lacking: route — the probe failed: https://kmaster.tailc00dac.ts.net did not answer (_ssl.c:1012: The handshake operation timed out)*. The rollback ran correctly (no `reach:`, *No serve config*). tailscaled's log shows the fetch started with the handler, was cancelled by the rollback (*context canceled*), started again at once and finished at 09:15:39; each attempt's DNS step took about 30 s, so an uninterrupted fetch would have needed 30–40 s, more than the probe's 25. Every new home meets this on its first run, and a person is told the route failed when it only needed to wait. A second run works, since the certificate is then cached.

**Fix:** the probe waits for a first certificate before it judges the route. Either `ao connect` asks tailscaled before probing (the `tls-cert-pending` health warning in `tailscale status --json`, or a `tailscale cert` of the name, which blocks until it has one, given `--cert-file`/`--key-file` in a scratch directory so it leaves no files behind; the design step checks that the warning shows in `status --json` during a fetch) and says *fetching the HTTPS certificate — the first can take a minute or two*; or the probe retries an answer that did not come, up to a bound of about three minutes, saying so. The design's §4.7 *The probe* names which, and the bound. A probe that answers with the wrong listener, or `421`, still fails at once. Test: a fake fetch that times out for the first few tries and then answers `route` passes inside the bound, and one that never answers fails at it, with the rollback.

**Done when** `ao connect tailscale` on a home whose tailnet name has never had a certificate succeeds on its first run.

**Related:** TD-648 (`ao connect`, archived: its live check passed on the second run), TD-646 (the design).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — ao-paul, with Paul. The live check passed on a new home's first run: kworker2 (a fresh install from the wheel of `ae210d0`, which contains #1730), whose tailnet name `kworker2-standard-pc-i440fx-piix-1996.tailc00dac.ts.net` had never had a certificate. Paul's `ao connect tailscale --allow eyecantell@github` printed *no answer yet (… handshake operation timed out): the first HTTPS certificate can take a minute or two — trying again for up to 3 minutes…*, then *ok: route — tailscale, https://kworker2-…ts.net, allows eyecantell@github* and the phone line. tailscaled's log: the ACME fetch started at 10:48:10 MDT (`tls-cert-pending`), its SetDNS took 32 s, and the certificate arrived at 10:48:43, 33 s, inside the 180 s bound. Afterwards `tailscale serve status` shows the 443 handler to `127.0.0.1:8766`, `settings.yml` keeps `reach:`, and `ao doctor route` reads ok. A first try had failed earlier for another reason: the Tailscale operator was set before `sudo tailscale up`, which cleared it; `ao connect` named the missing `--operator` step and rolled back before any handler was added, so no fetch had started, and the README's order (up, then operator) already says it.

## TD-718: `agent_tick`'s rule-6 declaration reading is marked by the settle clock, and no test would notice if it were not (#1811)

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1811–#1821)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`both()` in rule 6's `lane_seen` read: `for got, when in ((then, at), (tip, datetime.now(UTC))): TickMixin._settle(str(root), remote, got, when, fresh=False)`); `tests/test_lane_news.py` (`test_an_entry_still_settling_is_told_only_once_it_settles`), `tests/test_settle.py`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-15, mutating #1811 and running `tests/test_settle.py tests/test_lane_news.py tests/test_repo_facts.py` (63 passed unmutated) and then the 20 modules that name `lane_seen` or `_keep_running` (291 passed). Replacing the `TickMixin._settle(str(root), remote, got, when, fresh=False)` call in `both()` with `pass` still passes all of them. The one test that names rule 6 and settling hands `agent._repos[...]["ledger"]["entries"]` entries that already carry `settling` — the *checkout's* reading — so it exercises rule 8's `_lane_news` and `lane_matches`; the two readings `both()` builds (`then`, read at the declaration, and `tip`, read from the tip) come from `ledger_mod.entries_before`, which never writes a mark, and no test reads them. TD-710's own **Tests** list names *rule 6 tells a member of the entry only once it settles*; what is held is rule 8's news, not the declaration's `lane_seen` baseline. Without the marking, an entry still settling at the declaration is recorded in `lane_seen` as seen, and is then never told when it settles — the very case the call's comment says it is there for.

**Fix:** a test in `tests/test_lane_news.py` or `tests/test_settle.py` where a seat declares out of work while a ledger entry the clock records as settling is in its lane at the declaration (the record written through `settle.observe`, the entries read through `entries_before` in a git checkout), and after the window the seat is told it; it fails with the `_settle` call in `both()` removed.

**Done when** that test exists and fails with the call removed.

**Related:** TD-710, TD-707, #1811.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — grinder-ao-1. `test_an_entry_settling_at_the_declaration_is_told_by_a_first_write_after_it_settled` (`tests/test_lane_news.py`) commits two design-first entries to a git checkout, records TD-002 on the clock through `settle.observe` 12 minutes ago (settling for the built-in 5m), declares 10 minutes ago, and runs the first tick with the checkout's reading already settled. TD-002 is told once and `lane_seen` ends `[TD-001, TD-002]`. With the `_settle` call in `both()` replaced by `pass`, `then` is unmarked, so TD-002 is seen at the first write and no note goes (`assert 0 == 1`). The first shape tried, a first tick while the entry still settles, passes with the call removed: `work_mod.reread` prunes the marked id from the checkout's reading on the same tick. The call matters only when the first tick comes after the window ends.

## TD-707: A new `design-first` entry is pickable the moment it lands, so the person has no time to change it or add to it: a settle window per Kind, and a Hold

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (ao-paul, with Paul)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — Designed 2026-10-14 (the designer; no mockup: a row's mark and one button) — §4.4 *A new entry settles before it is pickable*: `settle:` per Kind in `settings.yml` and the repo's `.shiftlead.yml` (not `org.yml`: the home applies it and reads no `org.yml`), built-in `{design-first: 5m}`; the home's clock in `ledger_seen.json` from the first reading that holds the id, restarted by an edit while settling; a settling or held entry matches no lane and a claim on it is refused, `--force` too; **Hold** / **Release** on the Repo page and `ao td hold`, a person's own act (`PERSON_ONLY`); no Inbox row. Built by TD-710. Was: Open.
**Blocked by:** TD-710
**Location:** design §4.4 *Pickable is derived, never written* (L56), §4.8 *Choosing in a free-pick lane*, §5 (`org.yml`, `.shiftlead.yml`), §4.5a (Repo page ledger rows), §4.7 (`ao repo`, `ao progress claim`, a new `ao td hold`), §6 rule 8

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-14: *Lets talk about adding a wait for new TDs, Im thinking 5min default and we can use 10min. That way as new items are added, thoughts/changes that come to mind quickly are not too late to make changes.* And: *we would only want to require a settle on new items we generate. The idea is to give the user time to change their mind / add thoughts. Items from a designer should go immediately. Maybe … make a settle value available for all items (defaults to zero on all but design-first items, which default to 5min)?* The case that prompted it: TD-702 merged in #1792 at 2026-10-15T04:22Z, the designer opened its design (#1795) at 04:32Z and merged it at 04:40Z, while Paul was still deciding whether TD-702 was wanted at all (he had just said the feed *is just honest*). A ledger PR takes 10–15 minutes through the cadence, so a change made by PR cannot land inside a short window: the window has to be one in which the person can **hold** the entry, not one in which they must finish the edit.

**Fix** (agreed with Paul in the conversation; the designer writes it into the design):
- **`settle:`**, a map from `Kind` to a duration, in `org.yml` with a repo override in `.shiftlead.yml`, like a role's settings. Built-in default `{design-first: 5m}`; any Kind not listed settles 0. This repo sets `{design-first: 10m}`. Keyed on the entry's own `**Kind:**` line, so every reader decides from the entry alone, and the designer's builds (`Kind: build`) go at once.
- **The clock** starts when the home first sees the id on `origin/<default>` in its repo reading (recorded per repo by the home; `**Added:**` holds a date only). Until it runs out the entry is not pickable: `ao repo` and the Repo page show *settles in 7m*, and `ao progress claim` is refused with *settling until <time>* (`--force` does not pass it).
- **Hold**: while an entry settles, its Repo page row has a **Hold** button, and `ao td hold <id>` / `ao td hold <id> --release` does the same. The hold is the home's record, not a ledger edit, so it takes effect at once with no PR; it keeps the entry unpickable until released, or until the entry's text changes on `origin/<default>`, which ends the hold and starts the window again.
- **Not settled**: a decided board line, a red PR's work order, and every Kind the map leaves at 0. A `design-first` finding from an auditor or hunter settles too (accepted: it is a question the person may want a say on).
- To decide in the design: whether the person gets a quiet Inbox row when an entry starts settling, or the Repo page alone shows it.

**Done when** the design says the settle map, its clock, the Hold and its release, and what never settles, and build entries carry it.

**Related:** TD-702 (the case that prompted it), TD-693 / TD-696 (the home hands out ids, `ao td next`), TD-223 (pickable is derived).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — archived with its last build, TD-710 (live check of #1829 held; see its **Resolved:**).

## TD-710: Build TD-707: a new entry settles by its Kind before a lane may take it, and the person can hold it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-14 (the designer, building TD-707's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1829
**Status:** Done — Slice 1 built 2026-10-15 (grinder-ao-1): `sessionorc.settle` keeps `ledger_seen.json` (`paths.ledger_seen_file`) — `observe` records a fresh reading (a repo's first at the epoch; an edit while settling or held restarts the window and ends the hold, one after settling records the new `sig`), `mark` re-marks a carried reading, so a window ends on time — and `durations` layers the repo's `.shiftlead.yml` `settle:` over `settings.yml`'s over the built-in `{design-first: 5m}`. `ledger.entries` gives each entry `sig`; the tick's `_read_repo` marks every reading (`_settle`), and rule 6's reading at the declaration too; `lane_matches` reads `settling`/`held` as no lane's and `in_lanes` leaves them out of the rest. Slice 2 built 2026-10-15 (grinder-ao-1): `settle.hold` writes `held: {at, by}` on a settling entry's record and refuses a settled one, and a release settles the record at the epoch, so it is pickable at once; the home's `td_hold {repo, id, release}` (`agent_ids`, in `PERSON_ONLY` and `modes.HOME_EDITS`) marks the reading at once; `rpc_progress` refuses a declared claim on a settling or held entry before the lease, `--force` too (`settle.claim_refusal`); `ao td hold <id> [--repo] [--release]`, and `ao repo` says *settles in 7m* / *held 2h* after the owner and counts neither pickable. Slice 3 built 2026-10-15 (grinder-ao-1, #1829): the Repo page's row draws *settles in 7m* / *held 2h* with **Hold** / **Release** (`/api/ledger/hold` → `td_hold`), and `teamrun.lane_kinds` counts a withheld entry not pickable; the Settings page's **settle** field writes `set_settings {settle}` (the whole map; `{}` removes it) and each Repos card shows its `settle:`; `repoconfig` accepts and checks `settle:`; this repo's `.shiftlead.yml` carries `settle: {design-first: 10m}`. **Live check** once #1829 is live: read `~/.shiftlead/ledger_seen.json` for the next `design-first` entry filed here — `at` its landing, and no lane's claim on it for ten minutes (`ao repo` says *settles in …*) — and a designer's `build` entries claimed with no wait; a Hold is checked on a scratch home (done for #1829's UI check). Was: Open.
**Location:** design §4.4 *A new entry settles before it is pickable*, §4.7 `ao td hold` and `ao repo`, §4.8 *A claim is a lease*, §5 `settle:`, §6 rule 6, §4.5a *Repo page: Hold / Release on a settling entry* and *Settings page: settle*; `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (`entries`, `reading`, `lane_matches`, `in_lanes`), `src/sessionorc/paths.py` (beside `ids_file`), `src/sessionorc/agent_ids.py` (beside `rpc_td_next`), `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`PERSON_ONLY`), `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_progress`'s claim), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (rule 6's `lane_seen` ~L1353), `src/shiftlead/repoconfig.py`, `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`cmd_repo` ~L1710, a `cmd_td_hold` beside `cmd_td_next`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html`, the Settings page

**Why:** TD-707's design. TD-702 was designed and merged within 18 minutes of being filed, while Paul was still deciding whether he wanted it, and a ledger PR is too slow to stop that.

**Fix:** this touches `src/sessionorc/**`, so the techlead reads it (§4.9b). Slices, each its own PR:
1. **The clock and the reading** (`sessionorc`). `settle:` is read from `settings.yml` and the repo's `.shiftlead.yml` (the repo's wins key by key; built-in `{design-first: 5m}`; durations as `5m`, `1h`, `0`).
   - `ledger_seen.json` beside `ids.json` (`paths`), keyed by origin as `ids.json` is: `{<origin>: {<id>: {at, sig, held?}}}`, where `sig` is a hash of the entry's section text. It is written by the host agent beside the reading (the reader stays a pure function of the text), and a repo's first reading records every id it holds at the epoch. The agent annotates the reading's entries with the marks before any reader sees them, so `lane_matches` / `in_lanes` read them off the entry.
   - An entry that has not settled carries `settling: {until}`, and a held one carries `held: {at}`. An edit that changes `sig` while settling restarts the window, and on a held entry it ends the hold and restarts the window.
   - `lane_matches` / `in_lanes`, rule 6's `lane_seen` and rule 8's news, and every lane count treat either mark as matching no lane. `pickable` stays cadence §2.4's.
2. **Hold and the claim**. `td_hold {repo, id, release}` beside `td_next`:
   - Added to `PERSON_ONLY` (refused to every session, the person's shell passing; `tests/test_person_only.py`'s count of the list moves by one) and to `modes.HOME_EDITS` (a node forwards it and refuses it offline, as `ledger_decide`'s), and refused for an id that has settled and is not held. Release makes the entry pickable at once.
   - `rpc_progress`'s declared claim on a settling or held ledger reference is refused in the design's words, and `force` does not pass it.
   - `ao td hold <id> [--repo] [--release]`. `ao repo` prints *settles in 7m* / *held 2h* after the owner.
3. **The pages**. The Repo page's row draws the mark and **Hold** / **Release**, and the Settings page gets the **settle** field (`set_settings` gains `settle`). This repo's `.shiftlead.yml` gains `settle: {design-first: 10m}`.
- **Tests:** a new design-first entry is withheld for its window and pickable after it; a `build` entry goes at once; a repo's first reading settles every existing id; an edit inside the window restarts it, and an edit after settling does not; a hold withholds past the window until Release or an edit; a claim on a settling or held entry is refused with `--force` too; a session's `td_hold` is refused and the person's shell's passes; rule 6 tells a member of the entry only once it settles; the repo's `settle:` overrides the install's key by key; the §4.5a doc-bound tests pass.

**Done when** an entry filed `Kind: design-first` in this repo is untaken for ten minutes, a Hold pressed in that time keeps it untaken until Release, a designer's `Kind: build` entries are picked at once, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-707 (the design), TD-693 / TD-696 (`ids.json`, `td_next`), TD-223 (pickable is derived), TD-702 (the case).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-15 — grinder-ao-2, the live check of #1829 (live at a235a54, read-only). A `design-first` entry settled ten minutes: TD-722 (Kind design-first, filed by #1828) landed 18:44:52Z, and the home first told the designer's lane of it at 18:55:10Z (*your lane gained 1 entry … TD-722*, in the designer's transcript); the designer claimed it at 18:55:26Z (read from its record before its `done` on #1832 rewrote the line). A designer's `build` entries were picked at once: TD-724 (Kind build, filed by #1832, merged 19:30:02Z) read *pickable* in `ao repo` at 19:33Z with no *settles in*, as did TD-726 and TD-727 (#1833). A Hold and Release were pressed on a scratch home in #1829's UI check; the listed tests pass in CI.
