## TD-766: Build TD-761 (1): background shells read from the process tree — `ProcReader.children`/`cmdline`, the adapter's `background`, the record's `shells`/`shells_at`, `shells_live` in rules 3, 4 and 9

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (TD-761's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1905
**Status:** Built (#1905, 2026-10-16). `Monitor`'s task was checked: it is wrapped as a background shell is — a `bash -c source …/shell-snapshots/…` child of `claude`, its first child the script's command — so it is read and counted (§4.2). **What to read once #1905 is live** (`ao promote status`): an idle session of this host that ended its turn on a `run_in_background` command carries that task on its record (`ao --json status -v`, its `shells`, `cmd` the command) and reads `shells_live` true, and the list empties on the tick after the command ends. A read, no press; TD-767 draws it. **Read 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, live `102a5fd`, after #1905's `08b319e`), two of three parts hold.** Read from `ao --json status -v`, with no press. At 07:49Z `ao-shiftlead-designer-ao-1`, idle, carried one shell: `{pid: 2940010, start: 480558712, cmd: "sleep 10", since: 07:27:50Z}`, with `shells_live` true. That pid was the `bash -c source …/shell-snapshots/…` wrapper, a child of its `claude`, running an `until gh pr checks …; do sleep 10; done` loop, and `cmd` was the wrapper's current child. At 08:09Z it carried two shells, the first now with `cmd` `gh pr checks 1904 --watch --interval 30`. **Not yet read: the list emptied on the same record.** The designer was restarted (`wanted`) at 08:12:51Z, so the `shells: []` read at 08:12:54Z was a new record's, not the tick's clearing. What is left: a record whose background command ended, read once it is idle again with its `created` unchanged, shows `shells: []` and `shells_live` false. **Read 2026-10-16 08:33–08:40Z (grinder-ao-1, live `5d83316`, after #1905's `08b319e`): the third part holds, on one record.** `ao-shiftlead-grinder-ao-1` (`created` 08:32:08Z throughout) ended its turn on a `run_in_background` `sleep 60`; a detached watcher outside its process tree read `ao --json status -v` every ten seconds, with no press. Idle from 08:33:09Z it carried `shells: [{pid: 3542285, cmd: "sleep 60", since: 08:33:03Z}]`, `shells_live` true and `shells_at` moving each tick; at 08:34:00Z, woken by the command's end and `working`, the last reading was kept; idle again at 08:34:11Z the same record read `shells: []`, `shells_live` false, and `shells_at` held at 08:33:59Z, never moved back, through 08:39:40Z.
**Location:** design §4.2 *Working on its own* (*A background shell task*), §4.3 `background`, §6 rules 3, 4 and 9; `src/sessionorc/identity.py` (`ProcReader` ~L76, `LinuxProc` ~L84, and §4.8a's bounded walk); `src/shiftlead/adapters/claude_code/__init__.py` (`ClaudeCodeAdapter` ~L502, beside `context` ~L652); `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (a new `_refresh_shells` beside `_refresh_context` ~L173/~L3563; `_subagent_flips` ~L604; the rule sites reading `subagents_live` ~L1147, ~L1201, ~L2581, ~L2850; the *finished* dict ~L2031); `src/sessionorc/tmux.py` (`#{pane_pid}` in the pane list ~L21); `src/sessionorc/agent_common.py` (`subagents_live` ~L1048, `idle_from` ~L1059, `SEAT_PR_WAIT` ~L138); `src/sessionorc/agent_serve.py` (`_view` ~L71); `src/sessionorc/work.py` (~L197, ~L224); `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`NODE_OWNED` ~L66, the wake exclusions ~L708, the record's fields ~L957, the exit reset ~L1445)

**Why:** TD-761. A session idle on a background shell reads *ready to close ✓*; one Close kills the shell.

**Fix:**
- **`ProcReader`** gains `children(pid)` (from `/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children`, else by scanning `/proc/*/stat` for the `ppid`) and `cmdline(pid)`; `None` for a process gone or unreadable, never an error.
- **The adapter's `background(pid, proc)`**: Claude Code walks from `pid` to the first process, `pid` included, whose `comm` is the adapter's binary (`basename(self.binary)[:15]`, `comm`'s length; `claude` by default) (depth-bounded as §4.8a's walk; none is `None`), and returns its direct children whose argv is `bash -c` with `/shell-snapshots/` in the script, each `{pid, start, cmd}`, `cmd` the wrapper's first child's argv joined and cut to 120 characters. An MCP server child is never one. `shell` has no such method, and the tick finds it as it finds `context` (`getattr`). The build checks `Monitor`'s tasks against the wrapper and records the answer in this entry's Status and in §4.2.
- **`_refresh_shells(snapshot_at, panes)`**, called after `_refresh_context` in `tick()` (~L173) with the `panes` the tick already listed (`main_panes`), every tick: for each record of this host whose state is `idle`, attended or not, with no live subagent, and whose adapter has the method, read off the loop (`asyncio.to_thread`) with the pid `panes.get(s.id).pane_pid` (`panes` is keyed by the record id, its tmux session's name, as `_reconcile` reads it; a record with no pane there is not read); write `shells: [{pid, start, cmd, since}]` (`since` kept for a `pid`+`start` seen before) and `shells_at` (the last tick that read a shell within `SHELL_WAIT`, never moved back), saved on the loop as `_refresh_context` saves. Otherwise the last reading is kept. A record that turned `idle` by a hook between ticks is read on the next tick.
- **The record**: `shells` and `shells_at` on `Session`, in `NODE_OWNED`; named in the comment above `WAKE_FIELDS` (~L715) as excluded, which the allow-list already makes them; cleared where `subagents` is on exit (`set_state`, models ~L1445), which the tool's `SessionEnd` and every other exit path go through.
- **`SHELL_WAIT`** (two hours) beside `SEAT_PR_WAIT`; **`shells_live(record, now)`** beside `subagents_live`: a shell whose `since` is within it. `_subagent_flips` (agent_tick.py ~L604, its `seen[key] = live = …` line) keeps one dict (`_subagents_were`, declared in agent.py ~L731), now valued `subagents_live(r, now) or shells_live(r, now)`, and pushes when that combined *working on its own* reading flips; `agent.py`'s re-exports (~L123, ~L198) gain `SHELL_WAIT` and `shells_live`. The view (`_view`) and the *finished* dict carry `shells_live`, and `work.finished` reads it ("idle, shell live"). Rules 3 (seat close), 4 (idle nudge, and the `open` cause ~L2581) and 9 (*finished*) read it beside `subagents_live`, and `idle_from` takes the later of `since`, `subagent_at` and `shells_at`.
- **Tests** (in `tests/test_subagents_live.py`, `tests/test_identity.py` for the reader, `tests/test_claude_adapter.py`): a fake `ProcReader` with a wrapper child, an MCP child and a wrapper with a first child gives one task with that `cmd`; the walk finds `claude` under a hand-started shell and returns `None` with none; `children` falls back to `ppid`; the tick writes `shells` on an idle record, `[]` once the child is gone, keeps the last reading mid-turn and while a subagent is live, and clears it on exit; `shells_at` stops moving for a shell past `SHELL_WAIT`; `shells_live` flips push the record; a seat idle with a live shell is not closed, a member not nudged, a team not *finished*, and one past `SHELL_WAIT` is.

**Done when** an idle session's background shells are on its record and in its view, the rules read them as they read a live subagent, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-761 (the design), TD-767, TD-734.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, the live check; live `5d83316`, after #1905's `08b319e`) — it holds. An idle record carries its background shell (`shells`, `cmd` the command, `shells_live` true), keeps the reading mid-turn, and on the first tick after it is idle again with the command ended reads `shells: []` and `shells_live` false on the same record, `shells_at` not moved back (the Status's reads of 07:49Z, 08:09Z and 08:33–08:40Z).

## TD-765: A subscribe's omit is held by no test when it is said again, or when a send to it fails (#1886)

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1886)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_serve.py` (`_handle_conn`: `self._sub_omit.pop(writer, None)  # a subscribe again says its omit again`; `_send`: `self._sub_omit.pop(w, None)`); `tests/test_ui_repos_omit.py`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-16, mutating #1886's (TD-754) lines one at a time and running `tests/test_ui_repos_omit.py tests/test_ui_counts.py tests/test_ui_fanout.py tests/test_ui_events_light.py tests/test_ui_events_paths.py` (47 pass unmutated; main's venv, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src`). Four mutations fail a test (the `_handle_conn` cleanup pop, `CountsKeeper`'s `omit=`, `fan_seed`'s memo omit, the client's `omit or None`). Two pass all 47: (1) the `_handle_conn` pop on a subscribe again deleted — the comment says *a subscribe again says its omit again*, so a connection that subscribes a second time with no `omit` must be sent `repos` events whole, and with the line gone it keeps the first subscribe's omit; no test subscribes twice on one connection. (2) the `_send` failure path's `self._sub_omit.pop(w, None)` deleted — a send that fails drops the subscriber, and its omit must go with it; no test fails a send.

**Fix:** in `tests/test_ui_repos_omit.py`, (1) one connection that sends `subscribe` with an `omit` and then `subscribe` without: the second seed and the next `repos` event after it are whole; (2) a subscriber whose writer raises `ConnectionError` on `_send`: `agent._sub_omit` is empty after. Each fails under its mutation above.

**Done when** the two tests exist and fail under those mutations.

**Related:** TD-754, #1886.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1) — `tests/test_ui_repos_omit.py` gains `test_a_subscribe_again_on_one_connection_without_an_omit_is_sent_repos_whole` (one connection subscribes with an `omit`, then without: the second seed and the next `repos` event are whole) and `test_a_send_that_fails_drops_the_subscriber_and_its_omit` (a writer raising `ConnectionError` on a broadcast leaves neither `_subscribers` nor `_sub_omit` holding it). Each fails under its mutation: the `_handle_conn` pop replaced by `pass`, and the `_send` failure path's `_sub_omit.pop` deleted.

## TD-774: The anchor-record retirement's three branches — a suspended record skipped, a node's record removed over its link, a scheduled start cancelled — are held by no test (#1900)

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1900)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_retire_anchors`); `tests/test_anchor_retired.py`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-16, mutating #1900's (TD-757) `_retire_anchors` one line at a time and running `tests/test_anchor_retired.py tests/test_no_anchor_seat.py tests/test_agent.py tests/test_link.py tests/test_models.py tests/test_manager_on_call.py` (6 `test_link.py` tests fail in this worktree unmutated, for a reason outside the PR; the count is 6 before and after each mutation below, so each of these passes every test that passes unmutated). Mutations that fail a test: `clean = True`, and the `exited and not clean` skip. Three that do not: (1) `and not r.suspended` removed from the selection — the docstring says *a suspended one is the person's (§4.8a) and never forgotten here*, and no test suspends an anchor record; (2) `await self._route_act("remove", {"id": s.id}, None, s.host)` replaced by `pass` — a node's anchor record is never removed, and no test has one (the docstring promises *a node's removed*); (3) `if s.state == "scheduled" and s.host == self.host:` replaced by `if False:` — `await self._cancel_start(s)` is never called, and the existing scheduled case (`test_the_tick_forgets_a_closed_anchor_record...`, `e-anchor`) still passes because the fall-through forgets the record anyway, so it does not say the start was cancelled (a pending timer could still fire into a forgotten record).

**Fix:** in `tests/test_anchor_retired.py`: (1) a suspended anchor record, idle and clean, is still in `agent.sessions` after `_retire_anchors`; (2) a node's anchor record in `agent.remote` with its link present: the `remove` act is routed to that host, and with the link down the record stays; (3) the scheduled case asserts the start's timer is cancelled (`_cancel_start` called, or no start task remains). Each fails under its mutation above.

**Done when** the tests exist and fail under those three mutations.

**Related:** TD-757, #1900.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1) — `tests/test_anchor_retired.py` gains `test_a_suspended_anchor_record_is_the_persons_and_never_forgotten` (a suspended, closed, clean anchor record stays), `test_a_nodes_anchor_record_is_removed_over_its_link_and_left_while_the_link_is_down` (a node's closed anchor record: nothing routed while its link is down, then `remove` routed to that host once it is up) and `test_a_scheduled_anchor_records_start_is_cancelled` (`_cancel_start` is called on it). Each fails under its mutation: `and not r.suspended` removed, the `_route_act` line replaced by `pass`, the scheduled branch's test replaced by `if False:`.

## TD-767: Build TD-761 (2): the pages — Ready to close's *no background shells running*, *working · 1 shell* on the pill and the slot

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (TD-761's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1916
**Status:** Resolved — built by #1916 (grinder-ao-2, 2026-10-16): the Ready to close row (*no background shells running*, failing with the oldest shell's `cmd`, or past `SHELL_WAIT` its age and *stop it in the session, or Close kills it*), *working · 1 shell* on the pill (joined with live subagents, never *0 subagents*), the slot naming the oldest shell and its age, and on the person's own session *more ▾ → Close* with *Close kills: …* when that stale shell is the only failing row (card and Focus). **Live check** once #1916 is live (`ao promote status`), read-only: a Claude Code session idle on a `run_in_background` task — the next one a member or the person leaves, read with a headless GET of `/` and of its Focus — reads *working · 1 shell* with the slot naming the shell, and its Ready to close shows *✗ 1 background shell running — <cmd>* with no *ready to close ✓*; the same session once the shell ends reads the row ✓.
**Location:** design §4.2 (*Working on its own*, the Ready to close list), §4.5 (*working* on its own), §4.5a *Close session*; `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`ready_to_close` ~L1097, the pill ~L378, the slot's ending ~L565, ~L1022), the card's and Focus's *more ▾*

**Why:** TD-761. The read is useless until the card and Ready to close say it.

**Fix:**
- **Ready to close** gains *no background shells running* after *no subagents running*, failing while `shells` holds one: *1 background shell running — <cmd>* (the oldest's `cmd`, cut). *ready to close ✓* and **Close session** follow it, as every row does.
- **The pill** (cards.py ~L378): an idle record with the view's `subagents_live or shells_live` and nothing waiting is *working*, its ending joining the parts that are live, *working · 1 shell*, *working · 2 subagents*, *working · 2 subagents · 1 shell* (never *0 subagents*), the shell count `len(shells)`. The `own_work` text reused at ~L566 and ~L1025 (*its own subagents running*) says shells too.
- **The slot's ending** names the oldest shell: *working · 1 shell: <cmd> · 4m*.
- **A shell past `SHELL_WAIT`** is the view's `shells` non-empty with `shells_live` false; its age is from the oldest `since`, with `now` passed to `ready_to_close` as a new `now=None` parameter by `card()` (~L524), from the clock the card builder already reads. The row (label prefix *background shell*, which the card tests to know it is the only failing row) reads *1 background shell running 3h — stop it in the session, or Close kills it*; on the person's own session, when that is the only failing row, *more ▾* offers **Close** with a confirm naming the shell (§4.5a *Close session*). The gate is the page's alone: `ready_to_close` has no server-side caller to relax (it is read at cards.py ~L524).
- **Tests** (in `tests/test_ui_org.py` beside `ready_to_close`'s own, and `tests/test_subagents_live.py` for the pill): the row fails with a shell and passes without; *ready to close ✓* and Close are withheld while one runs; the pill and slot words, with 0 subagents and 1 shell; a shell past `SHELL_WAIT` still fails the row with its words, and the own session's *more ▾* Close and its confirm appear only then.

**Done when** a session idle on a background shell reads *working · 1 shell*, Ready to close names the shell and fails, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-761, TD-766, TD-734.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, live `3a19eb0`, after #1916's `803bbee`) — **it holds.** Read with no press: a detached watcher outside the session's process tree polled `ao --json status -v` every 15 s and, for each idle record carrying `shells`, a headless GET of `http://127.0.0.1:8765/focus/<id>`, reading the view's `pill_word`, `own_work`, `wait_reason`, `ready`, `ready_ok` and `shell_close`. At 10:39:01Z `ao-shiftlead-grinder-ao-1`, idle on `timeout 1200 gh pr checks 1917 --watch` (`shells_live` true, nothing waiting), read pill *working*, `own_work` *working · 1 shell*, the row *✗ 1 background shell running — timeout 1200 gh pr checks 1917 …*, `ready_ok` false and no `shell_close`. At 10:39:16Z `ao-shiftlead-grinder-ao-2`, idle on its own `run_in_background` `sleep 240` with a steer to Paul open, read pill *waiting* (the wait outranks *working*, §4.2 *One order*) and the row *✗ 1 background shell running — sleep 240*. At 10:42:53Z grinder-ao-1's shell was `python3 scripts/check_cadence.py --pr 1917` and its row read *1 background shell running — python3 …*: the cut drops a word that ends exactly at `SHELL_CMD_CUT`, filed as TD-778. A shell past `SHELL_WAIT` was not seen live (none ran two hours); its row and *more ▾ → Close* are held by the tests and #1916's UI check.

**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — Designed (2026-10-15, the designer): §4.2 *Working on its own* — a background shell is read from the process tree by the adapter's `background` (Claude Code: the `claude` process's `shell-snapshots` command-wrapper children, `cmd` the wrapper's first child), into the record's `shells` and `shells_at` on the tick, with no reset or bound needed since a reading is of what is there now; the pill reads *working · 1 shell*, Ready to close gains *no background shells running* (so *ready to close ✓* and **Close session** wait), and `shells_live` (within `SHELL_WAIT`, two hours) holds §6 rules 3, 4 and 9 as a live subagent does. Built by TD-766 (the read and the rules) and TD-767 (the pages).
**Blocked by:** TD-766, TD-767
**Location:** design §2 goal 11 (`docs/design/2-goals.md`); §4.2 *Working on its own* (`docs/design/4.2-state-feed.md`, *A background shell task … fires no hook and is not read*); `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`ready_to_close`); the Claude Code adapter under `src/shiftlead/adapters/claude_code/`

**Why:** 2026-10-15, 22:56 MDT. Paul's own session `ao-paul` ended its turn on a background Bash call (`sleep 20; timeout 1200 gh pr checks …`, *Running in the background*), waiting on CI before the cadence check and the merge. Claude Code's own footer read *1 shell still running* and *1 shell*. ShiftLead's pill read *IDLE*, the header read ***ready to close ✓***, and the Ready to close card passed all six rows (*agent not working (turn ended)*, tree clean, branch pushed, no subagents running, outcomes reported, mail read), with **Close session** offered. One press would have killed the CI wait and the merge after it. Goal 11 says the checklist includes *no subagents or background tasks running*, but §4.2 says a background shell task *fires no hook and is not read*. TD-734/TD-743 left it to an `ao doing` line, which the role briefs ask of unattended members. A person's own interactive session has no brief, and an `ao doing` line does not stop a Close anyway. The check is missing exactly on the sessions where Close is the next act offered (§4.5a *Close session*: the person's own session).

**Fix:** a design round first, since §4.2 rejects reading it today. Options the round weighs: (1) the adapter counts background tasks from the hooks it already gets: a `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` of `Bash` with `run_in_background`, or `Monitor`, opens one, and the round finds what closes it (the tool's task-end notification, a `BashOutput`/`KillShell` result, the process ending), reset as the subagent count is (`subagents_reset`); (2) the host agent reads the agent process's descendants for a live shell that is not an MCP server or the tool's own helper; (3) a scraped read of the tool's footer (*n shell*), advisory as every scraped read is. Whatever reads it, Ready to close gains a row, *no background shells running*, that fails while one runs. The round also decides whether the pill and the slot draw it as *working* (as §4.2 does for subagents) and how the count is bounded, so a lost end never holds a session unready for good.

**Done when** the design says how a background shell task is read and what Ready to close and the card do with it, its build entries are filed, and this entry's `Blocked by:` names them; a session idle on a background shell no longer reads *ready to close ✓*.

**Related:** TD-734, TD-743 (subagents read, background shells left to `ao doing`), TD-079 (the checklist's outcome row).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 — archived with its last build, TD-767 (TD-766 by #1905, its live check #1911; TD-767 by #1916, its live check #1920; see their **Resolved:**).

## TD-731: The person cannot hold a settled entry: a hold is only a settling entry's, so an entry that settled before the person looked is in a lane with no press to stop it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — Designed (2026-10-15, the designer): §4.4 *Hold*, *A claimed entry is held all the same*, *An entry can land held*; §4.5 screen 6; §4.5a *Repo page: Hold / Release on an entry*, *Inbox row: held entry*; §4.7 `ao td hold`, `ao td next --held`. A hold ends only at Release (an edit no longer ends it); a hold on a claimed entry mails each unattended lease holder to stop and drop it. Built by TD-735 (the home and the CLI) and TD-736 (the pages).
**Blocked by:** TD-735, TD-736
**Location:** `docs/design/4.4-host-agent.md` (*A new entry settles before it is pickable*: *Hold*, *A claimed entry is held all the same*, *An entry can land held*); `docs/design/4.5a-controls.md` (*Repo page: Hold / Release on an entry*, *Inbox row: held entry*); `docs/design/4.7-cli.md` (`ao td hold`, `ao td next --held`); `src/sessionorc/settle.py` (the hold and its refusal)

**Why:** 2026-10-15. TD-722 (`design-first`) merged at 12:44 MDT while Paul and an interactive session were still reviewing its proposal with Fable. It settled at 12:54, and Paul's `ao td hold TD-722` at about 12:56 was refused: *TD-722 has settled, and a hold is a settling entry's … take a settled entry out of a lane with its Blocked by: line*. designer-ao-1 designed it as #1832 by 13:30. Its build TD-724 (`Kind: build`, which settles 0 minutes) was claimed at once and under review as #1840 before the round's findings were adopted, and had to be stopped by hand. A `Blocked by:` line is a PR: minutes at best, and only after the person has a session write it. So the window is the person's only press, and a build has none.

**Fix:** a design round, Paul's direction (2026-10-15):
1. **The person may hold any unclaimed entry, settled or not**: the same `held: {at, by}` record, the same Hold and Release on the Repo page row (now on every pickable row, not only a settling one) and `ao td hold`. A held entry is withheld until Release or until its `sig` changes, as now.
2. **A claimed entry** is refused with its holder's name, since a hold does not take a lease. The person's way there is the claimer's manager or the claimer. Or, the round decides, the hold also asks the claimer to drop it.
3. **An entry filed during a conversation with the person** (Add entry from a session working with the person, `ao td add` with a flag) may land held, so the conversation ends before any lane looks.

**Done when** the design says when the person may hold an entry, what a hold on a claimed entry does, and how an entry can land held; its build entries are filed; and this entry's `Blocked by:` names them.

**Related:** TD-707, TD-710, TD-722, TD-724, TD-730.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 — archived with its last build, TD-736 (TD-735 by #1861; TD-736 by #1873; see their **Resolved:**).

## TD-745: A draft PR paused on the person's word reads as *a red PR nobody holds*, a High work order in the anchor's lane

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (the anchor, found reading its lane)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — Designed (2026-10-15, the designer): §4.4 *A red PR nobody holds is a work order* — a draft is no work order (no order, no note, no Inbox row), ready again it is under the rule at once; `ao repo`, the Repo page's tag and the facet's hover say *no order while a draft*; a draft `is_sync_order` orders is still an order. Built by TD-750.
**Blocked by:** TD-750
**Location:** design §4.4 *A red PR nobody holds is a work order*; `teamrun.red_prs`

**Why:** on 2026-10-15 `ao repo` listed #1840 (TD-724's build) and #1850 (TD-722's amendment) as `pr:1840` and `pr:1850`, both High, both *red since …: conflicting*, first in the anchor's lane. Both are drafts that Paul paused in an interactive session. #1840 waits for the amendment, and #1850 is held until its Fable and Sonnet rounds converge (memory `hold-a-design-until-its-round-ends`). The rule's cure, a rebase on the PR's own branch, would reach into a design under the person's review, so the anchor passed over both and named why in its `ao doing` line. Every anchor run until they land will read them first and pass over them again. The rule reads `isDraft` (§4.4, the PR list's fields) but never uses it for an order; §4.4 says a draft only for a sync PR.

**Fix:** a design decision first. A draft is no work order (or one only past a longer bound), or a paused PR names its holder (a `Paused:` line in its body, a label) and the reading counts that as held. Either way, `ao repo` says why it does not list the PR.

**Done when** a draft PR the person paused is not a pickable `pr:<n>` in any lane, and the design says what makes it so.

**Related:** TD-613 (the rule), TD-722, TD-724.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 — archived with its build, TD-750 (#1883; see its **Resolved:**).

## TD-778: A shell's `cmd` cut exactly at a word's end loses that word: *python3 scripts/check_cadence.py --pr 1917* is drawn *python3 …* (#1916)

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, TD-767's live check)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`shell_cmd`, `SHELL_CMD_CUT`); `tests/test_ui_org.py`

**Why:** TD-767's live read, 2026-10-16 10:42:53Z: grinder-ao-1's background `python3 scripts/check_cadence.py --pr 1917` read *1 background shell running — python3 …* on Ready to close and the slot. `shell_cmd` takes the first `SHELL_CMD_CUT` (32) characters and drops the last partial word with `rsplit(" ", 1)`; `python3 scripts/check_cadence.py` is exactly 32 characters, so the whole word that ends at the cut is dropped as if it were partial, and the row names nothing a person can recognise.

**Fix:** in `shell_cmd`, keep `head` whole when the character after it is a space (the cut lands at a word's end); drop the partial word only otherwise. A test in `tests/test_ui_org.py` beside the shell tests: `python3 scripts/check_cadence.py --pr 1917` → *python3 scripts/check_cadence.py …*; a cut inside a word still drops it (*timeout 1500 gh pr checks 1893 …*).

**Done when** a word ending at the cut is kept and the test passes.

**Related:** TD-767, TD-761.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2) — `shell_cmd` keeps `head` whole when the character after the cut is a space, and drops the partial word only otherwise; `tests/test_ui_org.py::test_a_shells_cmd_cut_at_a_words_end_keeps_the_word` holds *python3 scripts/check_cadence.py …* (32 characters, the word kept), *timeout 1500 gh pr checks 1893 …* (a cut inside a word), a 40-character word cut at 32, and a short `cmd` whole. Fails under the old `rsplit` alone.

## TD-724: Build TD-722 (1): one repo per team — `repo:` on a team, a project a heading on repos, the badge, the Project block, names unique per repo, the old keys refused

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (the designer, building TD-722's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1910
**Status:** Done. Built — slices 1–3 by #1840 (grinder-ao-2, 2026-10-16), rebased onto TD-757 and brought to the amendment: `repo:` on a team and one store of checkouts, a project a heading, `projects:` and every `home:` refused by name with their fix (no release of warnings), `repo:` in a repo's file refused, a name two teams on one repo start refused naming both (`org._names_per_repo`, at load, `ao org check` and every start), `ao team list` and `ao org` carrying `repo` and `project`; slice 4 by #1910: no `ao new --project` and no Project picker, a hand-started session's badge and Project block read from its directory's repo (`teams.repo_here`, `reach_block`). A nested `{team: …}` member in the org file is still read; the design refuses it, and TD-775 removes it. **Live check** once #1910 is live (`ao promote status`), read-only: `ao team list --json` and `ao org --json` carry `repo` and `project` for every team and no `projects`; `ao org check` names no old key and no name two teams give; the Org page's strip draws no *a definition could not be read*; `ao status -v --json`: a session started by hand since the promote, in a registered repo, carries its repo's project as `project` **Read 2026-10-16 09:40Z (grinder-ao-1, live `a6968f4`, #1910's merge, live since 09:16:57Z), no press: three of four parts hold.** `ao team list --json` and `ao org --json` carry `repo` and `project` for each of the four teams (ao-grind shiftlead, cm-grind contractmatch, dc-grind dev-cadence, samscrape-grind samscrape) and no `projects` key anywhere in `ao org --json`, whose `refused`, `shadowed`, `unread`, `notes` and `held_elsewhere` are empty; `ao org check` says *ok: 4 teams* and exits 0; a headless GET of the Org page (`/`, 200) holds no *a definition could not be read*. **Not yet read:** a hand-started session's `project` — it is written at `create` (`cli.py`'s `_repo_reach`), and no session has been started by hand since the promote: the two records that carry `project` empty, `ao-paul` and `ao-queue-vs-inbox`, are attended ones made before it, and every record made since (`grinder-ao-2` 09:17:44Z, `test-audit-ao-1` 09:38:35Z) is an unattended team member's, `project` shiftlead. The next one is read from `ao status -v --json`
**Location:** design §4.9 *Projects*, *Teams*, *A definition written before TD-722*, *Home and reach*, *The org is an aggregate*, §4.10 *across teams, by project*, §4.5a *Add entry form: Hand to the techlead*, §5 `org.yml`; `src/shiftlead/org.py` (`TeamDef.projects` ~L184, `ManagerDef`/`TechleadDef`/`SeatDef`/`MemberDef.home`, `MANAGER_KEYS` ~L628, `MEMBER_KEYS`, `TEAM_KEYS` ~L631, `TECHLEAD_KEYS`, `SEAT_KEYS`, `_project` ~L580, `_team` ~L675, `_validate` ~L858, `_home` ~L903, `team_repos` ~L273, `merge_repo_teams` ~L338, `_land` ~L415), `src/shiftlead/teams.py` (`project_of` ~L214, `project_block` ~L222, `reach_block` ~L244, `entry_teams` ~L481, `_launch` ~L784, `plan` ~L971), `src/shiftlead/teams.py` (the other readers of `team.projects` and `.home`, ~L330, ~L344, ~L352, ~L492, ~L541, ~L868), `src/shiftlead/ui/common.py` (~L757, ~L775, which read `t.projects`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/group_head.html` (~L20, `g.projects`), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`repo_teams` ~L383), `src/shiftlead/teamrun.py` (`rows` ~L457), `src/shiftlead/orgcheck.py` (`view` ~L100), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`cmd_team_list` ~L1072), `src/shiftlead/ui/settings_page.py` (`org_cards` ~L481)

**Why:** TD-722's design, as amended 2026-10-15 (§4.9 *Teams*, *Names are the org's*, *A definition written before TD-722*, *Home and reach*; §4.9b *No anchor seat*). A team that may span projects leaves its repo to be read from where its members sit, and that inference is what leaves the Org header's *mixed* place, `repo_teams`' first-team rule and a Repo page that can expand only one team (TD-721).

**Fix:** this touches no `src/sessionorc/**` (the badge stays a plain string there, and `mail.message_edge` is unchanged). Slices, each its own PR:
1. **The definition** (`org.py`).
   - `TeamDef.repo` (one name) replaces `TeamDef.projects`. `home` leaves every `*_KEYS` set and dataclass, `TEAM_KEYS` gains `repo`, and `_home` goes. In the org file `repo:` is required and resolves through a project's repos or the registry's directory names. In a repo's `.shiftlead.yml` it is that repo: `merge_repo_teams` writes it in place of `raw["projects"] = [rname]`, and a written `repo:` there is refused outright, as `host:` is. `repo:` resolves to a path in §4.9's order: the listing project's path for the host, else the host registry's one entry of that name (`_land`), else refused in `_land`'s words.
   - `Project` gains an optional `title`. A repo listed by two projects is an error naming both, at load.
   - **No synthetic project.** `merge_repo_teams` stops creating `Project(rname, …)` for a repo-defined team (~L382), since under the new check a repo-defined team's repo listed by a heading (TD-723's samscrape under `contractmatch`) would be in two projects. A repo in no project is its own heading with no `Project` object.
   - **One store of checkouts.** `Org.checkouts: {repo: {host: path}}` is filled from every project's `repos:` and from each repo-defined team's registered checkout, and is carried by every `Org(...)` copy (`merge_repo_teams` ~L354, `with_repos` ~L508) as `projects` is. A project's `repos:` stays its list of names for the heading and the block. `Org.checkout(repo, host)` (today `checkout(project, repo, host)`, ~L267) reads it, and so do `teams.py`'s launch and start checks (~L330, ~L541, and the *declared on* words of its no-checkout error ~L544), `entry_teams` (~L492), `reach_block` (~L255), `project_block` (~L229) and `_land` (~L430–L461). `_land` keeps its rule: a path the org file already gives for the landing host is used as it stands. It writes the landed path into `Org.checkouts`. Its *not landed* words become *add `{host}: <path>` under `projects.<project>.repos.<repo>`* where a heading lists the repo, and *register the checkout on `{host}`* (§5 *Repos*) where none does.
   - `Org.project_of(repo)` returns the listing project's name, else the repo's own name. `team_repos` becomes `[team.repo]` (§4.9c's `held:` is that one repo's). `_land` reads `team.repo`.
   - **Names are unique per repo.** At load, every session name the teams on one repo start (managers, techleads, seats, members with their count suffixes) is collected, and a name two teams give is an error naming both teams and the name, in `org.load`, `ao org check` and every start.
2. **The old keys** (`org.py`, `orgcheck.py`, `repoconfig.py`). A team carrying `projects:` or any `home:` is **refused by name**, the message saying the fix in §4.9's words (*write `repo: shiftlead`*; *guardians spans … — split it*). An `anchor:` on a team or at a repo file's top level is refused as **retired** (*the anchor seat is gone — delete the key*), except `anchor: false`, which is read and passed over silently. No release of warnings. `ao org check` lists each one.
3. **What reads a team's repo** (`teams.py`, `ui/app.py`, `teamrun.py`, `cli.py`, `settings_page.py`).
   - `project_of` is the repo's project. `project_block` lists the project's repos and marks the team's.
   - `repo_teams` and `entry_teams` map a checkout to the teams whose `repo:` is it, in definition order. The hand-to target is the first of them with a techlead seat.
   - `ao team list --json` carries `repo` and `project` (dropping `projects` and `anchor`), and `ao org` likewise. The Settings org card's row reads *repo*.
   - `team_repo` (`ui/org.py`, the inference) stays only for a badge no definition holds; TD-725 removes its other callers.
4. **No `--project`** (`cli.py`, `ui/app.py`, the New session form). `ao new --project` and the form's **Project** picker go; a hand-started session in a registered repo gets its repo's badge and Project block from its directory (`project_of`, `reach_block`), as a team session does. The tests that pin the flag and the picker (`grep -ln -- "--project\|Project picker\|project=" tests/`: `test_cli.py`, `test_ui_teams.py`, `test_cli_teams.py`, `test_prompt_from.py`, `test_notify.py`, `test_watch.py` — the last three may only pass `project` through a record) are rewritten or removed.

## TD-725: Build TD-722 (2): the Org page grouped project → repo → team — headings in file order, the Repo facet on the repo's line, a no-team strip per repo, *No repo*

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (the designer, building TD-722's design)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Resolved
**Location:** design §4.9 *The Org page*, §4.5 screen 1 (the team's header), §4.5a *Org: team groups*; `src/shiftlead/ui/repo.py` (`team_groups` ~L450, its `projects` from badges ~L522 and ~L567, `group_place` use ~L576), `src/shiftlead/ui/cards.py` (`group_place` ~L1150), `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (`team_repo` ~L60, `team_summary` ~L452), `src/shiftlead/ui/repo.py` (`compact_in` ~L366), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/group_head.html` (~L15), the Org page's template and its ordering

**Why:** TD-722's design. With a team's repo declared, the Org page can say what it groups: project headings over repos over teams, two teams on one repo two whole cards, and no *mixed* place.

**Fix:** design §4.9 *The Org page* as amended 2026-10-15, §4.5 screen 1, §4.5a *team groups*, *team card: summary*, *team card: Repo facet*.
- **Headings** in the org file's order: each project (its `title`, else its name) with its repos in its list's order, then the repos no project lists, in the registry's order. A project of one repo draws one heading, the repo's. Headings do not fold.
- **Under each repo**, in order:
  - **the repo's line**: its name linked to `/repo/<name>`, and the **Repo facet**, moved off the team card (`team_summary`'s `repo` facet becomes the repo line's, drawn once; `drawn_facets` and the stopped-team rule keep two facets on a team card). Its lanes *i* carries the repo's lanes, one line per servicing team (`teamrun.repo_lanes` over the teams, `ledger.in_lanes` for each); a team card's own lanes line is the *i* beside its TDs in motion heading. The Repo facet's entries selector is remembered per repo.
  - **its teams' cards**: the live and concluded first, then those with nothing live, each in definition order within its kind; two teams on one repo two whole cards.
  - **a no-team strip**, headed *n sessions, no team*: the full cards of the repo's sessions with no team badge.
- **A heading or repo line hides** when the filter hides everything under it. **The ring** runs repo line → team cards → no-team strip.
- **A registered repo with no team** is drawn as its line and Repo facet.
- **Top and bottom**: the person's row and, only where `director:` is defined, the director's card in a row of its own (TD-642 writes the seat), no Start or Wind down on it; at the end **No repo**, the sessions in no registered repo (the old *No team*, renamed in the template and the filter's words).
- **A team's repo is its `repo:`** (TD-724). A `team` badge no definition holds is drawn under the repo its records sit in, which is `team_repo`'s one remaining use. `team_summary` and `compact_in` read the definition's repo.
- **The team header's place** is the host alone: `group_place` returns the host, *mixed* where members' hosts differ, and the repo goes from it.
- **Unchanged:** the fold, the counts, every other mark and control, the cards, and the rollup.
- **Tests:**
  - Two teams on one repo are two groups under one repo line, and the Repo facet is drawn once, on the line.
  - Two repos of one project are under one heading with its `title`; a project of one repo draws one heading.
  - Headings follow the org file's order; within a repo the live team precedes the stopped one.
  - A repo in no project is its own heading, after the projects; a registered repo with no team draws its line and facet.
  - A session in a repo with no team badge is in that repo's no-team strip; one in no registered repo is under *No repo*.
  - The header's place has no repo (`tests/test_ui_org.py`'s `test_the_header_says_where_once_and_counts_by_state_and_no_team_says_its_count`, rewritten).
  - An undefined badge's group is under its records' repo.
  - A heading, and a repo line, hide when the filter hides everything under them, and show again with the first match.
  - The ring runs repo line → team cards → no-team strip.
  - The director's card is drawn only where `director:` is defined.
  - `g` then a digit counts *No repo* where it sits.

**Done when** the Org page draws every team under its repo and every repo under its heading in the org file's order, the Repo facet once per repo on its line, two teams on one repo stand side by side as whole cards, a repo's teamless sessions sit in its strip and the rest under *No repo*, no header says *mixed* for a repo, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-722 (the design), TD-724 (the definition), TD-721 (the Repo page as the repo group expanded), TD-642 (the director's card).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2) — `ui/repo.py`'s new `org_layout` draws the Org page from `team_groups`' groups: project headings in the org file's order (`title`, else the name; a project of one repo draws no heading of its own, its repo's line being the heading), then the repos no project lists in the registry's order; under each repo its line (`repo_line.html`: the name, *open →*, and the Repo facet, now `repo_facet.html`, drawn once, its lanes *i* one line per team), its teams (live and concluded first, then nothing live, each in definition order — `team_groups` gives each group its `repo` and `order`), and a no-team strip *n sessions, no team*; then a team whose repo is told nowhere, and *No repo* last. No team card draws the Repo facet (`summary.drawn` leaves it out; the Repo page and the rollup still read `summary.repo`). `team_summary` and `compact_in` read the definition's repo (`repo_named`), `team_repo` only for a badge no definition holds; `group_place` says the host alone; the header no longer names its project. The client (`syncGroups`) keys every element by `key` and places headings and lines in the server's order; the filter hides a repo line, and a heading, when everything under it is hidden; the ring runs repo line → team cards → strip (`RINGS.org`). Tests: `tests/test_ui_org_layout.py` (nine, a node probe among them), the header test rewritten. The director's card is TD-642's (its item 6a): no `director:` exists until it lands. ## TD-741: Build TD-722 (3): a board row carries its repo, not a team — the Inbox rail's Repos group and `?repo=`, `next:<n>` per repo

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (TD-722's amendment, an interactive round with Paul)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 6 (board items, *The board's horizon* `next:<n>`, *the rail*), §4.5a *Inbox page: the rail*; `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (the horizon ~L1571, `next:` ~L1605, its `repo_teams` badge ~L1582), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`repo_teams` ~L383 and its callers ~L758, ~L2171, ~L2397, ~L3241), the Inbox templates and rail

**Why:** the board is the repo's, but the Inbox badges a board row with the first team whose repo it is (`repo_teams`) and counts the horizon per team. With two teams on one repo (TD-722) the badge is arbitrary and the second team's rail pick shows none of the repo's board. Paul, 2026-10-15, asked whether a board row should carry the project or *project.repo*: the row carries its repo, and the project heading is read from it, since a repo is in one project.

**Fix:**
- A board row carries its **repo** and no team badge, drawn *ContractMatch · samscrape* where the repo's project has several repos (`Org.project_of`, TD-724), else the repo's name.
- The rail gains a **Repos** group after *Teams*, each repo a row on the page carries, with its count; the pick is the URL's `repo`. A **team** pick narrows board items to the team's repo.
- `next:<n>` is per repo: each board's n soonest open items, the board counted once whichever teams work its repo. The setting keeps its word.
- `repo_teams` keeps its other callers (Add entry's hand-to default, the start-on-work row), and stops badging board rows.
- A team's rail count includes the board rows of the team's repo, so the count and the narrowed page agree.
- **Tests** (in `tests/test_ui_board.py` and the Inbox tests, `tests/test_ui_inbox*.py`): a team's rail count includes its repo's board rows; a board row of a repo two teams service carries the repo and no team; `?repo=` narrows to it; a team pick shows its repo's board rows; `next:3` draws three per repo; a repo in a multi-repo project reads *Project · repo*.

**Done when** board rows carry their repo, the rail filters by repo, the horizon counts per repo, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-722, TD-724, TD-740, TD-207, TD-220.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, #1931) — board rows carry their repo (`repo_boards`: the repo's name, *Project · repo* where its project has several repos, and every team whose repo it is) and no team badge; the rail's **Repos** group and `?repo=`; a team pick and a team's count take in its repo's board rows; `next:<n>` per repo and the line saying so; `repo_teams` keeps Add entry's default and the start-on-work row. Every listed test is in `tests/test_ui_board.py` and `tests/test_ui_inbox.py`; checked on a scratch home with two teams on one repo of a two-repo project (the PR's UI check).

**Related:** TD-722, TD-724.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, #1932) — `_member` refuses `team:` with `NO_NESTING` (the design's words and the fix: delete the entry, start that team on its own), in the org file as in a repo's `.shiftlead.yml`. `MemberDef.team`, `_no_cycles`, `_validate`'s nested check, `edit_members`' nested branch, the planner's *not built yet* branch, the members view's `nested` row and every `m.team is None` filter are removed. `team_skill.md` and §4.9's edit refusals were updated, and the tests that nested a team now expect the refusal. ## TD-722: One repo per team, declared, and a project a heading on repos: a team names its repo, a repo has many teams listed together, the org page groups project → repo → team cards

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — Designed, amended 2026-10-15 (an interactive round with Paul after Fable's review, PR #1850): the anchor seat (first made the repo's, shared by its teams; then retired in round 4, §4.9b *No anchor seat*), its controllers the repo's managers; an agent's name is unique across a repo's teams; the old keys and a team's `anchor:` are refused, not read with a warning; the director carries an Org block from the registry and a directory of its own; the Org page's headings follow the org file's order with liveness inside a repo, the Repo facet and the anchor's card on the repo's line, a no-team strip per repo and *No repo*; a board row carries its repo; `--project` and the Project picker go. Round 2 (Fable's eleven findings, adopted by Paul): the home ties the anchor seat to its teams by `controllers`; one seat per repo per host; its review the first controller team's chain; the repo's lanes include the seat's; the Org page's repo line, ring, hiding and strip heading. Round 3 (Sonnet's twelve findings, adopted by Paul): the seat winds down only when no live record of the repo's teams is left; its stop time re-derived on a move or Clear; the anchor's review chain settled; the seat in no team's reserve, balance or start mark, its asks under its repo; `anchors:` for any repo whose file has no `anchor:`; the changeover before the promote; TD-724 split into an unheld slice 4 and a held slice 6. Fable round 3 (adopted by Paul): the seat's review is the repo's first team's chain, nothing per team, only that team reading *flow changed* over it; rule 8 reads the seat's news by the records' `repo`; a live record of the repo's teams defined, the seat wound down on any tick with none; `anchor: false` drops the seat; the changeover marks the old `<team>-anchor` records removed. Built by TD-724, TD-725 and TD-741; the Repo page is TD-721's, built by TD-740. Was: designed by the designer in #1832 — Designed 2026-10-15 (the designer; no mockup: the Org page keeps every card as it is and adds a heading per project and a line per repo above them) — §4.9 *Projects*, *Teams*, *A definition written before TD-722*, *Home and reach*, *The Org page*. A team declares one `repo:` (required in the org file, unsaid in a repo's own), and every `home:` and `projects:` on a team goes. A project is a heading on repos with an optional `title`, a repo in at most one, and a repo in none is its own heading. The `project` badge is the repo's project, so two teams on one repo always share one, and mail is unchanged. The director is the org's, with the org-wide block (a step added to TD-642). The Org page groups project → repo → team, cards whole and never combined. The old keys are read for one release where they name one repo, and refused where a team spans. §4.9's guardians example is two teams under one heading, and the ADR is amended. Built by TD-724 and TD-725. Was: Open. **Round 4** (Fable, adopted by Paul, 2026-10-15): **the anchor seat is retired**, reversing TD-381 — its jobs go to the grinders' pick list, the designer and the person (§4.9b *No anchor seat*); everything per-repo-anchor of rounds 1–3 is gone, and Sonnet round 2's seat-lifecycle findings are superseded; the removal is TD-757, TD-759 and TD-760.
**Blocked by:** TD-725, TD-741, TD-757, TD-759, TD-760
**Location:** `docs/design/4.9-org-team-project.md` (*Projects*, *Teams*: `projects: [...]`, `manager.home`, a member's `home`, the guardians example with a nested team; *Home and reach*); `docs/design/4.10-messages.md` (*across teams, by project*: the `project` badge, *the first of its team's projects that lists its home repo*); `docs/design/4.5-ui.md` (screen 1 *The Org, team-first*, screen 6 `repo_teams`, screen 11); `docs/design/4.5a-controls.md` (*team groups*: the header's place, *mixed*); `docs/design/4.9b-techlead.md` (*The director seat*); `docs/design/5-configuration.md` (`org.yml`, a repo's `.shiftlead.yml`); [ADR 2026-09-13](decisions/2026-09-13-org-teams-projects.md) (*a team may span projects*)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-15, in the conversation TD-721 waited on: *one repo per team, declared. We still want to be able to have multiple teams per repo (e.g. db team, compliance team) and those can be listed together (per repo) but not auto-combined* — and of a grouping such as Guardians, *a project heading*, placed **on the repo** (*project on the repo*). The design today lets a team span projects and a project hold several repos, and infers a team's repo from where its live members sit (`team_repo`); every project in the org file holds one repo, and no team spans two. The inference is what leaves the header's *mixed* place, `repo_teams`' first-team-in-definition-order rule, and a Repo page that can expand only one team's card (TD-721). The cases for a team over several repos each split by repo: a function across repos (docs, audits, dependency bumps) is a role or flow stage in each repo's team; a product over several repos is one team per repo, sequenced by cross-repo `Blocked by: <repo>#TD-NNN`; the cost a team per repo adds is its seats, which an on-call seat and a team managed by the person already keep small.

**Fix:** a design round:
1. **A team declares one repo** — `repo:` in its definition, replacing `projects: [...]`, `manager.home` and a member's `home`; a repo's `.shiftlead.yml` team's repo is that repo. A repo has any number of teams.
2. **A project is a heading on repos** — `projects:` in the org file keeps listing repos, and a repo sits in at most one project; a team's project is its repo's. A repo in no project is its own heading. Nothing acts on a project but the mail gate and the brief's Project block.
3. **Mail and reach stay as they are**, read off the repo: *across teams, by project* (TD-582) keys on the repo's project, so two teams on one repo always share one; the Project block names the project's other repos.
4. **The director** (TD-636, TD-642, TD-657) is the org's, above every heading: what it reads of the org's repos (an org-wide Project block: every registered repo's checkout) and where it is drawn (with the person, at the top of the Org page).
5. **The Org page groups project → repo → team cards**: a repo's teams listed together, each its own whole card, never combined; the *mixed* place and `repo_teams`' first-team rule go. The Repo page is one repo group expanded (TD-721).
6. **What goes**: §4.9's guardians example (one team over several repos, a nested team) becomes several teams under a Guardians heading; the ADR's *a team may span projects* is superseded, with a dated line in the history.
7. **Migration**: a definition carrying `projects:` or `home:` on a team — refused by name — and the backfill (TD-723). Then build entries.

**Done when** the design says the above, its build entries are filed, and this entry's `Blocked by:` names them.

**Related:** TD-721, TD-723, TD-582, TD-636, TD-642, TD-657, TD-040.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 — archived with its last builds (TD-724 by #1840, #1910; TD-725 by #1929; TD-741 by #1931; TD-757 by #1900; TD-759 by #1924; TD-760 by dev-cadence#276 and contractmatch#179; see their **Resolved:**).

## TD-721: The Repo page is not an expansion of the team's Org card: it draws the card's three facets but not its header, its controls or its member cards, and only the first of two servicing teams

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Resolved
**Blocked by:** TD-740
**Location:** `docs/design/4.5-ui.md` (screen 11 *Repo*: *The page opens with the team's three facets*); `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html` (includes `team_summary.html` alone), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/group_head.html`, `card.html`, `plus_card.html`; `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`repo_page`: `first = serving[0]`, `"g": {"team": ..., "summary": ...}`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-15: *everything that is shown on the org page card for a team/repo also shown on the repo page — the repo page should essentially be an expansion of the info shown on the org page.* Today the Repo page draws the team card's three facets (Repo, TDs in motion, Answer needed / Doing, all three even where the card leaves one out, TD-418) and nothing else of the card:

1. **The header** (`group_head.html`, §4.5a *team groups*): the flow chip and *flow changed* / *definition changed* with **Apply**, ✉ *n* unread, the *answered for you* mark, *n PRs waiting*, *n ready to close*, the *needs you* pill, the run's state (*concluded*, *wound down … by …*, *stopped*, *work waiting*), and the notes under it (*over its line*, *stops*, *started … for*).
2. **The controls**: Start, Wind down, Stop now, Forget all, and the ***i*** panel (Definition, Members…, Open file, Flow on Settings →, who for what, *not concluded:*).
3. **The member cards** (`card.html` compact, with their state pills and the lane's count) and the **+** card.
4. **A repo two teams service** names both in its *serviced by* line but draws only the first team's facets (`serving[0]`); the second team's card on the Org has nothing on the page that is meant to expand it.

**Fix:** a design round on screen 11: the page opens with the servicing team's whole Org card — header, controls, facets, member cards — drawn by the same templates, so the page cannot drift from the card, and the lists below expand it. Two teams on one repo are two cards, listed together and never combined (Paul, 2026-10-15, TD-722). It decides whether the member cards fold as on the Org; and how the page keeps the header and cards current, since the Org takes them from `/events` deltas and the Repo page re-reads `?part=1` on a 30 s poll. Then one or more build entries.

**Done when** screen 11 says the page carries everything the team's Org card shows, its build entries are filed, and this entry's `Blocked by:` names them.

**Related:** TD-722, TD-176 (slice 5 built the page), TD-418, TD-604, TD-693.

- **Kept by `/events`**: the cards and headers take the Org's deltas through the Org's own client code; the lists keep the `?part=1` poll and the `repos` / `doing` events. A team card folds by the same per-team choice as on the Org.
- **Doing** is every servicing team's kept calls, newest first; where two or more teams service the repo a team chip per team comes first (*db (12)*), then *all (n)* and the agent chips; a team pick and an agent pick AND.
- **Waiting on you**'s heading links `/inbox?repo=<repo>&kind=board` (TD-741's filter).
- **Add entry**'s form gains an optional **Team** pick where two or more teams service the repo: blank hands to the first in definition order with a techlead seat, a pick to that team's seat, and the form names the seat. TD-730 later says how the entry names its team.
- **Tests** (in `tests/test_ui_repo*.py`, beside the Repo page's own):
  - A repo two teams service draws both teams' whole cards, each with its header controls and member cards, and the Repo facet once.
  - A repo no team services draws its line and facet alone, with the lists.
  - A delta on a member re-renders its card on the Repo page as on the Org.
  - The Doing chips carry a team chip per team where two serve the repo, and none where one does.
  - The Team pick hands to the picked team's techlead seat, and blank to the first.

**Done when** the Repo page shows everything the Org shows for the repo's group, for every servicing team, kept live by the Org's deltas, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-721 (the design), TD-722, TD-725, TD-741, TD-730, TD-176.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, #1936) — the Repo page is the repo's items of the Org's own layout (`repo_items` over `team_groups` and `org_layout`), drawn by one partial, `org_item.html`, which the Org draws with too: the repo's line with its Repo facet once, every servicing team's whole card and the no-team strip. The cards take the Org's `/events` deltas through the shared `groupsEvent(ev, repo)` (`AO.repoItems`, `syncGroups(gs, drop)`), and fold by the Org's per-team choice. The lists, title line and seams keep the `?part=1` poll, re-read on this repo's events. Doing is every servicing team's calls, with team chips where two or more serve the repo (`repo_doing`, `doing_chips`). *Waiting on you* links `/inbox?repo=…&kind=board`. Add entry has an optional **Team** pick (`entry_plan(…, pick)`, `/api/entry/hand` `team`). ## TD-783: No test reads a rank file with bytes that are not UTF-8: `ledger.reading` decodes it with `errors="replace"` and a strict read passes every rank test

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1930)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #1942
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` `reading` (the `rank_text` read, `errors="replace"`); `tests/test_rank_order.py`, `tests/test_repo_facts.py`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-16. Changing `(Path(root) / lb.rank_path(rel)).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` to `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` leaves `pdm run pytest -q tests/test_rank_order.py tests/test_repo_facts.py` at 49 passed. The `errors="replace"` is the line that keeps a rank file with a stray non-UTF-8 byte from raising `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`, not the `OSError` the `except` catches) out of the whole ledger reading of the repo; no test writes such a file.

**Fix:** a `test_repo_facts.py` test that writes a rank file holding a byte like `\xff` beside a ledger and asserts `reading` still returns its entries (the bad line is ledgerboard's to flag, not a crash).

**Done when** the mutation above fails a test.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, #1942) — `tests/test_rank_order.py`'s `test_a_rank_file_with_a_byte_that_is_not_utf8_still_reads_the_ledger` writes a rank file holding a `\xff` line beside a good one; `reading` returns every entry and the good line still ranks its entry. Dropping `errors="replace"` fails it.

## TD-730: A ledger entry on a repo two teams service says which team's lanes take it: a `Team:` field, set at Add entry or by the techlead, and an untagged or stale one withheld and handed to a techlead

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-15 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed (2026-10-15, the designer): §4.4 *An entry names its team* — a `**Team:**` line whose vocabulary is the ledger's own `Fields:` line (`Team = db | compliance`), required only where it names two or more teams; the reader marks `needs_team` (untagged or unknown) and withholds it; `lane_matches` takes the lane's record's team; a claim on another team's entry is refused (`--force` passes); the techlead seat carries `seat.tags`, and the tagging seat (first in the vocabulary's order) is due `by: tag` to tag them in one PR; a stale or missing declaration is `ao org check`'s. The home reads the declaration, never the definitions. Built by TD-762 (reader, lanes, claim, `ao repo`), TD-763 (the tagging seat, `entry.md`, `ao org check`) and TD-764 (the pages, `entry.team`).
**Blocked by:** TD-762, TD-763, TD-764
**Location:** `docs/design/4.4-host-agent.md` (*An entry names its team*, *Repo facts*, *In a team's lanes*, *An entry says what it waits for*, *A new entry settles before it is pickable*); `docs/design/4.9-org-team-project.md` (*Teams*); `docs/design/4.5a-controls.md` (*Add entry form*, *Hand to the techlead*, the Repo page's lists); `docs/technical_debt.md` (the `Fields:` line); `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (`lane_matches`, `in_lanes`); `src/shiftlead/teamrun.py` (`repo_lanes`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-15: *when a TD is added to the ledger in shiftlead we can require that a team is selected (by the techlead if not beforehand by the user) … If TDs are added outside shiftlead, the host agent can identify them and send them to a techlead to have them resolved … We should also have a check for stale entries, e.g. team1 is assigned entries but is no longer defined.* Under TD-722 a repo has any number of teams (a db team and a compliance team), each with its own lanes, but an entry names only an `Owner:` role word. So two teams' grinders both take every pickable `Owner: grinder` entry. A claim keeps them off the same entry at once, but nothing keeps compliance work with the compliance team.

**Fix:** a design round. What Paul and the session proposed (2026-10-15), for the designer to check against the design:
1. **A `Team:` header field, not `Owner: <team>:<role>`.** `Owner:` is read by dev-cadence's synced `scripts/ledger.py` against a fixed word list in every cadence repo, ShiftLead or not. A field declared on the ledger's `Fields:` line is how `Waits` joined (TD-715), and dev-cadence reads past it. Its values are the repo's team names.
2. **Required only where the repo has two or more teams**; one team is implied, so no existing entry is edited. `Owner: paul` entries carry none.
3. **Set at Add entry**: the form's team pick, optional. Left blank, the techlead that drafts the entry writes it.
4. **An entry with no `Team:` on a repo of several teams, or one naming a team no definition holds any more (stale)**, is withheld from every lane, as a waiting entry is (TD-715). The home hands it to a techlead of the repo's teams to tag. The Repo page lists it as *needs a team*, and `ao org check` names the stale ones.
5. The lanes reader (`lane_matches` over `repo_lanes`) takes an entry only into its `Team:`'s lanes.

**Done when** the design says how an entry names its team, how an untagged or stale one is found and resolved, and how the lanes read it, its build entries are filed, and this entry's `Blocked by:` names them.

**Related:** TD-722, TD-721, TD-715, TD-707, TD-731.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2) — designed in #1893; its builds all merged: TD-762 in #1902, TD-763 in #1908 and TD-764, the last, in #1943, so it archives with it (§4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*).

## TD-788: Held by no test: the rank flush's join and prune PRs, its found-timer and signature guard, and the landed key's expiry (`agent_rank`, #1939)

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1939)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #1947
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_rank.py` (`_rank_flush`, `_rank_pass`), `tests/test_rank.py`

**Why:** #1939 added `_rank_flush`'s three batches — `("rank", lines)`, `("join", …)`, `("prune", …)` — and `_rank_pass`'s timing for them. `tests/test_rank.py` runs the flush only with a move pending (`test_the_flush_lands_per_repo_…`, `test_a_flush_is_due_…` stubs `_rank_flush`); the join and prune halves are tested only as the pure `rank.joins` / `rank.prunes` (`test_a_lined_card_keeps_its_place_…`) and `_rank_lined`. Probes, each applied alone to `agent_rank.py` in a worktree and restored, and `pytest tests/test_rank.py` run (the first also with `test_ui_events_light.py test_board.py test_queue.py`) — all still **pass**:
- delete the `("join", …)` and `("prune", …)` tuples from `batches` — no join or prune PR is ever landed; green;
- `found and t - float(state["found_at"] or t) >= rank_mod.RANK_FLUSH` → `found` — a join or prune flushes at once, not `RANK_FLUSH` after it was first found (design §4.4 *A move lands*); green;
- `if _signature(found) == self.rank_store.load()["flushed"]:` → `if False:` — a checkout that has not caught up is flushed again on every tick; green;
- `state["flushed"] = [] if missed else …` → `[] if False else …`, and `missed = missed or kind != "rank"` → `pass` — a join or prune that failed to land is never found again; green;
- drop `and t - float(v.get("at") or 0) < LANDED_KEEP` — a landed key stands in forever; green;
- `if it is not None and self._queue:` (`rpc_rank_move`'s broadcast) → `if False:` — the page is not told of a move; green (no test reads the `queue` event).
The suite's full run with the first mutation applied failed only in `test_link.py`, `test_settle.py` and `test_ui.py` (20 tests, none naming the rank).

**Done when** a test per probe above goes red against it: a flush with a pending join and one with a pending prune land one `queue: join` / `queue: prune` PR per repo; neither is due before `RANK_FLUSH` after it is found; a flush whose signature equals `flushed` starts nothing; a join that failed to land clears `flushed`; a landed key older than `LANDED_KEEP` is dropped by `_rank_pass`; `rpc_rank_move` broadcasts a `queue` event for a move and none for a move that leaves the card where it is.

**Related:** TD-769 (the build), TD-779, TD-780 (the same kind of gap in #1916).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1947) — `tests/test_rank.py` gains four tests: a join and a prune that land one `queue: join` and one `queue: prune` PR `RANK_FLUSH` after they are found and none before, with the signature guard holding while the checkout has not pulled; a join that failed to land clears `flushed` and is found again; a landed key older than `LANDED_KEEP` is dropped and a fresh one kept; `rpc_rank_move` broadcasts a `queue` event for a move and none for a move where the card already is. Each of the six probes above, applied alone, turns the file red.

## TD-769: Build TD-748 (1): the rank — the cards and keys of the `queue` reading, the intents and their flush, `rank_move` and `ao rank`, rank order in `pickable()`, `ao repo` and the briefs

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-748's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** live-check #1939 #1940
**Status:** Built — slice 1 (ledgerboard v1.2 synced and vendored; the ledger reading's `key`, `lined`, `card_key` and `order`; `ao repo` in rank order) by #1930; slice 2 (`sessionorc.queue`: the `queue` reading, RPC and event — cards across repos, the top entry, rows, row states, the ledger's part of the status, keys, completed cards, passed-over flags, other work) by #1933; slice 3 (`rank_move`, the intents in `ranks.json`, the flush with its joins and prunes by `board.land_rank`, `ao rank` and `--list`; #1933's review notes: a completed card dated by its `Resolved:` date first, `of_record` once per claim) and §4.4a's `rank_move` row by #1939; slice 4 (the briefs: work orders, then the highest-ranked pickable entry in the lane nobody holds; the primer's §4.10 pointer) by #1940. **A live check now** (design §4.9b): with #1939 and #1940 live (`ao promote status`), read the next `queue: rank` PR the home opens after the person's `ao rank` or a drag — one per repo, squash-merged at once, changing the rank file alone — and `ao rank --list` against `ledger.py --pickable`; read, never pressed (a move is the person's).
**Blocked by:** dev-cadence#TD-119
**Location:** design §4.4 *The Queue: cards, and the rank that orders them*, §4.7 `ao rank`, `ao repo`, §4.8 *Choosing in a free-pick lane*; `scripts/ledgerboard.py` and `src/sessionorc/ledgerboard.py` (the vendored release); `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (`reading` ~L672, the `lb.pickable` call ~L406, `blocked_ids` ~L140); a new `src/sessionorc/queue.py`; `src/sessionorc/board.py` (`_land` ~L329, its tree and `still()` ~L517); `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_repos` ~L863, beside it `rpc_queue` and `rpc_rank_move`); `src/sessionorc/agent_ids.py` (`rpc_td_hold` ~L100, the person-or-interactive check `rpc_td_next(held)` ~L206 makes); `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`cmd_repo` ~L1724, a new `cmd_rank`); `src/shiftlead/briefs/grinder.md`, `designer.md`, `work.md`; `docs/briefs/` (held: the techlead reads it)

**Why:** TD-748. The rank is the Queue's spine: the cards, their keys and the pick order land first, with no page, so the order can be read in `ao repo` and the briefs before anything draws it.

**Fix:**
- **Vendor** dev-cadence#TD-119's ledgerboard release into both copies (sync PR); `components()`, the key alphabet, `midpoint()`, the implicit key, the rank file's reader and writer, and `pickable()`'s rank order come from it, never re-derived here.
- **`sessionorc.queue`**: over every registered repo's ledger reading, the cards of §4.4 — components joined across repos by `<repo>#TD-n`, the top entry, the rows' tree (breadth first, a second parent noted), archived rows one hop, each row's state word from the readings the home holds (claims, the PR reading, `settling`, `held`, `waiting`), *stalled* at `QUEUE_STALL_AFTER` (24 h, beside `ORPHAN_AFTER`; §4.2's `STALL_AFTER` is another bound), the ledger's part of each card's status, keys (lined from each repo's `<ledger stem>_rank.yml`, else implicit) and key(card); completed cards over the whole archive, cached by the archive's blob sha; passed-over flags from the claims and the lanes (`ledger.in_lanes`). Served as the `queue` RPC and a `queue` event when it changes (§4.4 *Each reading has one owner*), with an `omit` as `repos` takes.
- **`rank_move {ids, prev, next}`**: the person's, and an interactive session's; refused to an unattended one. It stores an intent in `ranks.json` beside `repos.json`. **The flush**, `RANK_FLUSH` (60 s) after the last move: re-derive each intent against the cards as they are then (§4.4 *A move lands*), write the lines on `origin/<default>` in the board's own tree per repo, one PR per repo per flush, subject `queue: rank TD-a, TD-b (shiftlead)`, squash-merged at once by `board._land`'s road; the loser of a one-line conflict retries once, and a PR failing after that keeps its intent for the next flush and marks the card *not landed*; `queue: join TD-n (shiftlead)` for an unlined open member of a lined card, or a lined one whose line is not its card's key and `queue: prune TD-a, TD-b (shiftlead)` for a wholly archived card's lines, each a flush of its own kind, looked for at every flush and on every tick whose ledger reading changed; the subjects from ledgerboard's `queue_subject()`. Neighbours are named by a member id, re-resolved at the flush, always the adjacent Up next cards of the whole order; an In-progress card's ids are refused.
- **`ao rank <TD-n> (--above|--below <TD-m> | --top) [--repo]`** and `ao rank --list` (§4.7); `ao repo` lists in rank order; `ao repo --json` carries each entry's `key` and `lined` (§4.7).
- **The briefs**: `grinder.md`, `designer.md` and `work.md` say *work orders first, then the highest-ranked pickable entry in your lane that nobody holds*; `docs/briefs/techlead-context.md`'s §4.10 pointer reads *Nothing leaves the Inbox without an answer* (a held path: the PR waits for the techlead); the code and test comments that cite *The Inbox is a queue* are left, the heading naming its old title.
- **Tests**: components across two repos and both directions; the top entry (a design that names its builds; no design; a tie); a two-parent row; archived rows one hop; each state word and *stalled*; status precedence, *decision (designer)* reading *ready*; implicit keys sort High < Medium < Low and by Type, then id; a lined card keeps its place through a Priority edit; split, merge, join and prune; an intent re-derived after a neighbour archives; two flushes on one line; `ao rank` refused unattended; `ao repo`'s order equals `ledger.py --pickable`'s from the rank file alone for single-repo cards; a failed rank PR keeps its intent.

**Done when** `ao rank` moves a card and the move lands as one `queue: rank` PR per repo, `ao repo` and `pickable()` print the rank order the rank file gives, the `queue` reading serves every card's rows, states and keys, and every listed test passes.

**Related:** TD-748 (the design), TD-770, TD-771, TD-772, dev-cadence#TD-119, TD-734 (the holder state).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, live check) — with #1939 and #1940 live (`ao promote status`: live c4239d9), the home's first rank flush was #1950, `queue: rank TD-748, TD-769, TD-770, TD-771, TD-772 (shiftlead)`: one PR for the repo, one commit, opened 19:15:04Z and squash-merged 19:15:08Z, changing `docs/technical_debt_rank.yml` alone — a new file of the grammar's two comment lines and one line per open member of TD-748's card, each `0i`. `ao rank --list` (read 19:28Z; which cards are In progress moves with every claim) puts TD-748's card first (In progress) and the repo's Up next cards in key order (TD-717, TD-156, TD-410, TD-460, TD-637, TD-781, …); `ledger.py --pickable` on main gives the same order card by card (TD-769 on the lined `0i`, TD-784 on its card's best implicit key `1|0|000052` from TD-052 High, then TD-720 on `1|0|000717`, …), each In progress card at its key's place as §4.4 says, and `ao repo` lists its pickable entries in that order. Read, never pressed; no join or prune PR has been needed since.
