**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-787's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #1956
**Location:** design §4.4 *A held PR nobody asked is marked, never ordered*; `src/sessionorc/held.py` (new `match`, which `held_paths` calls; new `repo_key`; `HELD_READS`), `src/sessionorc/reports.py` (`pr_reading`'s new `held=`, `pr_files`, `_sync_flag` as the model for carrying from `old`), `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (`ledger_path`, the direct `.shiftlead.yml` read to copy), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (where `pr_reading` is called; `_red_prs`, its `pr_orders` and save comparison; the stale *never reads `.shiftlead.yml`* comment; `by_remote` ~L3208), `src/sessionorc/store.py` (`RepoStore`); tests beside `tests/test_held.py` and the reading's tests

**Why:** TD-787: a green held PR nobody asked read the same blank as one outside `held:` (#1842, 17 hours). This is the reading's half: the marks the Repo page and `ao repo` draw (TD-790).

**Fix:** as design §4.4 says, bullet by bullet:
- **The key**: `held.repo_key(root, records)` — the repo's `held:` from `.shiftlead.yml` (a list, or named sets' union), else the union of `review_links` globs on live records whose `repo` is the root; sorted; empty for neither. The tick passes it to `pr_reading` as `held=`.
- **The held read**: per open PR that is not a sync PR (a draft included), the changed files once per head and per key; the row's `held`, `held_head`, `held_key`, carried from `old`; `held.match(files, globs)`; at most `HELD_READS` (5) a pass, unread or stale rows first, oldest first; a failed read keeps the last word, an unread PR carries no `held`.
- **The key's scope**: live is §6 *Balance*'s (not `exited`/`closed`, no `superseded_by`); `_read_repos` takes `{root: key}`, computed by the tick from its graph before the read; roots grouped by their reading's `remote`, each remote's union passed to every root of it (`by_remote`); on a first pass, with no `remote` read yet, a second checkout takes the first's reading at the first's key and the union re-reads it next pass.
- **Asked**: `_red_prs` keeps `pr_orders.asked: {n: {at, to}}` — the first `ask` carrying `pr` in the record mail of every seat `review.standing` reads (techlead records and any record with a `seat`, auditors included) and in `person_inbox`; `to` the addressee it was found under; counted for every checkout of the sender's record's repo's `remote`; a sender with no record, or whose record's `repo` is no registered root (a node's session): every registered repo the seat's team's live records name, in `person_inbox` every repo of the sender's `team` stamp, else every repo; pruned when the PR closes, in the save comparison; nothing seeded.
- **`unasked`**: `_red_prs` writes `pr_orders.unasked: [n, …]` — `held` non-empty, no `asked`, not a draft, not a sync PR, not conflicting, `checks` *green* or *none*, and a live record of the remote carrying a `review` — in its save comparison; the rows keep only `held`, `held_head`, `held_key`.

**Done when** tests hold: the key from `held:` (a list and named sets) and its fallback to the live records' `review`, an empty key reading nothing; `held`/`held_head`/`held_key` carried through `old`, a changed key re-reading at the same head, a draft read, a failed read keeping the last word, the `HELD_READS` cap and its order; `asked` from a seat's mail and from `person_inbox`, kept past the mail's prune and across a `RepoStore` reload, pruned on close; an ask for #12 from a session of repo A leaving repo B's #12 unasked, and the person's ask counting for each repo of the seat's team; a wound-down repo keeping its `held` and listing nothing unasked, its key unchanged; an exited or superseded record's `review` not counted; an ask of an auditor seat counting as asked; an ask from a forgotten sender, one from a node's session, and one in `person_inbox` with and without a `team` stamp; two checkouts of one remote at the union of keys; `pr_orders.unasked`'s precedence (draft, sync, conflicting, red, pending, *not run*), kept across a re-read of the rows.

**Related:** TD-787, TD-790, TD-684 (the per-head sync read), TD-613 (`pr_orders`).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1956) — `held.repo_key` (the `held:` list or named sets, else the live records' `review` globs), `held.match`, `HELD_READS`; `reports._held_flags` reads each open non-sync PR's files once per head and key under the cap, carried from `old`, a failed read keeping the last word; the tick's `_held_keys` unions the keys per remote into `_read_repos`; `held.asks`/`unasked`/`has_reader` give `_red_prs` its `pr_orders.asked` and `unasked`, both in its save comparison. `tests/test_held_reading.py` holds the Done-when list.

## TD-791: Nothing asserts the remedy line of `ao org check`'s two-team lack: the left-out names can be dropped from `orgcheck.team_lacks`' `Team = …` suggestion and every test passes

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1943)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/orgcheck.py` `team_lacks` (`names = [*declared, *…left-out…]`); `tests/test_cli_org.py` `test_a_team_of_a_two_team_repo_its_ledger_does_not_declare_is_lacking`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-16. Changing `names = [*declared, *(s["team"] for s in stale if s["kind"] == "left-out")]` to `names = [*declared]` in `orgcheck.team_lacks` (the lines #1943 rewrote onto `teams.stale_teams`) leaves `pdm run pytest -q tests/test_cli_org.py tests/test_cli_teams.py` green. The lack's remedy, `add `Team = ao-grind | ops``, then names only the declared teams, so a person who follows it declares nothing new and the lack stays. `test_cli_org.py` asserts only the message's prefix (`startswith("alpha: has 2 teams and its ledger's Fields: line does not declare alpha-grind")`); the `add `Team = …`` assertion in `tests/test_cli_teams.py` reads `teamrun`'s own start-refusal message, a different function.

**Fix:** extend the two-team lack test to assert the whole remedy: with `declared = []` the lack says `Team = alpha-grind | span`; with `["span"]`, `Team = span | alpha-grind`.

**Done when** the mutation above fails a test.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1962) — `test_a_team_of_a_two_team_repo_its_ledger_does_not_declare_is_lacking` asserts each lack's whole remedy, `Team = span | alpha-grind` (declared first, then the left-out teams in `teams.stale_teams`' order — with nothing declared that is span first, not the order the Fix guessed); `names = [*declared]` now fails both cases.

## TD-792: No test holds Claude Code's `permission_channel = True`: the conformance suite checks only that the value is a bool, so flipping it to False passes

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt

**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `src/shiftlead/adapters/claude_code/__init__.py` (`permission_channel`); `tests/conformance/_harness.py` line 62, `tests/conformance/test_conformance.py` `test_shell_declares_no_permission_channel`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-16. Changing `permission_channel = True` to `False` on `ClaudeCodeAdapter` leaves `tests/conformance` at 17 passed, 3 skipped (run with the main checkout's venv and `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src`: a scratch worktree's venv has no `shiftlead.adapters` entry point, so there the suite's first test fails at baseline). `_harness.py` asserts `permission_channel` is a `bool` (`getattr(ad, "permission_channel", True)`) and nothing else; the only assertion on a value is the shell's and the command's `False`. The contract's comment says a pending permission is answered through the hook channel (Allow / Deny) where it is True: that is Claude Code's claim, and no test holds it.

**Fix:** a conformance test that Claude Code declares `permission_channel` True, beside the shell's `False`; and, once TD-784's hook-payload fixtures land, one that a declared channel's pending permission reads as answerable.

**Done when** the mutation above fails a test.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1962) — `test_claude_code_declares_its_permission_channel` holds `permission_channel is True` beside the shell's False; flipping it fails the test. The second half (a declared channel's pending permission reads as answerable) needs TD-784's hook-payload fixtures and is written on TD-784's Status.

## TD-787: A green PR that touches a held path and was never asked of its reader reads the same as one outside `held:`: nothing shows that its author still owes the review and the ask

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — designed (2026-10-16, the designer) — §4.4 *A held PR nobody asked is marked, never ordered* (the key, the held read, the asks remembered, the rule, its reader), §4.5 screen 11's *unasked* tag, §4.7 `ao repo` and `ao pr held`, §4.9b *The repo's mark beside it*, §4.9c *What is shown*; built by TD-789 (the reading) and TD-790 (what shows it). Filed in an interactive round with Paul. Fable round 1 (10 findings) adopted, with Paul's choices: **visible only**, and a PR the home ever acts on with no author it can find is the person's. Fable round 2 (9) and Sonnet round 1 (10) adopted, with Paul's choices: the tag is drawn **whoever wrote the PR**, and it carries an **age**. Fable round 3 (6, **READY**) and Sonnet round 2 (10) adopted, with Paul's choice: `ao pr held` names the repo-level mark when it answers *not held*. Sonnet round 3 **READY** (1 nit) and Fable round 4 **READY** (2) adopted: the rounds converged. Paul lifted the hold 2026-10-16: the designer's to design
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 11 *Open PRs* (4.5-ui.md ~L1062–L1074: the standing column, and *nothing is said when no entry names the PR (a PR outside `held:`, one asked of nobody, or a team with no reader all read the same blank)*, which this rewrites), §4.9c *What is shown* (the same blank), §4.7 `ao repo` (4.7-cli.md ~L231: *a session's `ao repo` shows none*, which this amends for the tag) and `ao pr held`, §4.9b *The reader* (4.9b-techlead.md ~L385–L395: *whether a PR is held keys on the record's `review`* and *read by the author's own `ao` … never by the host agent*; ~L459–L461 a team with no seat asks the person), §4.9c *What is the repo's: `held:`* (named sets ~L518–L523; ~L526 *a path is held for what it is, whoever wrote the PR*), §4.9 *A person in the team* (4.9-org-team-project.md ~L314), §6 rule 11 (6-policies.md ~L853); `.shiftlead.yml:16`; `src/sessionorc/reports.py` (`OPEN_PR_FIELDS` ~L297, the `checks` words ~L341–L351, `pr_files` ~L666, `_sync_flag` ~L681 and `sync_head`, `pr_reading` ~L737, `GH_TIMEOUT`), `src/sessionorc/ledger.py` (`ledger_path` ~L610, the direct `.shiftlead.yml` read to copy; agent_tick.py ~L3508's *never reads `.shiftlead.yml`* comment goes stale), `src/sessionorc/held.py` (`held_paths` ~L65, `addressed`, `READS` ~L30), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_red_prs` ~L2896 and its save comparison ~L2918–L2924; `pr_orders` carried across a re-read ~L2872; `person_inbox`), `src/sessionorc/store.py` (`RepoStore` ~L170, the reading written whole), `src/shiftlead/review.py` (`standing` ~L92), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`_pr_standing` ~L1581, `cmd_repo`'s `standing` ~L1778 and its print ~L1818, `ao pr held` ~L2278 and its *not held* prose ~L2318–L2320), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html` (~L6–L7 the *i* panel, ~L12–L14 the tags), `src/shiftlead/teamrun.py` (`red_prs` ~L1371)

**Why:** #1842 (the designer brief's Fable and Sonnet rounds) was opened 2026-10-15 20:42Z by the interactive session ao-paul and touches `docs/briefs/**`. `ao pr held 1842` printed *held for the techlead (bound 2h)* and *ask it: `ao msg --kind ask --pr 1842 <reader> "…"`*. The author wrote it down as *waits for the techlead* and did neither step §4.9b gives the author: the `cadence-review:` comment (posted 2026-10-16 14:27Z) and then the ask. It sat green, unreviewed and unasked, for 17 hours, until Paul asked whether it was stranded.
- The command said what to do; the miss was the author's reading of *held* as *parked*. An interactive session gets no brief, and AGENTS.md and `docs/cadence.md` did not name the ask (only `grinder.stage.md:1` does).
- Nothing else could have shown it. The Repo page's standing column reads the same blank for a PR outside `held:` and for one *asked of nobody* (§4.5 screen 11), `ao repo` says nothing, the home watches only a red PR, an ask past its bound and a held PR that merged (§6 rule 11), and the session-start hook names a PR only past two days.
- `holds_pr` (workorders.py ~L385) did not see the session as the PR's holder: its branch lived in a scratch worktree. **Not fixed here**: tracking every worktree a session makes is outside the one-agent-per-directory shape (§9 invariant 2), and a visible tag needs no holder.

**Fix (Paul, 2026-10-16: visible only, drawn whoever wrote the PR, with an age, and named by `ao pr held`).** *As filed; the design's Fable and Sonnet rounds amended items 1–5 — the key's scope and plumbing, `_red_prs` owning `pr_orders.unasked`, `asked` reading the standing's seats by the sender's remote, the reader as the first matching link, `ao pr held` reading the home's reading — and §4.4 *A held PR nobody asked is marked, never ordered*, TD-789 and TD-790 carry the amended form.* The home tells nobody and orders nothing; the reading marks, and the Repo page, `ao repo` and `ao pr held` show.
1. **The key, at the tick.** The tick computes each repo's held key and passes it to `pr_reading` as a new `held=` (a sorted list of globs): the **repo's `held:`**, read from `.shiftlead.yml` directly as `ledger.ledger_path` reads `ledger:` (named sets: their union), since `sessionorc` never imports `shiftlead.repoconfig`; else the union of the `review` globs on the repo's live records (`review_links`, records whose `repo` is the root — what §4.9 *A person in the team* fills from the roles). A repo with neither has an empty key: nothing is held and nothing drawn.
2. **Held, by the reading.** `pr_reading` reads the changed files (`reports.pr_files`, paginated, `GH_TIMEOUT`) of each open PR that is not a sync PR — a draft too, since marking it ready changes no head — **once per head and per key**: the row carries `held` (the matched paths, `[]` for none), `held_head` and `held_key` (the list read), carried from `old` as `sync_head` is; a changed head or key re-reads it. The match is a new `held.match(files, globs)`, which `held_paths` itself calls (`held_paths(files, {"held": key})` would match nothing: `review_links` returns no link for a mapping with no `reader`). A new constant `HELD_READS = 5` caps the reads a pass (separate from `held.READS` and from the sync read), rows with no `held_head` or a stale one first, oldest first; until a PR is read, or while its read fails, it is *not judged* and draws nothing, and a failed read keeps the last word, as `_sync_flag` does. The first fill after the build takes as many passes as it needs.
3. **Asked, remembered.** The tick (`_red_prs`, which owns `pr_orders`) reads the asks in the mail the home holds — each review seat's record mail (`techlead` seats and a flow's stage readers by `held.addressed`, never an auditor seat) and `person_inbox` — and keeps per held PR the first `ask` carrying its `pr` (`pr_orders.asked: {n: {at, to}}`), pruned when the PR closes, joining `_red_prs`' save comparison. The reading is written whole (`RepoStore`), so a restart keeps it, and mail's 12-hour retention or a pass-up past the bound never un-asks a PR. *findings*, *passed*, *the person's* and *merged* are all asked. **Only mail held at and after the build counts:** an open held PR whose ask was pruned before it reads *unasked* — ask again, or let it stand; nothing is seeded from rule 10 or elsewhere.
4. **The tag.** A PR whose `held` is non-empty, never asked, not a draft, not a sync PR, not conflicting, its `checks` *green* or *none* (TD-664's send set; *pending* gets nothing, *not run* keeps *CI never ran*, red keeps the red tags) reads **`unasked · <age>`**, the age from the PR's `created`, in the standing column's place, drawn `wait` (amber). Its title: *touches held paths (`<path>`): post its review, then `ao msg --kind ask --pr <n> <reader>` — where your own `ao pr held` says held*. `<reader>` is the reader of the **first servicing team in the Org's order whose review holds a touched path** — its techlead seat by name, under a flow the chain's first reader, else `person` (§4.9b, a team with no seat); the page gets it from the members it already reads for the standing (app.py ~L1455–L1468). Where no servicing team has any reader, nothing is drawn, as today. The Open PRs *i* panel (`repo_part.html` ~L7) gains *unasked*. **`ao repo`** prints it on the PR's standing line (`unasked 17h — post its review, then ao msg --kind ask --pr 1842 techlead-ao-1`), joining `pr_orders.asked`, and `--json` carries per open PR `held` (paths), `asked` (`{at, to}` or null) and `unasked` (bool, the precedence applied). Because the tag is the reading's, the author's own `ao repo` shows it — §4.7's *a session's `ao repo` shows none* is amended to the mail standing alone.
5. **Whoever wrote it** (Paul). The tag keys on the PR's files, never on its author, as §4.9c ~L526 already says of a held path (*whoever wrote the PR*): a PR from a session whose record carries no `review` still reads *unasked* on a held path, since the home cannot find every author (#1842's was in a scratch worktree). §4.9b gains the sentence that reconciles the two reads: the home's repo-level mark reads the PR's files against the repo's `held:`, the author's `ao pr held` reads its record's `review`; where they differ, an author with a `review` asks the reader the tag names, and one with no `review` merges on the cadence and lets the tag stand. **`ao pr held`** (Paul), on a *not held* answer (either branch: no `review` on the record, or no path its `review` holds) where the repo's key matches, adds *the repo holds `<path>`: the Repo page tags it unasked until a reader is asked*.
6. **AGENTS.md** says a held PR's author posts the review and sends the first ask once the PR is green, and how the tag and a *not held* answer meet — in the PR that filed this entry.
7. **Tests:** the key from the repo's `held:` (and named sets) and its fallback to the live records' `review`; `held`, `held_head` and `held_key` carried through `old`, a changed key re-reading at the same head, a draft read, a failed read keeping the last word, the `HELD_READS` cap and order, a repo-level key with no reader matching; `asked` from a seat's mail and from `person_inbox`, kept past the mail's prune and across a `RepoStore` reload, pruned on close; the tag's precedence (draft, sync, conflicting, red, pending, *not run*, a reader-less repo) and the two-team reader on the Repo page and in `cmd_repo`'s prose and `--json`; `ao pr held`'s added line. §4.5a is untouched (the standing column is no control); the *i* panel's text is pinned by no test today (`grep -ln 4.5a tests` to check at the build).

**No notes, no orders, no Inbox row.** If a held PR is ever stranded again despite the tag, the safety net is a second entry, and Paul has chosen its owner: a held PR unasked past `ORPHAN_AFTER` whose author the home cannot find is **the person's** (an Inbox row), never a grinders' `pr:<n>` order, since a grinder's ask would make the reader merge a PR an interactive author meant to merge (§4.9b, the asker's mode decides the merge).

**Done when** the design says how the reading marks a PR held and asked, and what the Repo page and `ao repo` show for one unasked, and its build entry is filed and named in this entry's `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-658 (an ask refused until the PR is green), TD-745 (a draft is no order), TD-652 (a red PR's holders), TD-613 (a red PR nobody holds), TD-684 (the reading's sync read, the per-head cache), TD-686 (*CI never ran*), #1842.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1) — designed in #1948; its builds all merged: TD-789 in #1956 and TD-790, the last, in #1965, so it archives with it (§4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*).

## TD-790: Build TD-787 (2): *unasked* shown — the Repo page's tag and *i* panel, `ao repo`'s line and `--json`, `ao pr held`'s *the repo holds* line

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-787's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 11 (Open PRs), §4.7 `ao repo` and `ao pr held`, §4.9c *What is shown*; `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/repo_part.html` (the *i* panel ~L7, the tags ~L12–L14), `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (the standing's members ~L1455–L1468), `src/shiftlead/review.py` (`standing`; the reader's one function), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`_pr_standing`, `cmd_repo`'s standing and its print, `ao pr held`'s *not held* prose ~L2318–L2320)

**Why:** TD-787: the marks TD-789 writes are seen nowhere until the page and the CLI draw them.

**Fix:** as the design sections say:
- **The Repo page**: a PR in the reading's `pr_orders.unasked` (never one with a standing: `asked` reads the standing's seats) reads *unasked · <age>* (age from `created`) in the standing's place, drawn `wait`, its title naming the touched paths and *post its review, then `ao msg --kind ask --pr <n> <reader>` — where your own `ao pr held` says held*; `<reader>` the first servicing team's, in the Org's order, whose review holds a touched path — the first link of its members' `review` whose `held` matches a path in the row's `held`, that seat by name, else `person` — drawn by one function in `shiftlead.review` that the page and `cmd_repo` share, each ordering the teams in the Org's order (`cmd_repo` today sorts them by name; it takes the page's order, `ui.repo.org_layout`); nothing where no servicing team has a reader. The *i* panel says *unasked*.
- **`ao repo`**: the same tag on the PR's standing line for every caller (*unasked 17h — post its review, then ao msg --kind ask --pr 1842 techlead-ao-1*); `--json` per open PR `held`, `asked`, `unasked`.
- **`ao pr held`**: on a *not held* answer (either branch), from the `repos` RPC's reading of the record's repo: the PR in `pr_orders.unasked` adds *the repo holds `<path>`: the Repo page tags it unasked until a reader is asked*; in `pr_orders.asked`, *the repo holds `<path>`: asked of <to> <age> ago*; a row with no `held` yet, *the repo's hold is not yet read*; no reading of the repo (a node's checkout), nothing; no key on the client, no file read.

**Done when** tests hold: the tag and its title on the Repo page, the two-team reader in the Org's order on the page and in `cmd_repo` alike and the named-set reader (a `ui` stage not named for a PR outside its set), a reader-less repo drawing nothing; `cmd_repo`'s line and `--json`, a session's `ao repo` (no mail standing) printing the tag and its reader; `ao pr held`'s added lines on both *not held* branches — unasked, asked, not yet read, no reading. §4.5a is untouched (the standing is no control); `grep -ln 4.5a tests` before changing the *i* panel's text.

**Related:** TD-787, TD-789.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1965) — `review.unasked_reader` names the reader for the page and `ao repo` alike: the first servicing team, in the Org's order, whose members' `review` holds a touched path, its first matching link's seat by name, else `person`, and nothing where no team has a reader; `review.unasked` reads the reading's `pr_orders.unasked`, never the rule. The Repo page draws *unasked · <age>* (`wait`) in the standing's place with its title, and the *i* panel says what it means; `ao repo` orders its teams as the Org does (`_org_order`), prints *unasked 17h — post its review, then ao msg --kind ask --pr <n> <reader>* on the standing line, and `--json` carries per open PR `held`, `asked` and `unasked`; `ao pr held` adds the repo's line on both *not held* branches (`_repo_hold`). Tests: `tests/test_unasked_shown.py`. The page was looked at in headless Chromium on the app served from a fixture reading (`look_home.py`'s fixture repo has no PRs and no reader): `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-16-td790-unasked.png`.

## TD-781: A stopped team's lanes gain work and nothing says so: rule 8 reads only a team that wound down, so a team renamed, forgotten or never started under its names waits silently under `on_work: start`

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — designed (2026-10-16, the designer; no mockup: one row's words and section, one card note; *never a start* confirmed by Paul 2026-10-16 on steer m-b7bce89ccde0) — §6 rule 8 *A team that stopped*: rule 8 reads a stopped team's lanes as a wound-down team's (the same `lane_seen`, `WORK_SETTLE`, `gained`), giving a member with no `lane_seen` one at the first stopped reading so only entries after the stop are news; the mark carries `stopped: {by: person|until|other, at}`; under `ask` and `start` alike the Inbox row *team start*, never a start — *Needs you* for `until` and `other`, *Later* and uncounted for the person's own stop; the baseline `lane_seen` (entries and work orders) for any read record without one, wound down or stopped; `by` read over current records, `until` from the tick's `stop time` word; told on Telegram except for `person`; *A team with no record*: the card, `ao team list` and an uncounted *Later* row say *its lanes hold n entries* (distinct ids) from `teamrun.lanes`, no start — so the dc-grind incident draws a row whether its records stood or not. §4.5a *Inbox row: team start*, *team card: work waiting note*; §4.7 `ao team list`; §4.9a. A rename keeps old-named records (TD-703), so it is a stopped or wound-down team, not the no-record case. Built by TD-782.
**Blocked by:** TD-782
**Location:** design §6 rule 8 *Work for a team that wound down* (6-policies.md:576), §4.9a *Out of work does not mean out of reach*, §4.5a **when work appears**; `src/sessionorc/work.py` (`wound_down`: *a team with no session carrying its badge has never run, or has been forgotten, and is neither*), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` and `agent_inbox.py` (the rule's `work_waiting` mark), `src/sessionorc/agent_notify.py` (its row), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao team list`'s *work waiting* only on a wound-down team)

**Why:** dev-cadence's TD-119 (filed 2026-10-16 06:52Z by ShiftLead's designer, #277) was the only pickable build of its ledger and the first step of the Queue (shiftlead TD-769 waits on it). `dc-grind` has `on_work: start` in `settings.yml`, and rule 8 had started it three times on 2026-10-14. This time it started nothing and wrote nothing — no `work_waiting` in `host.json`, no Inbox row — and the Queue's builds stood still for seven hours until Paul asked how the team was doing and started it by hand (13:58Z). The cause, read from the records: on 2026-10-14 20:05 MDT the definition's members were renamed (`grinder-dc-1` → `dc-grinder`, `manager-dc-1` → `dc-manager`, `techlead-dc-1` → `dc-techlead`, dev-cadence 1145d97), so no record carries the new names; `wound_down` returns None for a team with no records, so the team reads *stopped*, and rule 8 reads only a wound-down team (or a finished member of a team that runs on). A stopped team waits for Start or its schedule by design — but nothing tells the person its lanes hold work. Paul, 2026-10-16: *should it have started automatically when new work arrived?* (The old records are gone and the Start rewrote the new ones, so the rename is the reading of what is left, not a proof.)

**Fix:** the design decides what a team with no live session gets when its lanes gain an entry while it is *stopped* rather than *wound down* — at the least a row (*dc-grind is stopped, 1 entry waiting: TD-119 — Start*), drawn under every `on_work` but `off`; and whether `on_work: start` starts a team that has no record under its definition's names (a rename, a Forget, a definition never started), which has nothing to replay but its definition, under rule 8's five bounds. A team a person stopped (`ao team stop`, a closer naming the person) is the case to keep apart: its stop is the person's word. Then a build entry.

**Done when** the design says what a stopped team with waiting work shows and does under each `on_work`, and its build entry is filed and named in this entry's `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-214, TD-227, TD-457, TD-748, TD-769.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1) — designed in #1928; its build TD-782 merged in three slices (#1952, #1960 and the last, #1968), so it archives with it (§4.9c *A design entry archives with its last build*).

## TD-782: Build TD-781: rule 8 reads a stopped team — the baseline `lane_seen`, `work_waiting.stopped`, the row under Needs you or Later, never a start; the card's *lanes hold n* for a team with no record

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-781's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — slice 1 (the home) by #1952, slice 2 (a stopped mark's row under Needs you, the card note beside *stopped*, the board hint, `ao team list`) by #1960, slice 3 (the *Later* half) by #1968.
**Location:** design §6 rule 8 *A team that stopped*, *A team with no record*; §4.5a *Inbox row: team start*, *team card: work waiting note*; §4.7 `ao team list`; `src/sessionorc/work.py` (a `team_stopped` reading beside `team_wound_down`), `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_work_marks`, `_work_mark`, `_work_start` ~L1731–1960), `src/sessionorc/agent_inbox.py` (`rpc_clear_work`; `rpc_attention_snooze`'s row kinds ~L246–265), `src/sessionorc/agent_notify.py` (the Telegram tell ~L115–127), `src/shiftlead/ui/inbox.py` (the team-start row ~L898, `work_note` ~L978), `src/shiftlead/ui/repo.py` (~L604: the note's `wound_down` gate, which must take the stopped case too; and the no-record note from `teamrun.lanes`), `src/shiftlead/ui/templates/group_head.html` (~L51, the card's note), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao team list` ~L1092–1135), `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py` (`Help("on-work", …)` ~L400)

**Why:** TD-781: dc-grind stood stopped for seven hours with TD-119, the Queue's first build, in its lane, and nothing was drawn, since rule 8 reads only a wound-down team.

**Fix:**
- **The reading** (`sessionorc.work`): a team is *stopped* when none of its crew is live and `team_wound_down` is None, with at least one crew record. `stopped_by(records)` gives `{by, at}` over the **current** crew records (not superseded, not sat out):
  - A record's end is `ended.at` where `ended` stands, else `closer.at`, else `closed_at`; `at` is the newest end across the records, and `by` reads only the records whose end is within `FINISHED_SETTLE` of `at`.
  - `by` is `person` where such a record's `ended.by` (or, with no `ended`, `closer.by`) is the person, or it ended naming nobody after a wrap-up whose `wrapup_by` is the person; else `until` where its `ended.why` or `closer.why` is `stop time` (the tick's word, `agent_tick.py` ~L389–418), or it ended naming nobody with `wrapup_sent_at` standing (the stop time's wrap-up, ~L407–411); else `other`.
  - **`wrapup_by`** (new record field: `models.py` beside `wrapup_at` ~L1233, and in `NODE_OWNED` beside `"wrapup_at"` ~L90, so a node's member carries it home): `rpc_send` with `wrapup` (`agent.py` ~L2212) stamps it from the caller as `closer_of` reads one, and clears it with `wrapup_at`. `_sit_out` (`agent.py` ~L2086–2088) passes `rpc_relaunch`'s `caller` to `rpc_send` and to the routed act, so a lead's sit-out stamps the lead, not `person`. Where a record carries both `wrapup_by` and `wrapup_sent_at`, the later of `wrapup_at` and `wrapup_sent_at` decides between `person` and `until`.
  - Reword `finished_alone`'s docstring (~L86: *stopped, which rule 8 leaves alone*) to *never starts*.
- **The tick** (`_work_marks`/`_work_mark`):
  - A stopped team's records are read as a wound-down team's.
  - **The baseline**: every record the pass reads whose `lane_seen` is None, wound down or stopped alike, gets `{at, ids, base: true}` on the first tick that reads it. The ids are `ledger.entries_before(root, rel, <the record's end>)` matching its lane, plus the `_orders` matching now, plus the ids the checkout's reading holds that `entries_before(root, rel, None)` does not (rule 6's own guard in `_lane_news`); `entries_before` returns `(entries | None, label)`. It is written pruned as `reread` prunes it and saved with the record, and that record has no news on that tick. A failed read writes nothing. A `base` memory whose `at` is older than the record's `created` (carried by a supersede, `agent.py` ~L1456–1470) is rewritten the same way.
  - The mark is `work_waiting` with `stopped: {by, at}`, removed as now (a crew session live, no id new, `off`, Start, Dismiss). A team read *wound down* later has `stopped` dropped and its ids kept.
  - `_work_start` never starts a mark carrying `stopped`.
  - The log line *wound down with work waiting* (~L1775) says *stopped* for a stopped team.
  - Reword `_question_end`'s docstring to say a stopped team's lanes are read.
- **Telegram** (`src/sessionorc/agent_notify.py` ~L115–127, `src/sessionorc/notify.py` `work_line` ~L67; design §4.10 *What is told*): a mark carrying `stopped` is told when `by` is `until` or `other`, under `ask` and `start` alike (the `ask`-only gate and the `held` skip lifted for it), and never when it is `person`; `work_line` gains *· <team> stopped and has work: n entries*.
- **The row** (`ui/inbox.py` ~L898):
  - It reads *`<team>` · stopped <t> · its lanes gained n entries: …*, with *by you* (`person`) or *at its stop time* (`until`) after *stopped*. Under `on_work: start` it ends *· not started: a stopped team is started by Start*.
  - `person` goes under *Later*, uncounted; `until` and `other` under *Needs you*, counted. Start, Snooze and Dismiss as the row's.
  - A mark carrying `stopped` is never read as a team that runs on: `finished` is `[]` and `running` False (today `work_finished` is taken for any team not in `wound`, ~L896–975, which would draw *<member> finished* and send Start to `work_start` for a team with nobody live); the row's words and its `wound_down` field come from `stopped`.
  - **A defined team with no record** has a client-drawn row under *Later*, uncounted, under `ask` and `start`: *`<team>` · stopped · its lanes hold n entries: …*, with Start and Snooze and no Dismiss. Its Snooze is a new attention row kind, `lanes`, with the team as its id: `rpc_attention_snooze` (`agent_inbox.py` ~L246–265) adds `lanes` to its kinds and to the refusal's words, and the row's `sid` is `lanes:<team>`, as the `work` row's is `work:<team>`. It leaves when an unattended record carries the badge; the card note's no-record test reads the crew, not every record.
  - The *Later* section (`inbox_sections`) takes both rows.
  - The board hint (~L1319, *· <team> wound down — starts on `on_work`*) reads *· <team> stopped — Start it* for a stopped team.
- **`teamrun.lanes`** returns the distinct matching ids beside its per-role counts. The page reads it at most once in `DEFS_TTL` per team, and `ao team list` once per run.
- **The card and the CLI**:
  - The *work waiting* note sits beside *stopped* as it does beside *wound down*, through `inbox.work_note` (~L978) and the `wound_down` gate at `ui/repo.py` ~L604, which takes the stopped case too.
  - A defined team with no record reads *· its lanes hold n entries* (tooltip Start's line; nothing when empty or unread).
  - `ao team list` shows *work waiting: n entries* beside *stopped* too, and *lanes hold n entries* for a team with no record. `--json` carries `work_waiting` and `lanes_hold`.
- **Help text**: the **when work appears** paragraph (§4.5a help list, `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py` `Help("on-work", …)` ~L400) gains a sentence: *A team that stopped is never started for its work; the Inbox says its lanes gained it — under Later if you stopped it yourself.* Change §4.5a's help list and `ui/help.py` together in this PR.
- **Tests**:
  - A team the person stopped (a member killed by the person) gains an entry: the mark has `stopped.by == "person"`, there is no start under `start`, and the row is under Later and untold.
  - A crash-stopped team gives `other`: counted under Needs you and told, with `work_line`'s stopped wording.
  - A stopped mark's row is not a running team's: no *finished* clause, and its Start is the card's, never `work_start`.
  - A tick kill at the stop time gives `until`; so does a member that exited on its own after the stop time's wrap-up.
  - A superseded record closed by the person does not make `person`; nor does a member the person closed a day before a stop-time stop.
  - A team the person wound down from the Org page whose members left on their own reads `person` (`wrapup_by`); a manager's wind-down does not.
  - A plain send clears `wrapup_by`; a wrap-up a session sends stamps that session's id, one the person sends stamps `person`.
  - A killed record Closed later keeps its kill's end: the baseline and `at` read `ended.at`, and the Close's `person` does not override the kill's `stop time`.
  - The baseline is the ledger at the record's end: an entry filed while the home was down after the stop is news; one only on a branch checked out at the home is not. A baseline carried by a supersede onto a run that ended undeclared is rewritten.
  - A member with no `lane_seen` gets the baseline: an entry, or a red PR, present at the stop is not news, while an entry filed after it is.
  - Dismiss adds the ids; a crew session going live removes the mark; `work_start` does not start a stopped mark.
  - The no-record row and card note come from `teamrun.lanes`, with distinct ids.
  - `ao team list` covers each case.
  - `attention_snooze` accepts kind `lanes` and still refuses an unknown kind.

**Done when** a stopped team whose lane gains an entry draws the *team start* row in the section its stop decides and is never started by rule 8, a defined team with no record shows what its lanes hold on its card and in `ao team list`, and every listed test passes, with a screenshot of the row and the card in the PR (design §4.9b).

**Related:** TD-781, TD-703, TD-227, TD-457.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1968) — slice 3: a state row carrying `later` is drawn in the Inbox's *Later* section (`INBOX_SECTIONS` gains `later`, `#rows-later`, uncounted, snoozed as any state row): the *team start* row of a team the person stopped, and `inbox.lanes_rows`, a defined team no unattended record carries, under `ask` and `start` — *`<team>` · stopped · its lanes hold n entries: …*, Start the card's, Snooze kept under `lanes:<team>`, no Dismiss. `Readings.team_lanes` reads `teamrun.lanes` per such team at most once in `DEFS_TTL`, off the loop, over the request's one `repos` reading; `with_lanes` puts `lanes_hold` and `lanes_line` on the definitions' rows, so the team card of a team with no crew record reads *· its lanes hold n entries* beside *stopped*, its tooltip Start's line. The **when work appears** help paragraph gained its sentence (§4.5a and `ui/help.py`). Tests: `tests/test_ui_work_row.py`. Looked at on a scratch home (`look_home.py` with a team defined and never started): `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-16-td782-later.png`, `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-16-td782-card.png`.

## TD-793: No test holds that `asked` is the *first* ask: the sort by `at` in `held.asks` and the earlier-wins merge in `_red_prs` can be reversed and every test passes

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, auditing #1956)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/held.py` (`asks`); `src/sessionorc/agent_tick.py` (`_red_prs`, the `asked = {…}` merge); `tests/test_held_reading.py`

**Why:** `test-audit-ao-1`, 2026-10-16. TD-789's Fix says `asked` is "the first `ask` carrying `pr`" and kept past the mail's prune. Two mutations leave `tests/test_held_reading.py`, `tests/test_held_missed.py` and `tests/test_pr_held.py` at 21 passed: (1) `key=lambda x: str(x[0].at or "")` → `key=lambda x: 0` in `held.asks` (a later ask of the same PR then wins over the earlier by mail order); (2) `asked = {**(found.get(root) or {}), **(old.get("asked") or {})}` → `{**(old.get("asked") or {}), **(found.get(root) or {})}` in `_red_prs` (a fresh ask then overwrites the kept first one, so `at`/`to` drift on each pass). Run as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD/src pdm run pytest -q tests/test_held_reading.py tests/test_held_missed.py tests/test_pr_held.py`. TD-789's Done-when names "kept past the mail's prune" only; the one test with two asks on a PR (`test_held_reading.py`, #12) lists them earliest first and from the same seat, so a stable sort that ignores `at` keeps the right answer; none lists the later ask first or has different seats.

**Fix:** a test with two asks of one PR (different `at`, listed latest first in the inbox, to different seats) whose `asked[n]` is the earlier's `{at, to}`; and one where a second ask arrives on a later pass, `asked[n]` still the first's.

**Done when** both mutations above fail a test.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1971) — `tests/test_held_reading.py` gained `test_asked_is_the_earliest_ask_by_at_whatever_the_order_the_mail_lists_it_in` (two seats, the later ask in the first-read seat's inbox and listed first in its own; the person's earliest still wins) and `test_a_later_ask_on_a_later_pass_never_moves_the_kept_first_one` (the first ask pruned from the mail, a later one to another seat arrives on the next pass, `asked[12]` is still the first's `{at, to}`). Mutation (1) fails the first, mutation (2) the second.

## TD-801: The person's own shell is refused acts on other sessions: `ao team flow --apply` from **Open shell here** needs the control grant, since TD-580 let the shell through the person-only list alone

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.8 *The person's own shell is the person* (*nothing else changes*) and the `control` grant's paragraph; §4.8a (identity); §9 invariants 5 and 11; §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*; `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`person_shell`; `act_gate`, the control gate, which passes `is_person(caller)` alone, ~L229); `src/sessionorc/agent_common.py` (`person_only`, ~L314)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-16, ran `ao team flow ao-grind --apply` in a shell opened with **Open shell here** and it was refused with *cannot create a new session: needs the control grant (design §4.8)*. The same command ran from a terminal outside ShiftLead. TD-580 (built by TD-596, #1583) came from Paul's words *a shell being directly controlled by the user should have permissions to promote/other without interference*, but its design let the person's own shell through `PERSON_ONLY` alone and said *nothing else changes*. Acts on another session (`create`, `send`, `keys`, `kill`, `close`, `mode`, `decide`, …) still pass only a request with no caller, so the dashboard's own shell cannot apply a team's flow, start, stop or message a session. Paul then asked if the TD had been done: *a shell should be considered my permissions*.

**Fix:** design it first:
1. Decide whether the control gate passes the person's own shell (`person_shell(record)`) as it passes a request with no caller: the grant half, the membership half (`controllers`), and §9 invariant 5 (a person's interactive session, which no session may act on).
2. Decide what stays refused even to the person's shell, if anything: `decide` on its own prompt, and acts on itself that edit authority (`set_grants`, `set_controllers`).
3. Decide what the act records as its actor (the shell's id, as TD-580's acts do) and what `create` hands a child as its controllers and grants, since attenuation reads the creator's record.
4. Restate TD-580's risk for the wider right: an agent started inside the shell inherits its identity and could act on every session.
Then the build entry, named in `Blocked by:`.

**Done when** the design says whether and how the person's own shell acts on other sessions, and its build entry is filed and named in `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-580 and TD-596 (the person-only half), TD-077 (identity), TD-036 (membership), TD-041 (invariant 5).

---

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1) — built by TD-802: #1988 and #1990.

## TD-802: Build TD-801: the person's own shell passes the acting gate — `act_gate` reads `person_shell`, a create from it adds no creator and is not attenuated, the usage gate's send refusal passes it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-801's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.8 *The person's own shell is the person*, §9 invariants 5 and 11, §6 *Usage gate*, §4.4a; `src/sessionorc/modes.py` (`offline_refusal`, its call in `agent_serve.py` ~L370); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`act_gate` ~L229, `person_shell`, new `as_person`), `src/sessionorc/agent_remote.py` (`host_files`, `_route_act`, `_lift_by_person`), `src/sessionorc/agent_hook.py` (the refill), `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`_gate` ~L3226 and its usage-gate `send` check; `create`'s *Create adds the creator* seeding ~L1084), `src/sessionorc/agent_serve.py` (the caller injected after the gate ~L389); tests beside the gate's and `person_only`'s

**Why:** TD-801: `ao team flow ao-grind --apply` from **Open shell here** was refused with *needs the control grant*; Paul: *a shell should be considered my permissions*.

**Fix:** as design §4.8 says:
- **`mail.as_person(caller, records)`**: `is_person(caller)` or `person_shell` of the caller's record in the one graph (a node's shell under `id@host` read from the home's copy). It replaces `is_person` at every branch where a person passes an act — and the seeding's `if caller` becomes `if caller and not as_person(…)` — : `act_gate` (before grant, attenuation, invariant 5, membership and the self-act branches), `_gate`'s usage-gate `send` refusal, `create`'s creator seeding (agent.py ~L1084) and its checks `start_of` (~L1060), `_check_keep_mail` (~L1414), `_check_succeeds` (~L1442), `_refuse_suspended` (~L1592) wherever it is called (a create, a resume, `succeeds`, `rpc_remove`'s Forget ~L2194), the *dropped by the person* note on a Drop (~L2824), `set_start` at the restart ceiling (~L2684), `host_files` (agent_remote.py ~L276), and the wake-budget refill on `send`, `keys` and `decide` (agent.py ~L2232, ~L2399, agent_hook.py ~L196). `is_person` stays where it means the absent `caller` itself (the identity table, a mail sender, `closer`, the mail reads and pass-up in `agent_mail.py`, `_checks_at_ask`, and the rest that are identity or reply-shape uses: `agent_serve.py`'s reply hints, `agent_ids.py`, `agent_wake.py`, `agent_rank.py`, `agent_identity.py`, `person_only` itself). `as_person` takes `person_only`'s `isinstance(caller, str)` guard.
- `create` from the person's own shell adds no creator to the new record's `controllers` (the controllers the request names, only) and is not attenuated.
- **Routed to a node** (`agent_remote.py` `_route_act` ~L472, `_lift_by_person` ~L512): **every** act from the person's own shell is forwarded with no caller and a create lifts a suspended name as a person's; the home's `closer` keeps the shell's id; the node records *person* as who typed.
- **A shell at a node**: `_forwarded` (agent_remote.py ~L112–L135), whose bound today tests `params.get("caller") is None`, applies the same bound where `as_person` reads the forwarded caller (`id@node`) from the home's copy of its record; `modes.offline_refusal` (~L144, ~L164) takes the node's records as a new argument, passed at its call in `agent_serve.py` (~L370), and passes the node's shell on its own node's sessions.
- `send` and `keys` keep recording the shell's id as who typed.
- Refusal words keep naming the person (*open to a person and to its own controllers*): the shell is the person; the docstrings of `act_gate`, `person_shell` and `as_person` say the wider right.

**Done when** tests hold: the person's own shell passes each of `ACTING_RPCS` onto another session with no grant and no membership, an interactive target included; `create` from it with grants it does not hold passes, and the child's `controllers` hold only what was asked; its `send` to a gated session passes; a create from it passing `start_of`, `keep_mail` (a closed member with mail) and `succeeds` (a renamed member) and a suspended name; `set_start` at the ceiling and `host_files` from it; its `send` refilling the wake budget; a create from it routed to a node seeding no creator, and `set_start` at the ceiling on a node's record passing; Forget of a suspended record from it; a node's shell bound to its node, and passing on its node's sessions, link up or down; an unattended shell, a shell with a controller, a shell with a role or a team, and an agent session each still fail as today — each test calling the RPC with `caller=<the shell's id>`, as `tests/test_person_only.py` does, not through the identity machinery.

**Related:** TD-801, TD-580, TD-596.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1988 and #1990) — slice 1 (#1988): `mail.as_person` at `act_gate`, the usage gate's `send`, `create`'s creator seeding and its `start_of`, `keep_mail` and `succeeds` checks, `_refuse_suspended` at its four calls, `set_start` at the ceiling, `host_files`, the refills on `send`, `keys` and `decide`, the *dropped by the person* note and `person_only`; `tests/test_person_shell_acts.py`. Slice 2 (#1990): `_route_act` forwards every act from the shell with no caller and `_lift_by_person` lifts a suspended name on its create; `_forwarded` bounds a node's shell to its node as a person there; `modes.offline_refusal` takes the node's records and serves its shell on its node's sessions, link up or down; `tests/test_person_shell_link.py` (each of its four tests fails with the `src` change reverted).

## TD-784: Build TD-112 (1): the adapter conformance suite — `tests/conformance/`, offline fixtures in CI, `pdm run conformance <adapter>` live by hand; Claude Code passes it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-112's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.3 *The conformance suite*; new `tests/conformance/` (a conftest parametrizing over `sessionorc.adapters.names()` with agents, each adapter's declared methods), fixtures under `tests/conformance/fixtures/<adapter>/`; `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.pdm.scripts] conformance`); `src/sessionorc/adapters.py` (`permission_channel` on the protocol, the `shell` adapter's False); `src/shiftlead/adapters/claude_code/__init__.py` (`permission_channel = True`, the declared optional methods)

**Why:** TD-112: neutrality is checked on every change, not once by a spike; the suite comes first, so the Gemini CLI adapter is built against it.

**Fix:**
- **The declaration**: each agent adapter says which optional methods it implements (`links`, `background`, `context`, `usage_report`, `mail`, `composer`, `title`, `spend`), and `permission_channel`; the suite tests what is declared and asserts an undeclared method is absent.
- **Offline (CI)**: fixtures captured from the real tool — panes for `classify`, `composer`, `title`; hook payloads for the state mapping and `pending`; transcripts for `read_transcript`, `context`, `links`, `spend`. The assertions are neutral: a state for every pane and payload fixture, the neutral entry kinds, no tool field name in any returned structure, `context` within `window`. Claude Code's fixtures captured from its current transcripts and panes (from a scratch session, never a person's).
- **Live (by hand)**: `pdm run conformance <adapter> --profile <p>` — a scratch `SHIFTLEAD_HOME` (short path, memory `scratchpad-too-long-for-unix-sockets`) with its own host agent on a private tmux socket, started and stopped by the pid the walk holds; `SHIFTLEAD_HOME` in every launch's env; the tool's home the profile's; a scratch directory; launch with a chosen id, the first hook, a short prompt (`working` → `idle`), `send` confirmed by `composer`, a permission seen as `needs-you` (a profile with `permission_prompts: ask`), a doorbell delivering a mail the walk sends as the person, a resume with the same id, the transcript read back. Refuses to run without `--profile` and never in CI (`CI` set).
- **Tests of the suite itself**: a fake adapter missing a declared method fails; one returning a tool field name fails.

**Done when** `pdm run test` runs the offline suite with Claude Code passing it, `pdm run conformance claude-code --profile <p>` passes once live with its output in the PR, and the `shell` adapter is skipped as having no agent.

**Related:** TD-112, TD-785, TD-786.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, #1949, #1969 and #2003) — slice 1 (#1949): the declaration (`implements`, `OPTIONAL_METHODS`, `permission_channel`), the offline suite and its self-tests, Claude Code's pane, transcript and `/proc` fixtures; slice 2 (#1969): the live walk, `pdm run conformance <adapter> --profile <p> [--capture]` (`scripts/conformance.py`), and the hook's capture; slice 3: the walk's first live run on the `conformance` profile passed 7 of 7 with `--capture` (its output in the PR), the captured hook payloads, status lines and pane titles named in `manifest.json` and read by the suite (the state mapping and `pending`, `usage_report`, `title`, and a captured permission for the declared channel, TD-792's second half), `_need` failing a declared method with no fixtures, and the capture writing each payload's own bytes. The walk passes the tool's asking arguments (Claude Code's `--permission-mode manual`, TD-823) and resumes once the killed process's own `SessionEnd` has landed (TD-822). The lasting content: design §4.3 *The conformance suite*, `tests/conformance/`, `scripts/conformance.py`.

## TD-806: The Focus composer's Send clears whatever the box holds when the send answers, so a late answer wipes what the person typed since, and one send was delivered twice from Edge: nothing makes a send land once

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — built by TD-813 (#1999, #2005)
**Blocked by:** TD-813
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus composer* **Send** (confirmed by the tool's composer emptying, one `C-m` retry, then `prompt-stuck`) and **prompt chips**; §4.7 `ao send`; `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the Focus composer: `$("#send")`'s click, ~L4633, `compose.value = ""` after `await act(id, "send", …)`; the draft in `localStorage`, `AO.draftKey`); `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`, ~L2770); `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_send` ~L2208, `_record_send`, `_submit`)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-16, sending to an interactive session from the Focus composer in Edge while the session was mid-turn: the message was sent but the box did not clear; it cleared by itself halfway through his next message, wiping what he had typed; and the session received the first message twice. In Firefox the box clears as the message goes. The UI's log shows two `POST /api/sessions/ao-shiftlead-ao-queue-vs-inbox/send`, 200 each, at 21:36:51 and 21:37:47, the second on a new connection, each delivering the same text. Two causes in the code, and one to establish:
1. The click handler sets `compose.value = ""` when the send answers, whatever the box then holds. A send waits for the tool's composer to empty (§4.5a **Send**), so an answer can come long after the press; what the person typed in between is lost, and the draft key is removed with it.
2. A send carries no id, so a second request with the same text, whoever or whatever makes it, is delivered again.
3. Not established: why Edge's first request did not finish in the page and a second was made 56 seconds later (a browser retry over the tailnet's `tailscale serve`, a press while the box still showed the text, or the send's wait outliving a timeout).

**Fix:** design it first:
1. When the send answers, remove only the text that was sent, and only while the box still begins with it; never clear words typed since. While the send is in flight, say so on the composer (Send disabled or *sending…*) so a second press is not made by hand.
2. A send id made by the page, carried on the request and kept by the host agent for a while: a repeat of an id already delivered answers as the first did and types nothing. The same for a prompt chip and for `ao send`, if it can repeat.
3. Establish cause 3 from Edge (the developer tools' network log on a send to a working session), and say how long a send may wait before the page is answered.
Then the build entry, named in `Blocked by:`.

**Done when** the design says what the composer clears and when, how a send is made to land once, and how long a send may take to answer, and the build entry is filed and named in `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-219 (the draft kept in the browser, which the code cites), TD-500 (the composer's bar, which folds on Send), TD-805 (page loads).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1) — built by TD-813: #1999 and #2005.

## TD-813: Build TD-806: a send lands once — the page's key on every send, a repeat answered as the first, and a composer that clears only what it sent

**Priority:** High
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-806's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — slice 1 #1999 (the agent), slice 2 #2005 (the page)
**Location:** design §4.10 *A send lands once*, §4.5a *Focus composer* **Send**, **prompt chips** and **the bar**, *Focus* **Wrap up**; `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (the composer's `$("#send")` click, the prompt chips' click, the card's Wrap up, `act`, `wireComposerBar`'s `redraw`, a new `AO.SEND_PAGE_SECONDS = 30`); `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`: `send` and `wrapup` pass `key`); `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_send`, `_record_send`); `src/sessionorc/models.py` (`SendEntry`, its merge by id in `_overlay`); `src/sessionorc/agent_remote.py` (`_route_act`, whose two *its verdict is unknown* errors the page reads; it forwards `key` untouched); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`SEND_KEY_SECONDS`); `tests/` (`test_ui_composer_bar.py` and the agent's send tests)

**Why:** TD-806: a late answer clears what the person typed since, and a repeated request delivers the same text twice.

**Fix:**
- **The key.**
  - `SendEntry` gains `key: str | None`, kept in `to_dict` / `from_dict` and through the merge by id.
  - `rpc_send` takes `key=None`, and the lookup is **its first step**, above `_refuse_gone`, the pending refusal, the `wrapup_at` / `wrapup_by` stamps, `_record_send` and `_refill`. It looks in `s.sends` for an entry with that key from the same caller (`from_` as `_record_send` writes it), made within `SEND_KEY_SECONDS` (600).
  - **Found and done:** it returns as that send did: `None`, or `RpcError(entry.verdict)` when the verdict is an error. A keyed repeat ignores `wait` and returns at once.
  - **Found and still typing:** the agent that runs `rpc_send` keeps an in-memory `{(sid, key): asyncio.Future}` for each keyed send under way, and the repeat awaits that send's outcome. This is needed because the verdict reads *submitted* from the gate onward.
  - The future is resolved, and removed, in a `finally`: with the verdict, or with the exception.
  - A failure the agent does not put into words (a `TmuxError` from the paste, which `except RpcError` does not catch) leaves the entry *submitted*, as a restart does.
  - **Not found:** as today, with `key` on the entry.
  - The match runs wherever `rpc_send` runs (the home, or the node that owns the pane): `_route_act` forwards the params as they are, so `key` crosses the link.
  - `rpc_keys` takes no key.
- **The UI.** `/api/sessions/{sid}/send` and `/wrapup` pass `body.get("key")` to `send`.
- **The page.**
  - The composer's Send mints `crypto.randomUUID()` and holds `{key, text}`. While it waits, Send is disabled and reads *Sending…*, and the box stays editable.
  - `wireComposerBar`'s `redraw` reads the composer button's `disabled` and label as well as `compose.disabled`, so the bar's Send mirrors it.
  - **On success:** it removes `text` from the start of `compose.value` only when the box still begins with it (trimming one following newline), rewrites the draft key from what is left (removing it when nothing is), and folds the bar only when the box is empty.
  - **On failure:** the box is left untouched and the banner shows as today.
  - **A verdict ends the hold**: success, or an agent refusal (`act` throwing with the agent's words). The next press mints a new key.
  - **An unknown verdict leaves the hold standing**, as the 30 s path does: a 503 (any `AgentUnavailable`, a stuck agent or a dropped connection alike), or a 400 whose words carry `_route_act`'s *its verdict is unknown* (`agent_remote.py`: the link dropped while the send was out, or the node did not answer within `ACT_TIMEOUT`). `act` puts `r.status` on the error it throws (`e.status`), so the composer can tell these from a refusal.
  - **The hold is keyed** `{key, text}`. An answer is applied only while its key is the one held; any other answer is dropped.
  - `render(v)` leaves Send's label as the hold set it while it stands. Today it rewrites the label on every view event and never sets `disabled`, and the bar's `redraw` reads `compose.disabled`, so it must read the button too (above). The hold's start and end call `cbar.redraw()`.
  - **No answer after `AO.SEND_PAGE_SECONDS`:** Send is re-enabled with the hint *not confirmed — Send repeats it safely*. A press while the box still begins with the held text sends that text with the same key; any other text gets a new key.
  - A prompt chip mints its own key and is disabled until its send answers, never touching the box. The card's Wrap up mints one per press.
- **No help paragraph:** Send has none in `help.py` or §4.5a's help list, and gains none. The words the person sees are the hints above. If the build gives Send a `title`, `test_help.py` then requires a paragraph, so it gives none.
- **Tests:**
  - **The agent:**
    - a keyed repeat after success types nothing and answers OK, with no stamp, refill or gate (a repeat to a session that has since exited answers OK);
    - a paste raising a non-`RpcError` still answers a waiting repeat;
    - after a resume, a repeat answers as the first at the id the conversation holds, and one to an old id (where the resume took a new one) is refused as closed;
    - after a `prompt-stuck`, the repeat raises the same verdict;
    - a repeat while the first is typing awaits it, with one paste only;
    - a repeat from another caller is typed;
    - a key older than `SEND_KEY_SECONDS`, or pruned from `sends`, is typed;
    - a send with no key behaves as today;
    - the key survives `to_dict` / `from_dict` and the node merge.
  - **The page** (a JS unit, as the composer bar's tests are):
    - text typed after the press is kept;
    - a box edited at its start is left whole;
    - the draft is rewritten;
    - the bar folds only when the box is empty;
    - after a refused send, the next press mints a new key;
    - after a 503, or either of `_route_act`'s *its verdict is unknown* messages (the link dropped, or no answer in time), the hold stands and the next press reuses the key;
    - a late answer for an earlier key changes nothing;
    - a view event during a hold keeps *Sending…* on both buttons;
    - after 30 s, Send is re-enabled and a repeat goes under the same key;
    - the bar's Send mirrors *Sending…*.

**Done when** a send repeated with its key, whatever repeats it, types once and answers as the first did; the composer clears only the text it sent and never words typed since; Send and the bar's Send say *Sending…* while it waits and *not confirmed* after thirty seconds; and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-806 (the design), TD-219 (the draft), TD-500 (the composer's bar), TD-805 (page loads: a slow page lengthens the window a second press falls in).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-1, #1999 and #2005) — slice 1 (#1999): `SendEntry.key`, `rpc_send`'s keyed repeat matched first, `SEND_KEY_SECONDS`, `tests/test_send_key.py`; slice 2 (#2005): `app.py`'s `send` and `wrapup` pass `key`; `app.js`'s `AO.wireComposerSend` (the hold, *Sending…*, *not confirmed* after `AO.SEND_PAGE_SECONDS`, the box cleared only of what it sent, an unknown verdict keeping the key), `AO.mintKey` (falls back to `getRandomValues` off a secure context), `act`'s `e.status`, the bar mirroring Send, a keyed chip and Wrap up; `tests/test_ui_send_key.py` and a keyed repeat through the route in `tests/test_ui.py`.

## TD-810: **Open shell here** is refused when the session's shell is still open: the create takes the name `<session>-shell`, which the live shell holds, so the placeholder tab opens and closes and the refusal is easy to miss

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, in an interactive session)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done
**Blocked by:** TD-817
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here* (TD-577, TD-580, TD-801); `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`, the `shell-here` branch: `create` with `name=f"{s['name']}-shell"`, ~L2805); `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`AO.shellHere` ~L412: the placeholder opened in the press, closed on a refused create; the press's error path ~L815); `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`create`'s name check)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-16, in Edge: pressed **Open shell here** on an interactive session's Focus; the screen flashed and no tab opened, and on a second press a tab appeared and vanished at once. The UI's log has `POST /api/sessions/ao-shiftlead-ao-queue-vs-inbox/shell-here` answered `400`. The session's shell from earlier that evening, `ao-ao-queue-vs-inbox-ao-queue-vs-inbox-shell`, was still live: Paul had closed its browser tab, which ends nothing (a session lives in tmux), so the create's name `<session>-shell` was taken and the create refused. The page did as §4.5a says (the placeholder closed, the refusal shown as any act's), but the refusal reads as a flash, and the person gets no shell where one is already open beside the session. The first press left no request in the log; why is not known.

**Fix:** design it first:
1. When the session already has the person's own shell in its directory (a live `shell` record of the name the press makes, or of the same `dir` with no role and no controller), the press opens **that** shell's Focus in the tab or window instead of refusing; or, if the design prefers more than one, names the next one `<session>-shell-2` and so on. Say which, and what a shell the person ran `exit` in (closed) does.
2. A refusal that does reach the page stays visible long enough to read (not a toast gone with the placeholder), saying what to do.
3. Say what the first press's silence was if it can be found (the placeholder blocked without the toast, or no request made), and test that a blocked open says so.
Then the build entry, named in `Blocked by:`.

**Done when** the design says what a press does when the session's shell is open (and when it was closed), what a refused press shows, and the build entry is filed and named in `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-577 and TD-579 (the press opens a tab), TD-580 and TD-801 (the person's own shell), TD-622 (the shell press's untested lines).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-2) — built by TD-817: #2009.

## TD-817: Build TD-810: Open shell here reopens the session's live shell, keeps a refusal in its tab, and keeps a blocked open's toast

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-810's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*; `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`, the `shell-here` branch; `/new`'s `elsewhere` for the host); `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`name_check` / `_name_verdict`, read only); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`person_shell`, the test it mirrors); `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`AO.shellHere`, `AO.toast`); `tests/` (the shell press's tests, TD-622's)

**Why:** TD-810: a press while the session's shell is still live is refused because the name is taken, and the refusal shows as a tab that flashes open and shut.

**Fix:**
- **The route.** Before `create`, the `shell-here` branch calls the existing `name_check` RPC (`_name_verdict`) with exactly what the create sends: `dir=s["dir"]`, no `repo`, `name=f"{s['name']}-shell"`, and `host` as below. It does not re-derive the scope: the shell's id comes from its directory's basename, not the session's repo.
  - On verdict `live` with a recorded holder, the route reads the holder's record with `get` on the reply's `holder`, since `name_check` returns only the id and `holder_state`; for a node session the home has readdressed it to `id@host`. It tests the fields below on that record.
  - **Verdict `live` with a record that is the person's own shell:** `adapter: shell`, not `unattended`, no `role`, no `team`, no `controllers` (as `mail.person_shell` reads them), with `dir == s["dir"]`. The route returns `{"ok": True, "id": <its id>, "reused": True}` and creates nothing. It still marks the session seen.
  - **Verdict `live` otherwise:** a 409 naming why, e.g. *`<name>` is a shell with controllers `<ids>` — not your own; close it, or open a shell from its Focus*, *… is held by a shell in `<dir>`*, or *… is not a shell*. A live holder with no record (`holder_state: unrecorded`) gets the 409 in `name_check`'s own message.
  - **Otherwise** it creates as today, and `create`'s own supersede handles an exited or closed holder. A `suspended` holder falls here too: a person's create supersedes it.
  - **Two presses:** when `create` is refused for any reason (`agent_call` passes only the message, so the route cannot tell why), the route runs the lookup once more. A holder that qualifies is returned as `reused`, so both tabs land on one shell; otherwise the create's own refusal is re-raised unchanged.
  - **A node session** (`s["host"]` is not this host): `host` is passed to both `name_check` and `create`, as `/new` passes `elsewhere`, so the shell is made on the session's node in its directory.
- **The page.**
  - `AO.shellHere` sends the placeholder to the returned id either way. On `reused` the pressing page toasts *your shell here was already open — opened it*.
  - A refused create no longer closes the placeholder: it writes the refusal's words and *close this tab* into it, and rethrows, so the pressing page's toast says it too.
  - A blocked open's toast (*the browser blocked the tab — allow pop-ups for this page*) stays until it is pressed. This is a fifth parameter, `sticky`, on `AO.toast(text, ok, href, wait, sticky)`: it skips the timer and sets `el.onclick = () => el.remove()` with a pointer cursor. **Pop out**'s blocked toast uses it too.
- **Tests:**
  - a press with a live shell of that name opens it and creates nothing;
  - a press with an exited one creates a fresh shell that supersedes it;
  - a live holder that is not the person's own shell (another adapter, a shell with a controller, another directory) is refused with its reason;
  - the lookup finds a shell whose id comes from its directory, not the session's repo (TD-810's own case);
  - two presses yield one shell, both answered with its id;
  - a node session's press creates on the node;
  - a refused create leaves the placeholder open with the words (a JS unit with a stubbed `window.open`);
  - a blocked open makes no request and leaves a sticky toast, removed by a click (the stub in `tests/test_ui_popout.py` records `(t, ok, href, wait, sticky)`).

**Done when** a press with the session's shell still open opens that shell; a press after `exit` opens a fresh one; a refusal stays readable in the tab; a blocked open's words stay until pressed; and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-810 (the design), TD-577 (the press opens a tab), TD-580 and TD-801 (the person's own shell), TD-622 (the shell press's tests).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-2, #2009) — the `shell-here` route checks the name with `name_check` (on the session's host) and answers the person's own live shell as `reused`, refuses a live holder that is not one with its reason (`not_own_shell`), lets `create` supersede an exited one, and on a refused create looks once more so two presses land on one shell; `AO.shellHere` sends the placeholder to a reused shell with a toast, leaves it open reading a refusal and *close this tab*, and a blocked open's toast (and **Pop out**'s) is `sticky` until pressed. Tests: `tests/test_ui_shell_here.py`, `tests/test_ui_popout.py`; checked on a scratch home (the PR's UI check). The lasting content: design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*.

## TD-824: `tests/test_send_key.py` would not catch the keyed send's `asyncio.shield` going

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (test-audit-ao-1, the tests of #1999)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #2010
**Location:** `tests/test_send_key.py`; `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_send`, `_keyed_send`)

**Why:** #1999's `_keyed_send` answers a repeat with `await asyncio.shield(typing)` so that a repeat that is itself cancelled (the page's request dropped) leaves the first send's future alone. Probe: in an `origin/main` worktree, change that line to `await typing` and run `pdm run pytest -q tests/test_send_key.py`: **8 passed**. Without the shield, cancelling the waiting repeat cancels `typing`; the first send's `finally` then reaches `typing.exception()` on a cancelled future and raises `CancelledError` out of a send that was delivered. No test cancels a waiting repeat.

**Fix:** In `tests/test_send_key.py`, a test beside `test_a_repeat_while_the_first_is_typing_awaits_it_with_one_paste`: start the first send gated, start a repeat, `cancel()` the repeat, release the gate, and assert the first returns `None`, `t.typed == ["go"]` and `agent._keyed_sends` is empty. Revert the shield in the worktree and see it fail.

**Done when** that test exists and fails with the shield removed.

**Related:** TD-813, TD-806.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-1, #2010) — `test_a_waiting_repeat_cancelled_leaves_the_first_send_alone` in `tests/test_send_key.py`: a repeat cancelled while the first types leaves the first's answer and `_keyed_sends` as they were; with the shield removed it fails.

## TD-822: A killed session resumed at once reads `exited`: the killed process's own `SessionEnd` lands after the kill, on the resumed record of the same id

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (grinder-ao-2, TD-784's live walk)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #2012
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/agent_hook.py` (`rpc_hook` → `_apply_event`, the `exited` of a `SessionEnd`); `src/sessionorc/agent.py` (`rpc_kill`, `rpc_create` with `resume`); the identity check (design §4.8a) that already flagged it in observe mode

**Why:** TD-784's live walk killed its session (`rpc_kill`: `exited`, confidence `tick`) and at once created it again with `resume` under the same id. Claude Code ran its `SessionEnd` hook on the kill's hangup (`reason: other`), and that hook landed after the create: the resumed record read `exited (hook)` while the new process started, and the walk failed its resume step (2026-10-16, the second run). The host agent printed `identity alarm (observe): outside claimed 'ao-walk-conformance-walk' on hook` — the event came from a process no longer in the record's pane. A person pressing Kill then Resume within a second or so meets the same. The walk now waits for the late hook (`SESSION_END_WAIT` in `scripts/conformance.py`).

**Fix:** drop a `SessionEnd` (any `exited` by hook) that comes from a process other than the record's current one — the identity check's *outside claimed* verdict, or the event's `adapter_id`/launch older than the record's launch — rather than applying it; a test that a kill, a resume and then the old process's `SessionEnd` leaves the resumed record as it was.

**Done when** a test holds it, and the walk's `SESSION_END_WAIT` can go (or stays as belt and braces, said so).

**Related:** TD-784 (the walk), TD-490 (`ended`), TD-063 (a killed pane revived by an older tick).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-1, #2012) — `_apply_event` drops an `exited` hook landing within `KILLED_END_GRACE` (15 s) of a `kill`, once, on a record a new run has taken under the same id (`_killed_run_at`, kept past `_scrub`, dropped by a forget); design §4.2's `SessionEnd` row says so; `test_a_killed_runs_late_end_leaves_the_resumed_record_as_it_was`. The walk's `SESSION_END_WAIT` stays as belt and braces, said so in `scripts/conformance.py`.

## TD-814: A team's TDs in motion reads a design whose PR waits on its round as *design*, the same as the one the designer is writing, so one designer reads as two designs in progress

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-16 (design §4.5 screen 1's phase sentence, §4.4 *Repo facts* **Phases**, §4.5a *team card: TDs in motion*). A claim with a PR reads *review* whatever the entry's kind; *design* is a design-first claim with no PR yet. Built by TD-815.
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 1 (the phase sentence: *design* — a designer holds a design-first entry), §4.4 *Repo facts* (**Phases**), §4.5a *team card: TDs in motion*; `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (the phase line, `row["phase"] = "design" if e.get("kind") == "design-first" else …`, ~L354)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-16, on ao-grind's card: one designer working, and TDs in motion read *2 design · 1 review* — TD-806 (designer-ao-1, #1995) and TD-804 (designer-ao-1, #1993) — and he asked whether that is a bug. It is as designed: designer-ao-1 held both claims, each design written and its PR open — TD-804's #1993 waiting on Paul's steer, TD-806's #1995 in its round (a design is held until its round ends); the phase rule reads any claim on a design-first entry as *design*, whatever its PR, where a build's claim with an open PR reads *review*. Say it in §4.5 screen 1's phase sentence, §4.4 *Phases* and the §4.5a row, then the build entry: the phase line in `org.py` and a test of a designer holding one claim with an open PR and one without.

**Done when** the design says what phase a design-first claim with an open PR reads, and the build entry is filed and named in `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-197 (the phases: design-first reads *design*), TD-722 (the Org's team cards).
