## TD-815: Build TD-814: a design-first claim with a PR reads *review* in TDs in motion

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-814's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done
**Location:** design §4.5 screen 1 (the phase sentence), §4.4 *Repo facts* **Phases**, §4.5a *team card: TDs in motion*; `src/shiftlead/ui/org.py` (`motion_rows`: the phase line and its docstring); `tests/test_ui_team_summary.py` (`test_tds_in_motion_read_the_entrys_kind_and_find_a_claims_pr_by_its_branch`, whose comment states the TD-197 reading and gains the TD-814 clause); `docs/glossary.md` already states the rule

**Why:** TD-814: one designer with two design PRs open read as *2 design*, as if two designs were being written.

**Fix:**
- In `motion_rows`, the phase is `"review" if pr else "design" if e.get("kind") == "design-first" else "grind"`. `pr` stays what it is today: the claim's own `pr`, the tick's `review_pr`, or an open PR whose head branch names the reference. The PR check comes first.
- The docstring says the same.
- A merged or closed design PR keeps *review*, marked, until the claim is marked done or dropped, as a build's does.
- **Tests:**
  - extending the test above: a designer holding one design-first claim with a PR and one without reads *1 design · 1 review*, in the rows and in the summary's `phases`;
  - a design-first claim found by its branch's open PR alone reads *review*;
  - a build's claim reads as before.

**Done when** a design-first claim with a PR reads *review* on the team card and in the rollup's bar (whose segment links are unchanged), one without reads *design*, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-814 (the design), TD-197 (the phases).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-2, #2017) — `motion_rows` checks the PR first; `test_tds_in_motion_read_the_entrys_kind_and_find_a_claims_pr_by_its_branch` holds a design-first claim with its own PR and one found by its branch reading *review*, and a designer with one of each reading *1 design · 1 review* in `phases`.

## TD-827: Build TD-821: Open shell here on a team member gives the shell the member's `team` and `project`, and the person's own shell no longer requires *no team*

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-17 (TD-821's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #2023
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here*, §4.8 *The person's own shell is the person*, §4.9 *A person in the team*; `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`, the `shell-here` branch, and TD-817's `not_own_shell` beside it; RPC-side only, no change to `app.js`); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`person_shell`); `src/sessionorc/settle.py` (`team_refusal`, read only); `src/shiftlead/ui/repo.py` (`team_groups`, read only: a card's group is its record's `team`); `tests/test_person_only.py` (the *a team's shell* case and `test_person_shell_is_a_shell_interactive_with_no_role_team_or_controller`), `tests/test_person_shell_acts.py` (`_rec("ao-t", team="t")` read as a session) and `tests/test_person_shell_link.py` (a teamed shell at a link): each asserts *no team* today and is flipped, not only added to

**Why:** TD-821: **Open shell here** on a team member makes a shell with no `team`, so its card lands in the repo's *no team* strip, away from the team the person pressed it on.

**Fix:**
- **The press.** The `shell-here` branch's `create` passes the session's `team` and `project` where the record has them, and nothing else of the team's: no `controllers`, no `review`, no `role`, no `prompt_from`, and `unattended` stays false. The create is the person's (§4.8 *A create from it is the person's create*), so the host agent adds no creator, and the client fills no manager, as `ao new --team --adapter shell` already fills none (`_team_defaults`: a shell asks for nothing). That form, and the New session form with Shell and a Team pick, already make a teamed shell with no controllers; this change makes those the person's own shell too.
- **The definition.** `mail.person_shell` drops `not record.team`. It reads `adapter == "shell"`, not `unattended`, no `role`, no `controllers`. Its docstring says why, as §4.8 does. TD-817's reuse test, `ui/app.py` `not_own_shell`, is its own copy of `person_shell` on the record's view: it drops `rec.get("team")` from its *run by a team or a role* refusal, which then reads *a shell with a role*, so a teamed shell left open is reopened.
- **One other reading follows the badge, as designed.** A declared claim from the shell's prompt reads its badge as any badged record's does (`settle.team_refusal`, §4.4 *An entry names its team*): another team's entry is refused unless `--force`. No change; a test pins it.
- **Nothing else keys on it.** `team_groups` already groups by the record's `team`. `teamrun.persons` keeps it out of live, concluded, wound down and Forget all. `_team_stamp` stamps no stop time on an interactive record. The Wind down and Stop now confirms already name a person's session apart. A change is needed only where a test shows otherwise.
- **Tests:**
  - a press on a team member creates a shell carrying its `team` and `project`, with no controllers and no review, and the Org's team group draws it, not the no-team strip;
  - a press on a session with no badge creates a shell with none, and `/shell` (**+ New ▾ Shell**) makes one with none;
  - a claim from a teamed shell's prompt on another team's entry is refused without `--force`, as any badged record's is;
  - `person_shell` is true for a teamed shell with no role and no controllers, and false for one with a role or a controller;
  - a request from a teamed shell passes `ao promote` and the acting gate as the person's own shell does (TD-580, TD-801);
  - the team with only that shell live reads *stopped*, and `ao team stop` leaves the shell alone;
  - a second press with the teamed shell still live reopens it (TD-817's reuse).

**Done when** **Open shell here** on a team member opens a shell drawn in that team's group, which still passes every person-only act and is left alone by every team act, and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-821 (the design), TD-817 (the reuse, built in #2009: the same route), TD-580 and TD-801 (the person's own shell), TD-160 (a person in the team), TD-725 (the no-team strip).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-1, #2023) — `ui/app.py`'s `shell-here` create passes the session's `team` and `project` and nothing else of its team's; `mail.person_shell` drops *no team* (its docstring says why); `not_own_shell` refuses an unattended or a role's shell in its own words, so a teamed shell left open is reopened. Tests flipped from *no team* in `test_person_only.py`, `test_person_shell_acts.py`, `test_person_shell_link.py`; the claim refusal from a teamed person's shell pinned in `test_entry_team.py`; the press, the reuse and the team group in `test_ui_shell_here.py`. UI check on a scratch home: `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-17-td827-teamed-shell.png`.

## TD-821: A shell opened from a team member's **Open shell here** draws in the repo's *no team* strip, not on the team the person was looking at

**Priority:** Low
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Done — built by TD-827 (#2023)
**Blocked by:** TD-827
**Location:** design §4.5a *Focus: Open shell here* (the record it creates) and *card: compact* (*the full card stays on a repo's no-team strip*), §4.9 *A person in the team* (TD-160) and *The Org page* (the no-team strip); `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (`/api/sessions/{sid}/{action}`, the `shell-here` branch: `create(name=…-shell, dir=…, adapter="shell")`, no `team`, ~L2805); `src/shiftlead/ui/repo.py` (`team_groups`: a card's group is its record's `team`, else `NO_TEAM`, ~L655); `src/sessionorc/mail.py` (`person_shell`: *no team* is among its conditions today; TD-827 drops it)

**Why:** Paul, 2026-10-16, through Add entry: *When a shell is opened from a team, its card should show on that team (instead of "no team") - that way its more easily seen as a user is focused on a particular team.* Today **Open shell here** on a team member creates the person's own shell with no `team`, so its card lands in the repo's *n sessions, no team* strip, away from the team the person pressed it on, and a person working one team has to look for it elsewhere on the page.

**Fix:** design it first: the shell **Open shell here** creates from a session with a `team` carries that `team`, so it draws with the team's cards. Say:
1. Which presses carry it: Focus's and the card's **more ▾** on a team member, and whether **+ New ▾ → Shell** pressed while a team is in view does.
2. What the badge does not make it, and the tension it meets: the person's own shell is today a `shell` record that is interactive with **no role, no team** and no controller (§4.8 *The person's own shell is the person*; `mail.person_shell` checks `not record.team`), so a shell that simply carried `team` would lose the person-only acts **Open shell here** exists to give (TD-580, TD-801). Say whether §4.8's definition drops *no team* for a shell, or the team is shown some other way (the card drawn with the team it was opened from, kept apart from the record's `team`). Either way the shell is not a member any team act reaches (TD-160's *left alone by every team act*: Stop, wind down, rule 8, lane counts, TDs in motion), and keeps the full card or takes the compact one — say which, since §4.5a gives the full card to *a repo's no-team strip* and the compact one to *a team member*.
3. What carries on **Resume** (`team` is in `RESUME_CARRIES`) and what a shell on a concluded or stopped team shows.
Then the build entry, named in `Blocked by:`.

**Done when** the design says which shells carry the team, what the badge leaves unchanged, and which card they draw, and the build entry is filed and named in `Blocked by:`.

**Related:** TD-577 and TD-580 (Open shell here, the person's own shell), TD-810 (Open shell here refused while the shell is open), TD-160 (a person's session in a team), TD-725 (the no-team strip).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-1) — built by TD-827: #2023.

The guard does something only for a title adapter whose `explain` answers a bare tail, which no test builds. The other `#2024` lines tried (`_hook_state.pop`, the exited/closed bar, `TITLE_SHELL_WAITS` by state, `not s.told`, `ao explain`'s reason and `--file --title`) each fail a test.

**Fix:** one test with a title adapter whose `explain(tail, title="")` returns a verdict for the tail alone (a `hookstub` variant), a title that says nothing, and a record the screen rule would change: the record stands.

**Done when** removing the guard fails `tests/test_gemini_title.py`.

**Related:** TD-785 (slice 3, #2024), TD-112.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-1, #2031) — `test_a_title_adapters_screen_rule_is_never_read` gives the Gemini adapter an `explain` that also answers a bare tail, with a title that says nothing and no hook: `_screen_verdict` reads None and the record stands. With the guard removed it fails (1 failed, 8 passed); with it, 9 passed.

## TD-811: Build TD-804 (1): a promote's smoke at the home — `smoke:` run once `check` reads the commit, the promote in flight until it ends, a failed smoke rolling back to `from` with the hold, and the row's and `ao promote status`'s words

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** feature
**Added:** 2026-10-16 (TD-804's design, the designer)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Done — #2033, #2037
**Location:** design §6 *Promote* *The smoke*, §5 `promote:`, §4.5a *Inbox row: promote*, §4.7 `ao promote status`; `src/sessionorc/promote.py` (`KEYS`, `block` read on the tree, `_conclude`, `_concluded`, `survey`, `start`, `note_text`), the home's `PromoteMixin`; `src/shiftlead/repoconfig.py` (`PROMOTE_KEYS`, `_promote`); the promote row in `src/shiftlead/ui/` and `ao promote status` in `src/shiftlead/cli.py`

**Why:** TD-804, slice 1: today a promote is done when `check` reads the commit, and a build that breaks on the person's real state stays live until the person finds it.

**Fix:**
- **The key.** `promote:` takes an optional `smoke`, a non-empty string. `promote.block` returns it when present: today its `KEYS` reads past it silently. `repoconfig._promote` accepts it: today it refuses any key but `run` and `check`, so `ao new` in a repo whose block names `smoke` fails until this lands.
- **The start.** On the pass whose `check` reads the intent's commit (not `live_why`), with a `smoke` in the block and no `phase: smoke` yet:
  - split `_concluded` into the write at the `check` reading (`last.json`, and for a rollback `held.json`, so a rollback's failed smoke stands as a failure beside its hold) and the clear at the smoke's pass. A plain promote's `held.json` is cleared only when its smoke passes, or at the `check` reading for a block with no `smoke`.
  - in `start`, read `smoke` from the run's tree (`block(tree)`: the checkout for a promote, `promotes/<repo>/tree` for a rollback) and keep it on the intent, so a pull of the checkout mid-run changes nothing and a restart needs no second read. A repo whose checkout's block has no `smoke` concludes on `check` with its note unchanged. Where the checkout's block has one and the tree's has none (a missing file reads as no block), no smoke runs and the note says *no smoke in `<sha7>`*. A tree whose file or block cannot be read (`block` raises `ValueError`) runs none either, and its note says *no smoke read in `<sha7>`: <why>*. The raise is caught there and never escapes into `survey`.
  - start the smoke detached in the intent's tree (the checkout for a promote, `promotes/<repo>/tree` for a rollback);
  - pass `SHIFTLEAD_PROMOTE_SHA` (now live), `_FROM`, `_ROOT` and `SHIFTLEAD_PROMOTE_KIND`, with output appended to the run's log after `── smoke ──`;
  - run it through a wrapper (`sh -c '<smoke>; …'`, or a Python one) that writes `{sha, exit, at}` to `promotes/<repo>/smoke.json` when the smoke ends;
  - record `phase: smoke`, `smoke_pid`, `smoke_started` (the process's start time, as the run's is kept) and `smoke_at` in `inflight.json`.
  - A repo with no `smoke` concludes as today.
- **The judgement.** On later passes (at `PROMOTE_WATCH` while in flight):
  - **The run's bound stops at the smoke's start.** `_conclude`'s `PROMOTE_BOUND` check reads the run's `at` only while there is no `phase: smoke`. From then on, `SMOKE_BOUND` from `smoke_at` is the only clock.
  - **Pass:** `smoke.json` for the intent's sha reads exit 0 → the intent cleared, a plain promote's hold cleared, a failure standing cleared as today, `smoke.json` removed, and the note *promoted `<repo>` `<sha7>` — n commits · smoke passed in <s> s* (a rollback's note gains the same tail).
  - **Fail:** a non-zero exit, a smoke gone with no `smoke.json` (`alive` with its start time), or past `SMOKE_BOUND` (600 s; killed only while the pid is still the smoke) → a failed smoke, its why *smoke failed on `<sha7>`: <the log's last non-empty line>*.
- **A failed smoke.**
  - **Rolls back** when the intent's `kind` is not `rollback`, its `from` was read, and `from` ≠ the sha. It starts `start(..., kind="rollback", by="smoke", sha=from, frm=sha)` at once, keeping `why` on the new intent. It goes even under a standing hold.
  - A rollback that cannot start (`start` raises: the tree cannot be made) → `fail(repo, intent, "smoke failed on <sha7>: <why>; its rollback could not start: <why>")`, live left where it is.
  - When `check` reads that rollback's commit, `held.json` gains `by: smoke` and `why`, rewriting a standing hold as a second rollback does (its `from` kept).
  - The note: *rolled back `<repo>` to `<sha7>`: the smoke failed on `<sha7>` — <why>*.
  - **Otherwise** `fail(repo, intent, why)`: a failure standing, live left where it is.
- **The row.** `promote_rows` reads *checking `<sha7>` live · started <t>* under FYI, with Promote disabled, while `phase: smoke`. A hold with `by: smoke` reads *rolled back by the smoke from `<sha7>` <t> ago — <why>* in place of *rolled back from …*. The build chip's *· promoting…* covers the smoke too.
- **`ao promote status`** prints the same words, and `--json` carries `phase`, and `held.by` / `held.why`.
- **Tests:**
  - a block with `smoke` accepted by both readers;
  - the smoke started on the reading pass in the right tree with the four variables;
  - a pass, a non-zero exit, a smoke gone with no result, and the bound;
  - the rollback started with `by: smoke` and the hold written with `by` and `why` when `check` reads it;
  - a rollback that cannot start (both reasons on the failure);
  - a run plus smoke past `PROMOTE_BOUND` passing;
  - a rollback to a tree whose block has no `smoke` concluding on `check`, with *no smoke in `<sha7>`*, and one whose block cannot be read concluding with *no smoke read*;
  - the smoke kept on the intent at start, unchanged when the checkout moves before the `check` reading;
  - a press under a hold whose smoke fails: the hold rewritten, not cleared, and still standing when the smoke's rollback cannot start;
  - a rollback's failed smoke leaving the hold beside the failure;
  - no rollback for a rollback's failed smoke, an unread `from`, or `from` equal to the sha (a failure instead);
  - an agent restarted mid-smoke reading `smoke.json`;
  - precondition (3) refusing a press while `phase: smoke`;
  - the row's and status's words.

**Done when** a promote in a repo whose block has `smoke:` is concluded only when its smoke passes; a failed smoke puts `from` back with the hold and says why on the row, the note and `ao promote status`; a rollback's failed smoke stands as a failure; and the tests above pass.

**Related:** TD-804 (the design), TD-812 (this repo's smoke), TD-132 and TD-226 (the promote and the rollback).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-1, #2033, #2037) — slice 1 (#2033): the home. `smoke` is read by both readers and kept on the intent from the run's tree. It starts once `check` reads the commit, is judged from `smoke.json` under `SMOKE_BOUND`, and a failed one starts a rollback to `from` (`by: smoke`, the hold's `by` and `why`). Slice 2 (#2037): the row reads *checking `<sha7>` live · started <t>* (FYI, Promote disabled) and *rolled back by the smoke from `<sha7>` <t> ago — <why>*, and `ao promote status` uses the same words. Both were checked on a scratch home, with screenshots under `docs/mockups/reviews/2026-10-17-td811-*`. A smoke's rollback whose run cannot be spawned (an `OSError`) now fails with both reasons, as a tree that cannot be made does. Its live reading is TD-812's, when this repo's smoke lands.

## TD-847: Build TD-845: the bridge's attach asks tmux for `hyperlinks`, and the Focus terminal's `linkHandler` opens an OSC 8 target under the URL rule, its target shown on hover

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-17 (the designer, from TD-845)
**Owner:** grinder
**Kind:** build
**Status:** Built (2026-10-17, #2036).
**Location:** `src/sessionorc/tmux.py` (`attach_argv`), `src/sessionorc/containers.py` (`attach_argv_in`), `src/shiftlead/ui/pty_bridge.py` (`attach_argv`) and `src/shiftlead/ui/app.py` (the terminal websocket), `src/shiftlead/cli.py` (`ao focus`, unchanged), `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`AO.focus`, `AO.paneLink`), `src/shiftlead/ui/help.py`

**Why:** design §4.6 *A hyperlink in the pane is a link* and §4.5a's **a hyperlink is a link** row (TD-845). Claude Code prints Artifacts, PRs and docs as OSC 8 labels inside tmux; the pty bridge's plain `tmux attach` gets the label without its target, so the Focus pane shows dead text.

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (grinder-ao-2, #2036) — `sessionorc.tmux.attach_argv`, `containers.attach_argv_in` and `pty_bridge.attach_argv` take `features`; the terminal websocket's two attaches pass `("hyperlinks",)`, `ao focus` nothing. `AO.paneLinkHandler` is the Focus terminal's `linkHandler`. §4.5a's help list and `help.py` carry **a hyperlink is a link** (`pane-hyperlink`). Tests: `tests/test_ui_focus_hyperlinks.py`.

**Done when:**
- A test drives `tmux -L <private> -T hyperlinks attach`, as the bridge builds it, on a pane that printed an OSC 8 run, and reads the `ESC ] 8 ;` sequence and its target in the attach's bytes. It skips when `tmux -V` is below 3.4. `attach_argv` and `pty_bridge.attach_argv` without `features` have no `-T`, and `ao focus`'s argv has none. `tests/test_ui_teams.py`'s websocket attach for a container node now reads `["tmux", "-T", "hyperlinks", "attach", "-t", "=ao-repo-w:"]`; `tests/test_ui.py`'s `pty_bridge.attach_argv`, `tests/test_containers.py`'s and `tests/test_cli.py`'s `ao focus` assertions stay as they are.
- A node probe, as `tests/test_ui_focus_links.py`'s, builds `AO.paneLinkHandler(el)` on a stub element, with `window.open` stubbed to record its arguments (the wrapper passes no `open`). `activate({ctrlKey: true}, url, range)` opens `[url, "_blank", "noopener"]`, and `activate({}, url, range)` opens nothing. `hover(e, url, range)` leaves `el.title === url`, and `leave()` clears it. A `javascript:` target opens nothing on Ctrl+click.
- A text check holds that `new Terminal(` in `AO.focus` carries `linkHandler:` and no `allowNonHttpProtocols`, and that the vendored `xterm.js`'s `OscLinkProvider` keeps its `["http:","https:"]` check. The drop of any other target is xterm's, so the test pins the vendored copy rather than driving it.
- §4.5a's row is listed in `help.py`, or the URL row's help names it, and `tests/test_help.py` passes.

**Related:** TD-845 (the design), TD-421/TD-422 (the URL rule), TD-071 (no control from the text).

## TD-845: A link a program prints with OSC 8 (Claude Code's *Report: Team Spend by Seat*) is plain text in the Focus pane: tmux drops it before the browser, and xterm.js has no handler for it

**Priority:** Medium
**Type:** debt
**Added:** 2026-10-17 (Paul, through Add entry; drafted by ao-shiftlead-techlead-ao-1)
**Owner:** designer
**Kind:** design-first
**Status:** Designed 2026-10-17 (design §4.6 *A hyperlink in the pane is a link*; §4.5a *Focus pane: a hyperlink is a link*). Step 1's read: Claude Code emits OSC 8 under tmux 3.4 or later, and tmux 3.5a sends it only to a client attached with `-T hyperlinks`, in copy mode too. The bridge's attach asks for it and `ao focus` does not. The Focus terminal's `linkHandler` opens the target under the URL rule and shows it as the pane's tooltip on hover. With a target that is not `http(s)`, the label is text, read by the URL and path rules. Built by TD-847.
**Blocked by:** TD-847
**Location:** design §4.6 *A URL in the pane is a link* (TD-421) and *A path in the pane is a link* (TD-493), §4.5a's Focus link rows; `src/sessionorc/tmux.py` (`attach_argv`); `src/shiftlead/ui/static/app.js` (`AO.focus`: the `Terminal` options, the web-links addon, `AO.paneLink`)

**Why:**
- Paul's words: *there is a "Team Spend by Seat" that looks like it should be a link … we just check for files that exist. Is there a way we can make it a link?* The screenshot (ao-paul's Focus, 2026-10-17) shows Claude Code's line *Report: ⧉ Team Spend by Seat*. The text is a link label with no URL printed beside it (an Artifact's claude.ai page), so neither of the pane's two readers can take it: the web-links addon underlines only an `http(s)://` run it sees in the text, and the path provider only a run the host says is a file.
- A label with its target hidden is what an OSC 8 hyperlink is (`ESC ] 8 ; ; <url> ST <text> ESC ] 8 ; ; ST`). Two things stand between one and the person:
  - **tmux drops it.** tmux 3.4+ keeps a pane's hyperlinks but sends them only to a client whose terminal has the `hyperlinks` feature. kmaster runs tmux 3.5a, and its `terminal-features` default (`xterm*:clipboard:ccolour:cstyle:focus:title`) lacks it, so the pty bridge's `tmux attach` receives the label alone. `tmux -T hyperlinks attach …` asks for it for that one client, and sets no server or session option (`attach_argv`'s rule: attaching sets nothing).
  - **The page has no handler.** The vendored `@xterm/xterm` 5.5.0 parses OSC 8 and draws a link from its `linkHandler` option. `AO.focus` sets none, so xterm's own fallback would apply (a `confirm()` box on a plain click), and that is not §4.6's rule: underline on hover, Ctrl/Cmd+click, `http`/`https` only, a new tab `noopener`.
- Not yet checked: that Claude Code emits OSC 8 at all inside tmux (it decides from the environment whether the terminal supports hyperlinks), and what the ⧉ mark is. The first step of the fix reads this on a scratch pane before anything is designed.
- The value: Claude Code prints Artifacts, PRs and docs as labels more and more. In the pane they are dead text the person has to find again elsewhere, which is the friction §4.6's two link rules exist to remove.
- TD-071's rule (*nothing on a page is a control that parses what an agent printed*) is met in the same way as the URL rule: the press opens only the target the program attached, behind a modifier. But the label and the target can differ, and that is new: the person sees text, not the URL. The design has to say how the target is shown before the press (a hover title with the URL, as VS Code's terminal does).

**Resolved:** 2026-10-17 (built by TD-847, #2036) — design §4.6 *A hyperlink in the pane is a link* and §4.5a's row carry the rule; checked on a scratch home: an OSC 8 label underlines on hover, its target is the pane's tooltip, and Ctrl+click opens it (`noopener`).

**Done when** the pane underlines an OSC 8 label, shows its target on hover and opens it on Ctrl/Cmd+click under §4.6's rules, or the read says Claude Code prints no target and the entry archives with that reason.

**Related:** TD-421 and TD-494 (the URL rule and cut rows), TD-493 and TD-501 (the path rule), TD-071 (no control from the text), TD-818 (the report in the screenshot).
